articleTitle: Design of a Second Harmonic MW-Level Coaxial Gyrotron Cavity
abstract: An optimized second harmonic cavity for a 170 GHz 1.3MW fusion gyrotron is presented. The suppression of the competing modes at fundamental frequency is achieved solely due to a specific design of the coaxial cavity with corrugated inner conductor and does not require e.g. the injection of an external signal. The design is verified by self-consistent multimode simulations. The results show an excellent suppression of the competing fundamental modes.

articleTitle: Modeling of Serpentine Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube to Calculate Gain Diagram
abstract: We develop an analytical model for traveling wave tubes (TWTs) amplifiers based on the serpentine waveguide (SW). This analytical model is a generalization of the Pierce model, assuming one-dimensional electron flow along a dispersive slow-wave structure (SWS), with space-charge effects accounted for. The cold structure parameters, i.e., phase velocity and characteristic impedance, are accounted for in the equivalent circuit model. We use the relation between characteristic and interaction impedance with an extra correction factor that accounts for the non-uniform beam-wave interaction over the interaction area. Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results are compared to the calculated gain versus frequency using the proposed model, revealing excellent agreement over a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Electron Optics System for 0.67 THz Staggered Grating Backward Wave Oscillators
abstract: The electron optics system (EOS), which includes the electron gun and focusing system, is the core of backward wave oscillators (BWO). This paper presents a simulation and analysis of the EOS of a 0.67 THz BWO. The design process for the electron gun and Periodic closed magnetic focusing system is described. First, the initial parameters of the electron gun were obtained using the Tiwary method and MATLAB. After further simulation and debugging, the circular electron beam electron gun with operating voltage of 23.8kV and current emitted of 18.2mA was designed. Second, to reduce the device's size and weight, the Periodic closed magnetic focusing magnetic field structure matching the electron gun was adopted, making the stable transmission distance of the electron beam greater than 30mm, and the channel radius is 0.07mm.

articleTitle: THz Cherenkov Oscillator Efficiency Increase by Use of Long Structures
abstract: Peculiarities of self-fields excited on a slow wave circuit when electron beam is moving along either uniform grating (Smith-Purcell radiation) or bi-periodic/nonuniform grating (leaky radiation of spoof surface plasmon polariton) have been considered. It is shown that deceleration of electrons (energy transfer from electrons to EM wave) may occur for relatively long distances (grating lengths) without overbunching that may result in both low starting current and relatively high efficiency in the THz devices based on the SPR (orotron/DRO) and based on the hybrid bulk-surface modes.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication Aspects of an E-band Double Corrugated Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: E-band (71 - 76 GHz, 81 - 86 GHz) is commercially used for point to point links. The transmission power of E-band front ends is not higher than a few Watts, produced by solid state amplifiers. Front ends typically use large diameter antennas to ensure the required EIRP. The availability of power in the range of tens of Watts would enable long links and high signal to noise ratio for high modulation scheme. An E-band (71 - 76 GHz) Traveling Wave Amplifiers has been designed to enhance the capacity of future E-band links. This paper discuss the first version of the TWT based on a single section double corrugated waveguide slow wave structure, to test design and fabrication before the fabrication of a more complex 70 W two sections E-band TWT.

articleTitle: The Study on the Uniformity of Electric Field Distribution in the Coaxial Cavity Output Circuit of the Multi-Beam Klystron
abstract: High peak power multi-beam klystrons (MBKs) often use coaxial cavity as RF interaction circuits. Due to the influence of the coupling port between the cavity and the waveguide, the electric field distribution in the electron beam channels is uneven, so that the efficiency of the MBKs cannot reach the maximum. Based on the design of X band 3MW MBK, the electric field distribution of several types of coaxial cavity output circuits is calculated by using CST microwave studio. It is found that adding a fan-shaped metal ring to the inner conductor of the coaxial cavity can make the electric field distribution distortion, thus compensating for the electric field non-uniformity caused by the coupling port. This structure combined with filter loaded circuit can further improve the electric field uniformity. Comparing with the traditional output structure, the ratio of the maximum value to the minimum value of the characteristic impedance R/Q of the electron beam channels of this structure decreases from 9.83 to 1.45, and the efficiency of the MBK increases from 43.7% to 52.15%.

articleTitle: Automatic Threat Object Detection from THz Images using Artificial Intelligence Algorithms
abstract: Terahertz (THz) waves ranging from 0.1 THz to 10 THz, have the capability to penetrate most non-metallic and non-polar materials. This particular property of THz wave has opened up several application fields, particularly in the field of non-destrutive testing and security scanning. In baggage scanning applications, the THz wave penetrates through various baggage materials and can see-through the objects concealed within them. However, due to the limited THz emission power levels and limited THz detector sensitivities available, THz images acquired are of poor quality. These images have (i) high background variations, (ii) poor contrast, (iii) blurry images, and (iv) lack proper edge continuities. Due to these reasons, advanced image processing and artificial intelligence algorithms are utilized to enable automatic threat object detection and identification from THz images. In this work, authors have employed artificial intelligence-based algorithms for object detection, namely YOLOv5, for automatic threat identification, and evaluated its performance using various metrics such as precision, recall, and mean average precision (mAP) {0.5 and 0.5:0.95}

articleTitle: Design of A 0.23THz Extended Interaction Amplifier with Trapezoidal Subwavelength Holes
abstract: In this paper, a novel extended interaction amplifier (EIA) is designed by combining the trapezoidal subwavelength hole array with the traditional ladder-shaped line resonator. Due to this new structure, the electromagnetic coupling of the cavity is effectively enhanced. After staggered tuning, the 3D Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulation predicts that the designed multi-cavity EIA produces stable 136.8 W output power from a 20 mW input driving signal, with 38.35 dB gain and more than 1.2 GHz −3dB operating bandwidth at 230.52 GHz.

articleTitle: A bilayer substrate dynode for the performance improvement of box-and-grid electron multiplier
abstract: The bilayer substrate dynode for box-and-grid electron multiplier is proposed, and its electrical properties are studied by CST simulation. The two layers of substrate are both made of stainless steel. However, the outer layer is covered on the middle of the inner layer and its area is smaller than that of the inner layer. With the adoption of the bilayer substrate for dynodes, the maximal average electron collection efficiency of dynode is increased from 96.07% to 99.54%, and the electron multiplier's gain is significantly increased correspondingly. In addition, the proposed structure is easily accessible in industry. Thus, building this bilayer substrate structure of dynodes is promising to be a popular method for the performance improvement of electron multiplier.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of a long-pulse high-power 170GHz gyrotron
abstract: The MW gyrotrons are key devices in ECRH of magnetic confinement nuclear fusion systems. In order to achieve the high-power and long-pulse of the 170GHz gyrotron, which are adopted in the CFETR, a <tex>$\mathbf{TE_{25.10}}$</tex> -mode 170GHz gyrotron research are given in this paper. A single-anode magnetron injection gun (MIG) and the cylindrical resonant cavity operating are designed and optimized by PIC. The theoretical output power of the gyrotron with operating Voltage 75 kV, electron current 45 A is about 1.1 MW, corresponding to electron efficiency of 32.6%. The prototype of the gyrotron has been fabricated and tested preliminarily. The First results of the 170 GHz gyrotron experiments are that an output power of <tex>$\boldsymbol{\sim 350}\ \mathbf{kW}$</tex> with Gaussian beam is achieved at 15-ms pulse length in operating voltage 52.2 kV, electron beam 40 A.

articleTitle: High responsivity nano-air-channel photomixer for mmWave generation
abstract: Photomixer with high-speed and large-bandwidth is a key device for photoelectric conversion in photonic millimeter wave and terahertz information system. Herein, for the first time, nano-air-channel photodiode is demonstrated as a photomixer to generate coherent mmWave signal in experiment. Based on the external photoelectric effect, photoelectrons emitted from the InGaAs photocathode can reach the metal anode by scattering-free ballistic transport in the quasi-vacuum nano-air channel, resulting in a high-speed response. The large electric field nearby the nano-air channel led to carrier multiplication inside the InGaAs, which enables a high responsivity. This work provides a new type device which has great potential to break through the limits of the traditional semiconductor photomixers in bandwidth, efficiency and output power.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Quasi-Optical 170 GHz Pulse Compressor with Laser-Driven GaAs Switch
abstract: A quasi-optical three-mirror pulse compressor with laser-driven GaAs switch was developed and experimentally tested. GaAs switch was activated by 532 nm laser with a pulse duration of about 100 ps and a pulse energy of about 50 mJ. Power gain of about 25 was obtained when compressing the output radiation of 170 GHz backward wave oscillator operating in a continuous wave mode, with an output power of about 10 mW.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Microwave Plasma Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition System Operated at 2.45 GHz Using the Multiphysics Modeling based on a Finite Element Method
abstract: Microwave plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (MPECVD) is one of the most extensively used thin film manufacturing methods for growth of diamonds than any other plasma based systems. Microwave plasmas are different from other plasmas where the microwave frequency can oscillate electrons and the collision of electrons with gaseous atoms and molecules generates a high degree of ionization. Hence in an MPECVD system, by applying microwave the plasma can be ignited and sustained, where a thin film can be deposited at lower temperatures. This paper discusses the design of a 3-D MPECVD chamber operated at a 2.45 GHz of frequency using the Multiphysics modeling based on a finite element method (FEM) that incorporates many physical interfaces including laminar flow, heat transfer in fluids, plasma, and electromagnetic waves to give more self-consistent and accurate simulation results. The plasma discharge is modeled by coupling drift-diffusion, heavy species transport, and electric fields into a single multiphysics model. The conservations of mass and momentum are modeled in simulation by solving continuity and Navier-strokes equation, respectively. The geometrical design of MPECVD consists of a coaxial waveguide connected by slots to a cylindrical plasma chamber at the center to produce T'M<inf>011</inf> mode. With an input power of 1 kW at the input port of WR340 coaxial waveguide at 2.45 GHz with the argon pressure at the chamber varied from 600 to 1000 Torr, the plasma density increases from 5.51e16 to <tex>$\mathbf{5}.\mathbf{81}\mathbf{e}\mathbf{161}/\mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> reaching steady-state at around 5 msec and a uniform argon plasma is excited by the TM<inf>011</inf> cavity resonance. Detailed analysis of the dependence of the MPECVD operation on different pressures and input powers will be presented.

articleTitle: Design and test of an E-band CW space TWT
abstract: This paper presents a design and experimental study of an E-band continuous wave (CW) space traveling wave tube (TWT) with overall efficiency of over 37% using multistage depressed collectors (MDC) at 71–76 GHz. The folded waveguide (FWG) and phase velocity tapering circuit are used to achieve the electronic efficiency of over 7.8%. A prototype tube has been fabricated and tested with beam voltage of 14.7 kV and beam current of 74 mA. The testing results show that the TWT has achieved over 85W output power and above 39.5 dB gain within a bandwidth of 5GHz, with a maximum saturated output power of 100.7W, a corresponding gain of 43 dB and overall efficiency of 46%.

articleTitle: Inter-dynode Voltage Optimization of Discrete Dynode Electron Multipliers by Numerical Simulation
abstract: In order to improve the performance of discrete dynode electron multipliers, the effect of inter-dynode voltage on device gain was investigated by numerical simulation, and the distribution of inter-dynode voltages was optimized. The investigation results reveal that for an electron multiplier with 11-stage dynodes, when the inter-dynode voltage of the first 10 dynodes is 3.1 times that of the last 1 dynode, it can obtain a higher gain due to the improvement of electric field intensity and electron collection efficiency, whose overall electron collection efficiency and device gain increase by about 63% and 95%, respectively, in comparison with the case of applying the same inter-dynode voltage for all the dynodes.

articleTitle: A New K-band 1-bit Broadband Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antenna
abstract: Metasurface antennas are considered as one of the future 6G communication technologies due to their beamforming ability. We design a K-band beam-controllable reflectarray using a wideband 1-bit reconfigurable metasurface unit. The unit cell provides phase compensation for both states by simultaneous state inversion by two PIN diodes. The 180° reflected phase difference between the two states is achieved by the parallel patch circuit current change, and the wideband comes from the similar resonance frequency. The reflection loss of the K-band component in both states is less than 0.6 dB. The reconfigurable reflectarray antenna excited by the linear polarized horn has the characteristics of low loss, with a maximum gain of approximately 22.6 dBi in the frequency band and frequency coverage of 22–26 GHz.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of a 28 GHz Third Harmonic Cyclotron Magnetron Electron Gun
abstract: According to the requirements of the 28 GHz third harmonic cyclotron, a single-anode magnetically controlled injection gun with a voltage of 30kV, a current of 1A, a guide center radius of 7mm, a speed ratio of 1.4 and a transverse velocity dispersion of 2.41% was designed. Simulations were carried out using Magic particle simulation software and the effects of voltage and current on the velocity ratio and transverse velocity dispersion were analysed. From the simulation results, it can be concluded that the velocity ratio and velocity dispersion of the single-anode electron gun designed in this paper can meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: Simulation and Cold Test of a W-band Staggered Double Vane Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: The W-band staggered double vane Slow Wave Structure (SWS)Travelling Wave Tube (TWT) adopting the negative phase-velocity tapering technique is proposed and investigated in this paper, benefiting the improvement of the output power. The input/output coupler, which uses resonators to feed electromagnetic waves into SWS, for this kind of SWS are put forward. It is not only simple to manufacture, but also greatly reduces the longitudinal size of the TWT. In this paper, the high frequency characteristics, transmission characteristics and beam-wave interaction are analyzed by simulation software. The particle-in-cell results show that its output power and gain at 91 GHz can reach 1800 W and 10.5 dB, respectively. Its 3-dB bandwidth is from 87 GHz to 96 GHz. Based on these, the experiment of the fabricated high frequency system with filleted staggered double vane slow wave structure is carried out.

articleTitle: Final version - The Low-Voltage X, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{u}}$ and W-Bands Magnetrons with Two Energy Outputs: New Possibilities
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical and experimental results of the studies of the new designs of the magnetrons known as the magnetrons with two energy outputs (or dual-output magnetrons). The prototypes of the two magnetrons for X and Ku-bands are developed. The magnetrons produce the average maximum powers of ~ 18.6 W and ~ 15.5 W, frequency tuning of ~ 220 MHz and ~ 150 MHz, and frequency stability of <tex>$(3\ldots 5)10^{-6}$</tex>, respectively. The results of computer modeling of the W-band magnetron are presented. Examples of applying the dual-output magnetrons in radar systems and communication are given.

articleTitle: A method suitable for solving the magnetic field of permanent magnet and energized coil system
abstract: This paper introduces a method based on MFS software to solve the fusion magnetic system of permanent magnet and energized coil. The basic idea of this method is to solve the magnetic field generated by the energized coil through analytical methods first, then save the result and add it as the electromagnetic base to the solution result of the coercive force of the permanent magnet material, as the influence exerted on the permanent magnet material, and then By solving the magnetic field of the permanent magnet system by the finite element method, the magnetic field of the permanent magnet and electromagnetic fusion magnetic system can be obtained.

articleTitle: The Effect of the High Order Mode of Cavity on Performances of the High Power Klystron
abstract: In addition to the working mode <tex>$TM_{010}$</tex> mode, there are also many high-order modes in the cavity of the klystron. These modes have an important influence on the stability, output spectrum and other performances of the klystrons, especially broadband klystrons. This paper introduces the problem of high second harmonic level (-10dBc) and the breakdown of RF output system at certain frequency of the low frequency end of the S-band broadband klystron. Through analysis and simulation, it is determined that the problem is caused by the <tex>$TM_{011}$</tex> mode of the front cavity of the double gap coupling cavity (DGCC) broadband output circuit. By placing a metal ring at the middle of the front cavity, the resonant frequency of the <tex>$TM_{011}$</tex> mode decreases from 4.634GHz to 4.552GHz, which is lower than 2 FL (Lowest operating frequency of the klystron). The test of this klystron shows that the second harmonic level of the operating frequency is lower than - 30dBc. At the same time, the breakdown problem of the output system is overcome. The performance of the klystron fully meets the user's requirements.

articleTitle: Effect of Cathode Surface Roughness on Quality of Electron Beam in a Gyrotron Electron Optical System
abstract: An approach to simulate electron trajectories in gyrotron electron optical systems taking into account cathode surface roughness is proposed. It is based on the use of standard parameters of the thermionic emission model, which is available in the three-dimensional simulation software, for consideration of the micron-size non-uniformities of the cathode surface. Based on this approach, the influence of cathode surface roughness on electron beam quality in the 74.2 GHz, 100 kW gyrotron is studied. A comparison between the simulated data and the data obtained earlier in the experiments on velocity spread allows to estimate an averaged size of microstructures on the surface of a lanthanum hexaboride cathode used in this gyrotron.

articleTitle: Design of S-band high-efficiency magnetrons based on cooker magnetron
abstract: In order to achieve high-efficiency output in the S-band, a 10-cavity magnetron is designed. The size of each part of the magnetron is determined according to the design requirements. We use the cross-chain structure to improve the frequency interval between the <tex>$\pi$</tex>-mode and the adjacent mode, and improve the coupling output matching structure. PIC simulation is done to calculate the performance of the magnetron. The final result of <tex>$\boldsymbol{PIC}$</tex> simulation is displayed that the magnetron in this paper was able to produce the calculated output power increased to 12.6 kW with anode current <tex>$\boldsymbol{I_{a}=1.79}$</tex> A, operating frequency <tex>$\boldsymbol{f_{1}=2.4624}$</tex> GHz and, which resulted an increase in electronic efficiency of the magnetron operation of 90.25% at external axial magnetic field <tex>$\boldsymbol{B_{0}=0.32\mathrm{T}}$</tex> and applied voltage <tex>$\boldsymbol{V_{0}=7.38\text{kV}}$</tex>. Compared with the traditional S-band magnetron, the magnetron designed in this paper provides an effective scheme for high-efficiency microwave output.

articleTitle: Velocity and Position Spread of Electron Beam in Gyrotrons
abstract: In the gyrotron, the phenomenon that electron velocity spread coupled with beam radius spread may occur, which is quite different from the traditionally considered uncoupled ones. In this paper, the formation of such spatial velocity spread is investigated. It is found that the inhomogeneous electric and magnetic fields in the cathode region are responsible for this problem. This phenomenon is much more visible in low-voltage, high-frequency gyrotrons, in which the beam Larmor radius may be significantly smaller than the beam radius spread.

articleTitle: Development of the Plasma Limiter for High Power Microwave Weapon Protection
abstract: Due to the rapid development of high power microwave weapon (HPMW) technology and in order to avoid its damage to radar, satellite and other electronic systems, the protection technology is constantly breaking through. This paper introduced the threat of the high power microwave weapon (HPMW) to the receiving system, the protective effect of the plasma limiter against high power microwave weapon, and the development of the plasma limiter at home and abroad. The research showed that the plasma limiter has the advantages of high power capacity, short response time, high isolation, low insertion loss and high reliability. Faced with the urgent demand for miniaturized and integrated protective devices for the UAVs, the phased array radars and the communication systems, the plasma limiter has been developed and applied for miniaturized and broadband serialized products. However, its leakage power is too large (W level). Therefore, the research work of multi-level protection has been carried out, which has made a technical breakthrough. And it will soon realize product level application.

articleTitle: Quasi-Optical Gyro-BWO With Zigzag Transmission Line As One-Octave Bandwith Sub-THz Source
abstract: A broadband frequency-tunable gyrotron backward-wave oscillator (gyro-BWO) is discussed. The gyro-BWO under consideration is using a recently proposed interaction circuit in the form of quasi-optical transmission line where a Gaussian wave beam propagates along a zigzag-like path with vertical and inclined segments periodically spaced along longitudinal z-axis. A static B-field and translational electron velocity are directed along z-axis, so that the electron beam periodically intersects with the wave beam. The resonant cyclotron beam-wave interaction occurs in the regions of perpendicular beam-wave intersections resulting in low sensitivity to the particle velocity spread similar to a gyrotron. The 3D PIC simulations show prospects of this “zigzag” gyro-BWO in realization of frequency tunable oscillators capable of high power and unique (octave width) frequency tuning in the sub-THz range. In the paper, a general layout and results of computer modeling of major experimental components (interaction circuit, electron gun, output microwave system etc.) are discussed for a CW device using a cryomagnet with the B-field of 4–8 T. According to CST simulations, the designed gyro-BWO ensures output of nearly Gaussian wave beam of kilowatt power level at any predefined frequency within 107–215 GHz range. A gyro-BWO with a 20-T magnet is also discussed enabling continuous coverage of the 260–530 GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Research Progresses of Terahertz Vacuum Electronic Devices in AIRCAS
abstract: In this report, the developments of terahertz electronic devices in Aerospace Information Research Institute of Chinese Academy of Sciences are reported, in which the 0.5THz backward wave tube, extended interaction klystron including G-and Y-band, and traveling wave tube (TWT) including the W/G/Y-band TWT.

articleTitle: Research on UV-LIGA Process of a Folded Waveguide for 850GHz TWTs
abstract: Folded waveguide is the most mature slow-wave structure for submillimeter-wave and terahertz travelling-wave tubes (TWTs). The UV-LIGA process of the folded waveguide for 850GHz TWTs is introduced. In which a new RD-2050 photoresist is employed instead of commonly used SU-8. Good RD-2050 patterns are achieved repeatedly under optimized processing conditions. The critical dimensional (narrow side of <tex>$\mathbf{25\mu m}$</tex>) accuracy of the structure is better than <tex>$\mathbf{1.2\mu{m}}$</tex> with a nearly vertical profile.

articleTitle: $\mathbf{SrVO_{3}}$ electron emission cathodes with stable, >250 mA/cm2 current density
abstract: This work reports improved emission performance of bulk, polycrystalline <tex>$\mathbf{SrVO_{3}}$</tex> thermionic emitters with low effective work function (2.3 – 2.4 eV) and stable emission properties. We observed that long term vacuum annealing <tex>$\boldsymbol{(\sim 5\ \mathrm{x}\ 10^{-10}}$</tex> torr, <tex>$\boldsymbol{\sim 1250\ ^{\circ}}\mathbf{C}$</tex>, 100–200 hours) of as-prepared polycrystalline <tex>$\mathbf{SrVO_{3}}$</tex> cathodes results in the enhanced thermionic emission of > 250 mA/cm<sup>2</sup>at around 1175 <tex>${}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> and emergence of a low work function surface. Vacuum annealing may help to remove any surface contamination and aids the formation of the desired low work function grains on the cathode surface. In addition to the low work function and high emission current density, the perovskite oxide cathode also demonstrates excellent emission current stability which is essential for its practical applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Ku band 400W radiation-cooled Space TWT
abstract: In order to meet high-capacity and wide band requirement of communication satellite, a ku-band 400W TWT is designed in this paper. A dual-anode electronic gun, double taper helix slow wave structure, output section of SWS with Couplers, and 4-stage depressed collector are designed. The simulated results show that output power reaches more than 400W, with the electronic efficiency of 36.7<sup>%</sup>, and collector efficiency of 80.48% at 1 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design of a Planar Helix Slow Wave Structure for TWT applications in the K-Band
abstract: A novel slow wave structure (SWS) consisting in a planar helix with straight-edge connections, operating in the K-band with a very low cathodic voltage, is herein proposed. The structure has been designed so to have a working band centered around 20 GHz. Considering an electron beam generated by a cathode with voltage and current of 1700V and 15mA respectively, we have predicted a gain of 35dB and a saturated output power of 5.5W at 20GHz in a 100 periods structure. Furthermore, our SWS has been designed in order to be more promising in terms of fabrication, if compared with other similar structures already reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Low-threshold Microstrip Limiter Based on Polycrystalline YIG
abstract: In this paper, a novel absorptive ferrite frequency selection limiter (FSL) based on resonant structure loading is proposed, which has a low limiting power threshold. Such limiter substantially enhances the magnetic energy coupling between the microwave magnetic field signal and the ferrite material through a microstrip resonant structure, which will reduce the limiting power threshold. A seventh-order limiter prototype was fabricated and tested. Test results show that at low RF power, the insertion loss of the limiter prototype is less than 1.5dB, and the limiter prototype already has limiting capability at the input power of 0.2W, which significantly decreases limiting power threshold of polycrystalline YIG FSL.

articleTitle: Magnetic force calculation of static magnetic field of two-dimensional element in MFS
abstract: Any ferromagnetic object and current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field will be subjected to forces, And the electromagnetic force has a good elimination (increase) eddy current effect. So the calculation of electromagnetic force is an important part of electromagnetic field analysis. At present, MFS (magnetic focusing simulator) does not have the function of magnetic force calculation. Therefore, this paper mainly deduces a method to calculate the electromagnetic force and adds it to MFS. This method uses the principle of virtual work and the finite element method to obtain more accurate magnetic field force results. Finally, the two-dimensional axisymmetric model was used for verification, and compared with CST and Maxwell, the electromagnetic force calculation results were in good agreement.

articleTitle: Modified Accurate Dispersion Characteristics with field restricted current density distribution for Open Rectangular Planar Tape Helix
abstract: A rectangular open tape helix is analysed for its dispersion characteristics by deriving the dispersion equations that restrict the fields within the tape helix region by incorporating a confinement function. The dispersion equations are derived by applying the accurate boundary conditions to one-quarter of the structure in axial and transverse directions owing to the symmetricity of the rectangular helical waveguide. The dispersion characteristics are numerically computed from an infinite number of simultaneous equations. The computed characteristics is compared with the theoretical model of sheath helix consisting of only the fundamental harmonics. Plotted dispersion characteristics reveals the potential usability of such devices as compact traveling wave tubes by miniaturization and can be printed.

articleTitle: Development of the Terahertz Sheet-Beam TWT Amplifier in BVERI
abstract: A G-band sheet beam TWT amplifier with output power over 100 W has been successfully developed in BVERI. The research project of the terahertz sheet-beam TWT is outlined with the technical challenges analyzed. To develop the new SWS more suitable for the sheet beam at terahertz frequencies is a focus in the next work, which can greatly promote the performance of the devices.

articleTitle: Fabrication of G-band Double Corrugated Waveguide by Precision Cutting
abstract: Fabrication of sub-THz slow wave structures usually requires expensive high precision equipment. A low cost fabrication method for the double corrugated waveguide at sub-THz frequencies is proposed. The use of the precision cutting machine permits to quickly produce square pillars with dimensions in the range of hundreds of microns or smaller with good precision. A double corrugated waveguide has been simulated at G-band (275 - 305 GHz) with the geometry modification to keep into account the cutting profile produced by the cutting wheel. A first sample of pillars with cross section <tex>$\mathbf{70}\times \mathbf{70}$</tex> microns by using the precision cutting has been demonstrated. The preliminary results are promising making the process a possible alternative to CNC milling or UV-LIGA.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Test of a 1.7kW W-Band Sheet Beam Staggered Double-grating TWT
abstract: The CST simulation results, cold test results and hot test experiment for a W-band sheet beam staggered double-grating TWT are reported in the paper. A 1.7kW peak output power at 94GHz is obtained under 32kV operating voltage and 550mA sheet beam current

articleTitle: Multiple Beam Higher Order Mode W-Band Extended Interaction Oscillator With Improved Transmission Rate
abstract: A Compact Multi-beam Extended interaction oscillator (MBEIO) has been designed with an attempt to address the power-limitation problem associated with the fundamental-mode EIO and to improve the beam-transmission rate by making the overall-length of the cavity shorter. The W-band MBEIO operates in the <tex>$TM_{31}-2\pi$</tex> higher-order-mode (HOM) to increase the cavity size which in turn increases the power-handling capability and relaxes the high machining-precision requirement. The overall axial-length is made shorter by exploiting the synchronous-condition and by lowering the beam-voltage which may alleviate the problem of low beam-transmission in conventional EIOs with longer beam tunnels. Both the CST-PIC and MAGIC-3D simulations predict a stable device operation after 30ns with and an output power of 7.5kW and 7.38kW respectively. Furthermore, to account for the losses due to skin effects in the W-band and surface roughness the reduced conductivity of <tex>$4.12 \times 10^{7}(S/m)$</tex> is used for background copper material.

articleTitle: Development of Ka-band 100W Radiation-cooled Space TWT
abstract: The Ka-band 100W radiation-cooled space TWT has been developed in Nanjing Sanle Group Co. LTD, which has the bandwidth 2GHz, the output power more than 103W, the overall-efficiency more than 63% and the weight less than 950g. It's dimension is 344mm*135mm*135mm. The TWT has passed the space qualification and reliability tests, and its reliability has been proved by test results. The development process of the radiation-cooled space TWT are introduced briefly in this paper.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of X-Band Phase-Locking Magnetrons
abstract: This paper introduced the preliminary study on <tex>$X$</tex>-Band phase-locking magnetrons. This study was aimed at designing a high-power microwave radiation source with magnetrons based on phase-locking and power-combining theory. The relevant simulation results showed three magnetrons connected by carefully-designed coupling bridges could realize the phase-locking design and ensure magnetrons operate in the <tex>$\pi$</tex>-mode without mode competition. Meanwhile, the results showed the total output power of a phase-locking system with three magnetrons nearly tripled the output power of a free-running magnetron. This work laid a foundation for further study about magnetrons with array design for satisfying the practical application requirements.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Short-circuit Withstand Capability of Press-pack IGBT modules with Optimized Package Structures
abstract: In this paper, based on the finite element simulation, the short-circuit process of press-pack IGBT modules (PP-IGBT) with various optimized package structures are compared and analyzed, and the effect of package structure design on the short-circuit withstand capability (SCWC) is analyzed. First, several finite element (FE) models of PP-IGBT with existing typical optimized package structure, including silver sintered, liquid metal optimized and phase change materials optimized PP-IGBT are established. Next, the actual short-circuit process of PP-IGBT is obtained, and the short-circuit processes of PP-IGBT with various package structures are compared and analyzed based on the FE simulation results. Finally, the effect of package design, including the optimized location and the chip-attaching layer thickness on the SCWC are investigated. The simulation results show that the SCWC can be improved by about 5% by adding the chip-attaching layer on emitter side.

articleTitle: Design of A High Average Power Gyro-TWT Loaded with Dielectric High-frequency System
abstract: In this paper, a high average power gyrotron tr -aveling wave tube (gyro-Twt)with a radial power-dividing wav -eguide stage is designed and simulated. To suppress the potential gyro-backward wave oscillator interactions involving the spurious modes TE<inf>11</inf> and <tex>$\text{TE}_{21}$</tex> and increase the heat dissipation area, a new type lossy ceramic loaded structure is used in the high frequency (HF) interaction circuit of gyro-TWT. The particle in cell (PIC) simulations show that the new topology structure has stable high-power output performances. The pulse peak output power of this gyro-TWT is 163kW at 34.5 GHz, corresponding to a satu -rated gain of 53.14 dB and an efficiency of 27.21%.

articleTitle: The study of micro-nano structure design for radiation excited by free electron beam
abstract: When electrons pass above the metallic micro/nano periodic structure, radiation is generated. Through the radiation field, the periodic structure and electrons will have interaction forces. Similarly, radiation with different distribution coefficients may achieve by adjusting the interaction force between the periodic structure and electrons. On this basis, we designed different micro-nano structures based on radiation mechanism, and analyzed the dependence of the energy distribution and spectra of the diffracted radiation with the structure shape. This research helps study radiation in complex micro-nano periodic structures. And it is expected to be used in Terahertz radiation sources to improve the efficiency of electron radiation.

articleTitle: Design of a G-Band Quasi-optics mode converter
abstract: The loss of terahertz waves in transmission lines should not be neglected, and the use of Gaussian beam propagation electromagnetic waves can make the energy highly concentrated at the center of the transmission structure, which helps to reduce the loss. In this paper, a smooth-walled dual-mode antenna is designed for receiving Gaussian beams in the terahertz band, which is converted into TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>waveguide mode to facilitate subsequent conversion to the mode required for beam-wave interaction in electric vacuum devices. The VSWR of the Gaussian beam reception system in G band designed in this paper is less than 1.06. And the efficiency of receiving the ideal Gaussian beam is more than 93%. The use of this technique will be beneficial to solve the problem of high loss at higher frequency bands such as 1 THz.

articleTitle: Effect Analysis of Local-Regional Increment of Secondary Emission Yield on Multipactor Formation
abstract: Multipactor is a detrimental electromagnetic phenomenon caused by the secondary electron avalanche in powerful microwave devices. The spatial discrepancy of the secondary emission yield (SEY) is probably exacerbated by local-regional SEY increment due to unexpected surface contamination or gas-absorption. This accordingly results in an increased risk of multipactor onset. In this research, multipactor process modeling and threshold analysis of the parallel plates with local-regional SEY increment are performed with 2D, 2-velocity statistical modeling to investigate the effect of the spatial SEY discrepancy on multipactor formation. The results indicate that the multipactor onset condition is greatly affected by the high-SEY region, which can fully dominate multipactor establishment especially when the region size is on the order of a centimeter.

articleTitle: Recent Results of a 50 GHz High Power Gyrotron for ECRH at XL-50 Tokamak
abstract: Recently, a 50 GHz high power gyrotron has been developed at IAE-CAEP. This gyrotron was developed for ECRH experiments at the spherical tokamak XL-50. The gyrotron has a diode type magnetron injection gun (MIG). The operating cavity mode is TE<inf>8,3</inf>, which is converted into a Gaussian mode by an internal quasi-optical mode converter. In order to enhance the overall efficiency, a single stage depressed collector with a sweeping coil is used. According to the simulation results, 500 kW output power could be expected. A prototype of the gyrotron was completed and tested. In the high power operation, output power of 200 kW with 5 s pulse duration at 50.05 GHz was achieved. The efficiency is ~38%. And 300 kW for 3 s with 30% efficiency was obtained. However, the output efficiency is low and some unstable problems occurred in the operation. Some improvements should be made to enhance both power and efficiency. Now the prototype has been installed at the XL-50 tokamak and used as a trial product in the ECRH experiments.

articleTitle: MMW Broadband Radar Compressed Sensing Imaging Based on SAMP Optimization Algorithm
abstract: With the development of gyrotron traveling wave amplifier, long-range high-resolution millimeterwave (MMW) imaging broadband radar has been developed rapidly. Nyquist theorem brings challenges to wideband radar signal sampling, and the hardware complexity and cost of the required equipment will increase significantly. Compression sensing (CS) takes advantage of the sparsity of the signal in the transformation domain. Under the condition that it is far less than Nyquist sampling rate, it uses random sampling to obtain discrete samples of the signal, and then perfectly reconstructs the signal through nonlinear reconstruction algorithm. This paper proposes a linear majorization sparsity adaptive matching pursuit (LMSAMP) algorithm based on CS theory. The LMSAMP algorithm with adaptive optimization step size selection is used to reconstructed two-dimensional image of wideband MMW radar. The imaging results show that LMSAMP algorithm has a good imaging effect.

articleTitle: Design of Depressed Collector for 0.22THz Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, the design of the single-stage depressed collector of 0.22 THz traveling wave tube is introduced. A novel sawtooth structure is proposed to reduce the secondary electron emission and increase the heat dissipation area of the inner surface of the collector. Using PIC simulation, taking the particle data after beam-wave interaction as the entry condition of collector, and considering the secondary electron emission, the recovery efficiency of 88.6% is obtained, which is 6% higher than that of collector without sawtooth. These studies show that the sawtooth depressed collector is helpful to improve the overall tube efficiency of TWT.

articleTitle: Enhanced field electron emission from ZnO nanowires by $\text{Bi}_{0.5}\text{Sb}_{1.5}\text{Te}_{3}$ coating
abstract: Joule heating would be generated in the field emission process of the nanowire field emitter. This could induce the rising of the temperature, cause energy loss and lead to melting of the emitter. In this study, in order to make use of the phenomena, a thin layer of thermoelectric <tex>$\mathbf{Bi}_{0.5} \mathbf{Sb}_{1.5} \mathbf{Te}_3$</tex> was coated on the surface of the ZnO nanowires. The field electron emission current from a single nanowire was studied. It was found the emission current of a single ZnO nanowire increased from 11.1 pA to 8.95 nA after being coated with the <tex>$\mathbf{Bi}_{0.5}\mathbf{Sb}_{1.5}\mathbf{Te}_{3}$</tex> film under the same electrical field. The effect of temperature on the field emission was also studied and it was found the field emission was more sensitive to temperature after the coating. It is proposed the enhanced current is related to the built-in potential due to the temperature gradient in the axial direction of the nanowire. Our results are important for exploring new high efficiency energy conversion device.

articleTitle: Design of a C-Band Klystron with High Power and High Efficiency
abstract: The design of a C-band klystron with high power and high efficiency (HE) is reported in this paper, involving beam-wave interaction, electron optics system (EOS) and RF window. The simulation result of the beam-wave interaction is presented, in which the klystron could deliver up to 48% electronic efficiency and 47% RF efficiency. The pulsed output power is 5.29 MW at the bandwidth of 16 MHz with the gain over 46 dB. The simulation results show that the gun of electron optics system can generate a pencil beam with radius of 4.5 mm, voltage of 130 kV, current of 85 A. Permanent magnet (PM) focusing is adopted in this Klystron, providing a peak magnetic field of 0.26 T in the interaction region. A compact two-stage depressed collector was designed for collecting particles at the end of interaction with thermal dissipation density less than 0.01 kw/cm2. RF window design is also conducted to compete the physical design study of this C-band HE Klystron.

articleTitle: Communication Jamming of High Power Microwave Pulse to UAV
abstract: High power microwave pulse (HPMP) is an effective way to anti unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), and the jamming of frequency hopping (FH) communication is the best starting point to achieve anti UAV. This paper uses DJI Phantom 4 Pro as the research object and analyzed the relationship between the power, pulse width and duty cycle of HPMP to achieve the jamming of FH communication of the UAV based on its FH communication characteristics, and the reliability of the analysis is verified through experiments. This paper can provide a good idea for the design of an anti UAV scheme based on HPM.

articleTitle: Research On High Frequency Structure of A Novel Dual-beam 0.14THz EIO
abstract: In this article, A novel dual-beam extended interaction oscillator(EIO) with frequency of 0.14THz is designed. Compared with the traditional single-cavity EIO, this design connects the two single-cavity structures with an H-T waveguide in the middle of the grating and couples the output. Through numerical calculation and computer simulation, <tex>$\text{TM}_{31}$</tex> mode, field distribution, the dispersion curve and <tex>$\mathrm{s}_{11}$</tex> parameter of a high frequency structure of 0.14THz EIO are studied. Through particle simulation, the influence of operating voltage, output structure on the output power was studied, and the optimal parameters are obtained. The simulation results show that the high frequency structural material is oxygen-free copper, the conductivity is <tex>$3^{*}10^{\wedge}7\mathrm{S}/\mathrm{m}$</tex> the voltage is 12.6 kV, the current is 1.15A, and the longitudinal magnetic field is 0.5T, it interacts with TM31 mode, and the output wave frequency is 0.14THz and the output power is 613.58W. Compared with single-beam under the same conductivity, voltage, current and the longitudinal magnetic field, the output power of the dual-beam is more than twice that of the single-beam. The novel dual-beam design could improve output power greatly.

articleTitle: A HPM Dual Transmission Array Lens for Arbitrary Polarization Rotation
abstract: A high power microwave dual transmission array lens for arbitrary polarization rotation is proposed in this paper, which consists of the variable polarizer and the circular polarizer. The principle of arbitrary transmission polarization is analyzed from theory and simulation, and the feasibility of this dual transmission array lens for arbitrary polarization rotation is verified by simulation in CST Studio Suite. The designed X-band dual transmission array lens with 64 combined units which made into a disk with a radius of 17 cm can realize the arbitrary polarization rotation and has high power capacity of 8GW, which would be applied in the HPM system.

articleTitle: Weak optical-field assisted field emission in vertically structure with nano-vacuum-gap
abstract: Vacuum electronic devices based on ballistic transport of electrons possess some outstanding advantages: no scattering, anti-irradiation and high temperature resistance. Simultaneously, electrons can release from metal surface to vacuum or gas with nanoscale gap driven by optical field emission under only a few-volt direct current bias. Moreover, low power is expected by combining its merits with light assisted field electron emission while with the help of field enhancement excited by surface plasmon. In this work, a vertically aligned structure is investigated compared to flat structure. Weak optical-field with plasmonic enhancements enhances the emitted current when DC bias significantly reduces the threshold for electron tunneling. The proposed structure may be useful for detecting, such as field strength, local field enhancement. And the designed nano-vacuum-gap is benefit for micro/nano vacuum electronic devices.

articleTitle: Volcano-structured Double-gated Field Emitter Arrays; Emission Characteristics and Applications
abstract: Volcano-structured double-gated field emitter arrays (VDG-FEAs) have realized both highly focusing electron beam and high emission current. The prototype image sensor using Spindt-type VDG-FEA has obtained a reproduced image with uniform image intensity without magnetic focusing. we describe a compact image sensor using the VDG-FEA. We are developing a 300 GHz band traveling wave tube (TWT) using a thermal cathode. We believe that the VDG-FEA is a promising cathode for the 300 GHz TWT in the future.

articleTitle: Space qualification of Dual mini-TWT for active array antenna
abstract: Motivated by the advent of disruptive flexible satel-lite payloads, Thales is radically revisiting its TWT architecture to offer cost efficient solutions with very low mass and dimensions for dense integration into active array antenna. Very short development time is at the heart of this “new space” approach. One year after presenting breadboard results, qualification is close to completion. Technical challenges are successfully reached. An electrical efficiency of 44% at 3 <tex>$\text{dB}$</tex> output power back off is demonstrated with low mass and only 32 mm spacing between TWTs for compact integration into the antenna. We present the performances of the final design and space qualification results.

articleTitle: Caculation of The floating potential of the TWT electron gun in EOS
abstract: EOS(electron optical simulator) is a three- dimensional steady-state particle trajectory code for finite elements that can be calculated electron guns and multistage depressed collector. In order to simulate the floating potential of the gun electrode when the electrode is disconnected from the power supply. EOS has added the floating potential calculation code. In this paper, we introduce the theory of floating potential calculation in EOS. We compare the results of floating potential calculated in EOS and CST, and the comparison results show good agreement. This verified the validity of the EOS calculation of the floating potential. We can use EOS to predict the floating potential performance in TWT electron gun or multistage depressed collector.

articleTitle: Development of Cathode-grid Assembly for Accelerator Application
abstract: In order to meet the emission current requirement for the electron gun in accelerators such as BEPCII and HEPS, a cathode-grid assembly was developed at Institute of High Energy Physics by cooperating with domestic cathode manufacturers in China. A cathode-grid assembly consists of a thermionic cathode and a controlled grid. The M-type dis-penser cathode impregnated with 612 barium calcium alumi-nate is applied for its good emission characteristics, long life-time and environmental stability. The grid is woven with tungsten-rhenium wire with transparency of about 80%. The peak current of 14 A with 1ns beam pulse width was obtained on the electron gun test bench. In this paper, the detailed de-sign parameters and test results are described.

articleTitle: Simulation Investigation of Reversed Cherenkov Radiation Amplifier
abstract: A metamaterial-based reversed Cherenkov radiation amplifier (RCRA) is proposed. Simulation results of the dispersion characteristics of the meta material slow-wave structure (MSWS) of the RCRA show that its fundamental wave exhibits reversed Cherenkov radiation properties. Further, the beam-wave interaction of the RCRA is simulated with an input power of 8 W, an axial magnetic flux density of 0.2 T, and beam voltage and beam current of −38 kV and 0.45 <tex>$A$</tex>, respectively, using CST PIC code. The simulation results show that the saturated output power is 388 W at 2.291 GHz, the saturated gain is 16.86 dB, the electronic efficiency is 2.27%, and the 3 dB operating bandwidth of the device is about 7 MHz (2.289 GHz - 2.296 GHz). The above results indicate that the RCRA investigated here can effectively amplify high-frequency signals, which confirms the feasibility of the amplifier based on the reversed Cherenkov radiation mechanism. Meanwhile, RCRA's MSWS has a diameter of only <tex>$0.32\lambda (\lambda$</tex> is the wavelength in free space), enabling the miniaturization of the device.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Electrons by Subnanosecond Superradiant Pulses: Modeling and Experiments
abstract: On the basis of numerical simulations, we develop an experimental scheme for high-gradient acceleration of electrons by Ka-band GW-level sub-nanosecond pulses of microwave superradiance (SR). The scheme represents a “generator-accelerator” unit, combined in one vacuum volume and powered by two coaxial electron beams. The SR pulse, generated by the external beam, pumps the “pill-box” resonator where the internal test beam is accelerated. The electron energy was determined based on measurements of the internal beam current after it passed through aluminum filters (foils) of various thicknesses. We have been experimentally demonstrated the increase in electron energy above 1 MeV at an acceleration gradient of 250 MV/m. The obtained gradient value significantly exceeds the record parameters achieved on the basis of long-wavelength klystrons.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Self-Decoupled MIMO Antenna for 5G Mobile Terminals
abstract: A dual-band multi-input and multi-output (MIMO) antenna with self-decoupled characteristic for 5G mobile terminals is presented in this paper. The proposed MIMO antenna possess a simple structure, which consists of two identical antenna elements placed very closely with an edge-to-edge spacing of only 0.012 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>at 3.5 GHz. The simulated results show that the -10 dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna are 180 MHz (3.42-3.60 GHz) in the low band and 290 MHz (4.75-5.04 GHz) in the high band, and isolation better than -18.4 dB at both two bands are achieved, which provides a promising solution to compact 5G MIMO mobile terminal antennas.

articleTitle: Deposition and Characterization of Ammonia-free PECVD Silicon Nitride
abstract: Silicon nitride is widely used in microelectronics technology, photoelectric technology and so on. Common silicon nitride preparation methods include Low Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD), Plasma Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition (PECVD), Plasma Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition (PEALD), etc. Among them, the PECVD method has the characteristics of relatively low process temperature and fast film deposition rate. In this work, we have successfully prepared silicon nitride thin films using Ammonia-free PECVD process technology and studied the influence of Radio Frequency (RF) power and <tex>$\mathbf{SiH}_{4}/\mathbf{N}_{2}$</tex> gas ratio on deposition rate of silicon nitride thin film and get a low deposition rate of 2.59 nm/min.

articleTitle: Microwave Drill based on Frequency Adaptive Solid-state Sources
abstract: This paper verifies the feasibility of the microwave drill becoming an integrated device in terms of both solid-state source operating frequency adaption and microwave radiation safety. Using the designed frequency adaptation module and timing module of the solid-state source, we solve the difficulty of resonant frequency point change due to the shape change around the drill bit during the drilling process and complete the array of continuous drilling on the camel leg bone at 3s intervals. We also met the simulation of the microwave drill in terms of radiation safety by using the parameters of the human skull to verify its feasibility for use in surgical or biological tissue experiments.

articleTitle: Design of a Tunable PCM-QM Focusing System for a 220 GHz Sheet Beam Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, the design and simulation of a tunable periodic cusped magnet-quadrupolar magnet (PCM-QM) focusing system for a 220 GHz sheet beam traveling-wave tube (SB-TWT) is presented. Simulation results show that a 0.1 A, 30 kV sheet electron beam with a cross-sectional size of <tex>$\mathbf{0.6} \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{0.1}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex> can be transported smoothly through a 75 mm-long drift tube with a beam tunnel size of <tex>$\mathbf{0.826}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{0.143} \mathbf{mm}$</tex> under the focusing of this PCM-QM. The transmission rate of the sheet beam is up to 100%. The quality of the sheet beam at the end of the drift tube is acceptable.

articleTitle: Laser-Based Technologies for Microfabrication of Key Electromagnetic Components of Miniaturized Vacuum Electron Devices
abstract: Recent results of fabrication of micron-sized electromagnetic structures and other components for vacuum microelectronic devices are presented. We focus on our practice of laser micromachining of electromagnetic structures for millimeter- and THz-band devices. Various findings from morphological examinations of electromagnetic structures fabricated by using different laser-based technologies are presented. Additionally, the benefits and challenges of using laser technologies that rely on nanosecond, picosecond, and femtosecond pulses are considered. Other microfabrication techniques like 3D printing, nano-CNC machining, UV-LIGA, and deep reactive ion etching are also briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of plasma on the radar cross section characteristics of target
abstract: In this paper, the influence of plasma on the radar scattering cross-section characteristics of the target is studied, and the results show that the plasma cladding affects the radar scattering cross-section (RCS) characteristics of the detected target. Through electromagnetic simulation, the relationship between plasma density, collision frequency and RCS, and the relationship between incident wave frequency and plasma parameters are studied. In this paper, the RCS characteristics of a metal cone covered with plasma are simulated. By changing the plasma parameters in the model, RCS data at different detection frequencies (10GHz, 15GHz, and 20GHz) were observed. The results show that the overlay plasma has a great influence on the RCS characteristics of the metal. By changing the incident wave frequency and plasma density, the specific influence law on RCS data were obtained.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Microwave Windows Tuning
abstract: An intelligent tuning method of microwave window based on reinforcement learning is proposed in this paper. Using Python script to drive HFSS, the method can obtain the structural parameters and simulation response data of the microwave window. This method takes the structural parameters and simulation response data as input and output to establish the forward prediction model and the reverse prediction model of the microwave window. HFSS environment, action, state, reward and other elements of reinforcement learning are constructed in this method. Based on this method, the S-parameter curves of microwave window can be rapidly optimized, and the microwave window with reflection coefficient less than −26.444 dB in the working frequency band of <tex>$\boldsymbol{135\sim 145}\mathbf{GHz}$</tex> is realized.

articleTitle: Research on Testing of Positive-negative polarity Pseudo-spark switch
abstract: In this paper, the characteristics of the positive-negative polarity discharge of the pseudo-spark switch are tested and studied. The positive-negative polarity pseudo-spark switch test circuit is designed based on the LTD single module circuit to test the positive-negative polarity pseudo-spark switch. The pseudo-spark switch used in this paper has four discharge gaps, and the main size of the switch is <tex>$\Phi\ 122\text{mm}\times$</tex> 104mm, the design working voltage is <tex>$\pm\ 50\text{kV}$</tex>, the pulse current value is 50kA, and the delay time is <tex>$\leqslant$</tex> 1ms. After testing, the working voltage of four-gap pseudo-spark switch is <tex>$\pm\ 40\text{kV}$</tex>, the pulse current is 11.8kA, and the time jitter can reach 8ns under fixed hydrogen pressure.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Secondary Electron Emission from Textured Structure Surface
abstract: The secondary electron emission (SEE) of microwave device materials is an important physical process affecting the micro-discharge effect of components. The surface structure design applied to reduce SEE has increased year by year, but there are few reports on the surface simulation of textured structures. In this paper, the Monte Carlo (MC) model of SEE on metal surface is used to realize the Monte Carlo simulation of the secondary electronic yield (SEY) of some specific textured structure surface, which provides a reference for the design of textured structure surface, and has important application value for studying the mechanism of SEE and suppressing micro-discharge effect.

articleTitle: Study of field emission gas pressure sensing performances of carbon nanotubes with different crystallinities
abstract: The gas pressure sensing properties of multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWNT) emitters with different crystallinities were investigated. The MWNT emitters were grown directly on the catalytic substrates with excellent emission properties. The results showed that the low pressure sensing performances, which are related to the field emission current increase, vary for helium, nitrogen, and air depending on the MWNT crystallinities in the range of 10<sup>−7</sup> to 10<sup>−4</sup> Pa. The high crystal MWNT samples presented strong air and nitrogen sensing behaviors, while the low crystal ones exhibited excellent helium sensing performance.

articleTitle: Endoscopic Real–Time Electro–Optic Sensing System for High–Power RF Signal Measurement
abstract: Metal- and semiconductor-based sensors can show distortion and degradation performance when they measure high frequency and high power radio-frequency (RF) signal. Few specialized differential probes for high RF output power measurement have a maximum corresponding frequency of about 10 GHz. On the other hand, commercial field probes and detectors support very high frequency RF signal measurement, but those are only for low output-power measurement. Thus, an RF power introduced into the probes and detectors must be reduced by attenuators and couplers in order to measure high RF power. Nevertheless, the reliability of the measurement is not good due to nonlinear characteristics of the attenuators. In this paper, we propose an endoscopic real-time electro-optical sensor with a photonic assisted circuit for high power Ka-band RF signal measurement to overcome the limitations of present sensors.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication Aspects of an E-band Double Corrugated Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: E-band (71 - 76 GHz, 81 - 86 GHz) front ends are commercially available for point to point links with a few gigabit per second (Gb/s) for range of about one kilometer at full capacity. The transmission power of E-band front ends is produced by solid state amplifiers, typically not higher than a few Watts. For this reason E-band front ends have to use large diameter antennas to ensure the required EIRP (Equivalent, Isotropically Radiated Power). The availability of power in the range of tens of Watts would enable long links with high signal to noise ratio for high modulation schemes and tens of Gb/s capacity. An E-band (71 - 76 GHz) traveling wave amplifiers has been designed to enhance the capacity of future E-band links. This paper discuss the first version of the TWT based on a single section double corrugated waveguide slow wave structure. This first prototype of E-band TWT will be preparatory to the fabrication of a more complex 70 W two sections E-band TWT.

articleTitle: Development of Quasi-Optical Mode Converter based on Metamaterials
abstract: In this paper, the development of quasi-optical mode converter based on metamaterial in University of Electronic Science and Technology of China is presented. The metal-dielectric metasurfaces and all-dielectric metamaterial are introduced into the quasi-optical mode converter (QOC) investigation. Both of them are succeeded to convert waveguide modes to free space Gaussian beam not only in simulations but also in experiments. In experiments, the observed scalar Gaussian mode contents of output wave from QOC based on metal-dielectric metasurfaces are 95.96%, 97.01%, 96.84%, and 97.85% at 35, 36, 37, and 38 GHz, respectively; the observed scalar Gaussian mode content of output wave from QOC based on all-dielectric metasurface is 97.84% at 35 GHz.

articleTitle: Indian Scenario of Vacuum Electron Devices Research and Development
abstract: The academia such as Indian Institute of Technology (IIT)-Banaras Hindu University; IIT-Roorkee; and Devi Ahalya Vishwa Vidyalaya, Indore; national laboratories such as Central Electronics Engineering Institute under the Ministry of Science and Technology, Pilani and Microwave Tube Research and Development Centre, Bangalore under the Ministry of Defence, and industries such as Bharat Electronics Limited, Bangalore under the Ministry of Defence are devoted to research and development in the area of vacuum electron devices (VEDs). The VEDs within the purview of this research and development include wideband electronic warfare travelling-wave tubes (TWTs), high efficiency space-qualified TWTs, magnetrons, klystrons, gyrotrons, plasma assisted VEDs, tubes accruing the advantages of solid state devices and microelectronics technology, fast-wave tubes filling the technology gap between the microwave and optical frequencies such as gyrotrons and gyro-TWTs, plasma assisted VEDs and metamaterial assisted VEDs. An attempt has been made to bring out the scenario of this research and development in India.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Electron Gun for Terahertz Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: A novel design scheme of electron gun for terahertz traveling-wave tubes (TWTs) is proposed, whose beam focusing electrode (BFE) includes an outer-focusing electrode and an inner-focusing electrode to form a beam-compressive electrostatic field. In this paper, the electron gun is designed for 0.22 THz TWT and simulated by OPERA Charged Particle Solver. A circular-cylindrical cathode with a radius of 0.6 mm is employed in the electron gun, which provides a circular beam of 52 mA at the beam voltage of 19.5 kV. Furthermore, the simulation characterization suggests that the designed electron gun produces an electron beam with a high compression ratio of more than 100, corresponding to the shooting distance of 16 mm and the beam waist radius of 0.05mm.

articleTitle: Design of an Input Coupler with a Bragg Reflector for a THz band Gyro-TWA
abstract: This paper presents a design of an input coupler based on a rectangular-to-circular waveguide for a gyrotron traveling wave amplifier operating at a central frequency of 263 GHz. A T-junction input coupler with a Bragg reflector was optimized and manufactured. The simulation of the coupler achieved an operating frequency range of 253–278 GHz, with the loss below −20dB. The vector network analyzer measured return loss of the input coupler is shown to be < −15 dB at 253–278 GHz.

articleTitle: Development of a Terahertz Harmonic Gyrotron
abstract: The demand for high-strength magnets partly limits the operating frequency of gyrotron increasing to the terahertz band, which restricts the further development of gyrotrons. To effectively solve the problems, the design of the 1- THz forth-harmonic gyrotron is proposed using a conventional 10- T superconducting magnet and is presented here. Low-temperature cooling, for example applying liquid nitrogen, is proposed to increase the limit of the Q factor and extend the effective length of the cavity. A large orbit gun is employed to reduce the mode competition problem. Applying multi-mode time-domain theory in the simulation, it was found that although the competing third-harmonic <tex>$\text{TE}_{3,6}$</tex> mode was excited first, the fourth-harmonic TE<inf>4,8</inf> mode finally dominates in the steady state regime. Furthermore, the experimental scheme of the 1 THz <tex>$4^{\text{th}}$</tex> harmonic gyrotron is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of A Series of 33GHz∼1100GHz Horn Antenna
abstract: A series of 33GHz∼1100GHz horn antenna has been designed and fabricated. The horn antenna comprises of conical and pyramidal horn antenna. The simulated VSWR of conical and pyramidal horn antenna is less than 1.2 and 1.1 separately. The simulated gain is more than 20dB.

articleTitle: Investigation on Maximum Operating Bandwidth for Sheet Beam Slow-wave Structures
abstract: In future electronic devices, the ultrawideband property will be a severe challenge. This paper proposed a sheet-beam slow-wave structure (SB-SWS) to realize the high-power operation in an ultrawide frequency range. Coalesced-Mode Operation for a Sheet-Beam Traveling-Wave Tube is introduced to achieve ultrawideband property. Simulation results demonstrate that the optimized RF circuit produces over 2.5kW output power (<tex>$\sim\mathbf{10}\%$</tex> efficiency) in a very broad frequency from 18 to 26 GHz, corresponding to a relative bandwidth of 36.4%.

articleTitle: Planar Slot-Line Slow-Wave Structure of a V-band Backward Wave Oscillator
abstract: A planar slot-line slow-wave structure (SWS) is proposed for a V-band backward oscillator (BWO). Consisting of only a metal sheet with a meander slot line and a metal shell, the proposed SWS is very simple to fabricate and assemble by using laser cutting and welding. High frequency characteristics and transmission properties of the proposed SWS have been investigated. According to results from particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, this structure can produce 42.1 <tex>$\mathbf{W}$</tex> of output power at 59.4 GHz. Additionally, it has a wide voltage tuning range of 8.2 <tex>$\mathbf{kV}$</tex> and a 23% frequency tuning range with a central frequency of 56.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Terahertz Computed Tomography Imaging Based on an Improved Back-Projection Algorithm
abstract: A terahertz computed tomography (THz-CT) system was proposed in this paper. The system was built based on vector network analyzer, two-dimensional rotating platform and four terahertz lenses. The transmission coefficient of the sample at different projection angles was measured with the frequency of 0.39 THz. And then the two-dimensional image of the sample was reconstructed by the filtered back-projection algorithm. The results show that the system can recognize the internal structure of the object. We also compared the effects of different filter functions on image reconstruction results. This work has potential value for non-destructive inspection, medical field and related applications.

articleTitle: AIRCAS TWT Manufacturing Research Group Released a Complete Sets of Electron Gun Solutions
abstract: The AIRCAS TWT manufacturing research group released a complete sets of electron gun solutions, and currently looking for cooperation partners in need for the design, manufacturing and testing of electron gun. Our service scope includes particle optics simulation and design, parts and molds CAD design, electronics vacuum engineering, ultra-high vacuum (UHV) and high voltage (HV) testing, precision mechanical manufacturing, exceptional welding process, etc. we hope to provide complete sets of solutions related to electron guns for TWT, EIK, Gyrotron, Accelerators, X-ray systems and custom apparatus for the space industry, etc.

articleTitle: Temperature uniformity analysis of 140GHz magnetron injection electron gun
abstract: The temperature uniformity of the cathode of the magnetron injection electron gun were analyzed by ANSYS software, and the steady-state temperature distribution of the cathode emission belt of the electron gun was obtained. By selecting the appropriate heating power to reach the working temperature, and optimizing the slotting parameters of the rear focusing electrode of the electron gun, the temperature difference of the cathode emission belt is reduced to 3.2°C.

articleTitle: Research On Fast-warm Cathode With High emission For Vacuum Electronic Device
abstract: This paper presents fast-warm cathode with high current density for microwave tubes applications. The computed results of thermal transient simulation are in good agreement in actual thermal environment of the device. Methods for improvement in temperature and emission profiles of Fast-Warm cathodes with thermal efficiency and modified activated material respectively are discussed. The characteristics of the fast-Warm cathode including emission, reliability and run-up time are introduced, with current density up to <tex>$\mathbf{50A}/\mathbf{cm^{2}}$</tex> and <tex>$3s$</tex> fast warm up in electron gun.

articleTitle: Formation of $\text{Ba}_{3}\text{Sc}_{2}\text{WO}_{9}$ on the $\text{Ba}_{2}\text{ScAlO}_{5}$ Therminoic Cathode Surface
abstract: A large number of surface analysis techniques yield the distribution and proportions of the elements on the surface. Unfortunately, little has been reported about the compounds and phase structures of the surface layers. It has been found some compounds containing Ba and Sc including <tex>$\text{Ba}3\text{Sc}_{2}\text{WO}_{9}$</tex> display low work function. While these compounds are rarely reported for practical operation cathodes. This work aims to identify the formation of <tex>$\text{Ba}3\text{Sc}_{2}\text{WO}_{9}$</tex> on the <tex>$\text{Ba}2\text{ScAlO}_{5}$</tex> cathode surface by controlling the evacuating process. Our results reveal that residual oxygen is crucial for the formation of the compound <tex>$\text{Ba}3\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{C}2}\text{WO}_{9}$</tex>. Finally, a routine process for the generation of a <tex>$\text{Ba}3\text{Sc}_{2}\text{WO}_{9}$</tex> layer is provided.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Filter Synthesis with Frequency-Variant Couplings Based on Two Low-Pass Prototypes
abstract: In this paper, the frequency-variant coupling structure is applied for the first time to a two-passband filter based on two low-pass prototype functions, which allows for a simpler topology in addition to the different order, return loss and bandwidth of the different passbands. In this work, matrix synthesis method are given to implement asymmetric double passband filters with frequency-variant coupling. By using this method, the frequency-variant coupling matrix of the dual-passband filter can be obtained. The paper gives an example of a fifth-order, three-zero-point dual passband filter designed with two passband return losses less than 15 dB and 20 dB respectively.

articleTitle: Methods for enhancing the radiation of photonic crystal
abstract: The radiation characteristics of a photonic crystal excited by bunches of line beams are studied. The maximum radiation intensity and power are discussed. The resonance effect of the photonic crystal is closely related to its structural parameters, and it is used to improve the coherence and intensity of the radiation. The effect of the electron beam positions on radiation is also given. Controlling the incident position of the electron beam can change the radiation conversion efficiency. This efficiency can be maximized through the combination of different paths. It provides a method to increase the radiated power in the terahertz region.

articleTitle: R/Q Measurements of Multi-Gap Metamaterial Extended Interaction Resonant Cavity Using Perturbation Method
abstract: In this paper, the <tex>$\boldsymbol{R/Q}$</tex> measurement method of a metamaterial extended interaction resonant cavity (MEIRC) is investigated using the perturbation method. The <tex>$\boldsymbol{R/Q}$</tex> expression for MEIRC is accordingly given, which depends on the natural frequency <tex>$\boldsymbol{f_{0}}$</tex> of the MEIRC, the perturbation frequency shift <tex>$\Delta f$</tex>, and the structural parameters. The <tex>$\boldsymbol{R/Q}$</tex> expression is verified by CST simulation where a PTFE dielectric cylinder is considered as the perturbed body. After fabrication and assembly of the MEIRC, the measured natural frequency <tex>$\boldsymbol{f_{0}}$</tex> of the double-gap MEIRC is 2.427 GHz, with an <tex>$\boldsymbol{R/Q}$</tex> of 182.5 <tex>$\Omega$</tex> and an <tex>$\boldsymbol{R/Q}$</tex> error of 1.5% relative to the simulated one. In addition, the measured natural frequency <tex>$\boldsymbol{f_{0}}$</tex> of the three-gap MEIRC is 2.443 GHz, <tex>$\boldsymbol{R/Q}$</tex> is 286.0 <tex>$\boldsymbol{\Omega}$</tex>, and the <tex>$\boldsymbol{R/Q}$</tex> error is 5.7% relative to the simulated one. The measurements reported here pave the path for developing the metamaterial extended interaction devices.

articleTitle: Multipactor Suppression via 3D-Printed Conductors
abstract: Preventing multipactor is essential for ensuring vacuum electronic systems operate reliably. Textured materials have previously been shown to significantly reduce secondary electron emission. However, these surface treatments are difficult to achieve inside of coaxial structures. Additive manufacturing can be used to produce textured components that can suppress multipactor. The multipactor breakdown threshold in such coaxial transmission lines was experimentally measured using two different 3D-printing technologies on two outer conductors. The partially 3D-printed transmission line was found to dramatically reduce multipactor (up to 2.9 dB increase in threshold power), and our experimental results consistently outperformed our simulations. This work demonstrates proof-of-concept for using 3D-printed materials for preventing multipactor.

articleTitle: The study on focusing properties of electron beam with ferromagnetic loaded vanes
abstract: When broadband TWTs adopt compound pipe shell process, non-uniformity of transverse magnetic field interferes with electron beam trajectory, making electron beam hard to be focused. In this paper, the reason of the non-uniformity of transverse magnetic field and its interference with electron movement were discussed. And a practical loaded vane structure which could ensure good focusing performance and interaction performance at the same time was proposed.

articleTitle: Power Capacity and Stability Investigation of Collector in the 50-kW-Average-Power Q-Band Gyro-TWT
