abstract: In this paper, the microwave transmission performance of the curved collector, the beam power density distribution, and the efficient interception of trapped electrons are described. <tex>$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{21}}$</tex> of the TE<inf>01</inf> mode is higher than -0.45 dB, and <tex>$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}}$</tex> is lower than -17 dB between 44–54 GHz. The dissipated power is associated with the transverse energy of the electron beam. When the gyro-TWT operates at zero drive, the collector has a maximum dissipated power density of <tex>$\mathbf{2} \mathbf{kW}/\mathbf{cm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>. The thermal analysis results indicate that the maximum temperature on the collector is 302°C. By applying a 1.35 T transverse magnetic field, the trapped electrons generated by the cathode can be entirely intercepted by the collector. The simulation results demonstrate the high power capacity and stability of the wideband curved collector.

articleTitle: Study on plasma instability of nonuniform two-dimensional electron gas
abstract: The plasma instability of two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) is a crucial physical mechanism of generating terahertz radiation in high electron mobility transistors. In this paper, a new theoretical model is presented to study the plasma wave excitation in nonuniform 2DEGs. By using the auxiliary function and Wenzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation method, the general solution of plasma waves is obtained. On this basis, combined with the Dyakonov-Shur instability's boundary conditions, the modified wave increment caused by the non-uniformity is gained, which proves that the negative gradient of electron concentration in the channel will attenuate the wave increment and decrease the plasmonic frequency.

articleTitle: Research on high parameter consistency and high yield technology of space traveling wave tube
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low product yield and poor performance consistency in the batch manufacturing process of space traveling wave tube, this paper carried out research related to the high parameter consistency and high yield technology of space traveling wave tube, focusing on improving the automatic assembly and manufacturing control technology. The feasibility and effectiveness of the technology of high parameter consistency and high yield are verified by small batch tube manufacturing experiments, which provides pioneering technical support for the promotion of the production technology of high parameter consistency and high yield for similar space traveling wave tubes.

articleTitle: Development of ITER Gyrotrons in JADA
abstract: The 170GHz ITER gyrotron is required for 1MW output power and long pulse (maximum 3600s) operation with 50% electrical efficiency. All eight gyrotron, which is planned to be procured by Japan Domestic Agency (JADA), are manufactured. Six of them are tested and successfully satisfy the ITER requirement. The other gyrotron, which can generate the 170GHz/104GHz are also designed and manufactured. The initial short pulse test is performed.

articleTitle: The Random Vibration Analysis of Electron Gun Based on Finite Element Method
abstract: As an important part of microwave tube, the reliability and stability of electron gun has always attracted more and more attentions of researchers. Because the working environment of microwave tube is very harsh, such as vibration, collision and impact. Therefore, numerical simulation technique is a necessary for researchers to optimize structures to avoid deformation and fatigue fracture in severe working conditions. In this paper, we developed the Mechanics Simulator module (MCS) of microwave tube mechanics simulation software by using finite element method. To validate MCS, numerical results for a simplified electron gun are shown compared with ANSYS.

articleTitle: Finite Element Method based on High Order Mesh for Traveling-wave Tube Simulation
abstract: Folded waveguides are common slow wave structures in traveling-wave tubes (TWT) where energy transferred from electronic beam to microwave. Efficiency of energy transition and S-parameters of a folded waveguide affect a TWT's bandwidth, output power and gain performance, etc. In this paper, we propose a finite-element framework for electromagnetic wave simulation of TWT. Arbitrary high order mesh and basis function techniques are integrated, as well as a geometry manifold embedded information for efficient mesh refinement.

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigations on Static After Cavity Interaction in a Terahertz Gyrotron
abstract: In the after cavity of a high power gyrotron, parasitic oscillations have been studied in this paper. Based on a time domain self-consistent nonlinear beam wave interaction model, a code has been created. The findings demonstrate that after cavity interaction reduces overall efficiency.

articleTitle: Study on Temperature Characteristics of Capacitance Diaphragm Gauge
abstract: Capacitance Diaphragm Gauge (CDG) is a type of sensor commonly used under low vacuum with high accuracy and stability. Temperature is one of the most important factors affecting its measurement accuracy. When the ambient temperature changes, the measurement results of CDGs will also drift accordingly. We experimented with the effect of temperature on CDGs and quantified the measurement errors of heated and unheated CDGs in the environment of <tex>$\mathbf{(-30\sim50)} ^{\circ} \mathbf{C}$</tex>. The error caused by the temperature for the unheated CDG is relatively large. The temperature-pressure error surface we proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the measurement error of the unheated CDG and improve its accuracy.

articleTitle: THz electromagnetic distribution in a layered medium uses Dyadic Green function
abstract: In this work, we provide the analytical dyadic Green function method to quickly get the electromagnetic distribution law of layered medium in the THz region. To start, we use the layered media dyadic Green's function method to determine the analytical solutions for electric fields under different emission sources. Then, using the THz time-domain spectrometer (THz-TDS) model, as an illustration, we demonstrate the model's electric field distribution under various circumstances. The THz-TDS uses an x-directed photoconductive antenna to irradiate multilayer structures with THz waves. To determine the distribution of the electric field in the medium, we employ the layered medium's dyadic Green function. Finally, an analysis is done of how the distribution of the electric field changes in various liquids. This technique offers theoretical support for the use of THz-TDS by providing a better, quicker, and more accurate analysis of the electric field distribution in a layered medium.

articleTitle: Optimization of high-power microwave sources based on deep artificial neural network
abstract: One optimization algorithm for high-power microwave (HPM) sources based on deep artificial neural network (ANN), micro-genetic algorithm (micro-GA) and particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation is proposed in the paper. The deep ANN model is introduced in the paper. The performance of the deep ANN model is tested. The test results show that the deep ANN model can be used to predict the performance of HPM devices. Then, the ANN-based micro-GA is introduced. The ANN-based micro-GA and PIC-based micro-GA are used to optimize one relativistic back-wave oscillator (RBWO), respectively. By comparing the optimization results generated by the two optimization algorithms, the correctness and efficiency of ANN-based micro-GA are verified.

articleTitle: Optimal Design and Analysis of Sheet Beam Electron Gun with High Compression Ratio
abstract: For the sheet beam electron gun with high compression ratio, the electron beam state is very sensitive to the structural parameters of the electron gun. An optimization program SB_EgunAPP1.1 is designed, which can optimize the sheet beam electron gun with high compression ratio. In this program, the optimal sheet beam electron gun is obtained by changing the structural parameters of the electron gun and then iterating continuously. We have designed several 45kV 2.5A electron guns with different compression ratios through the optimization program. It is concluded that with the increase of the compression ratio, the velocity ratio of the electron beam increases, especially in the direction of greater compression, at the same time, the current density of the cathode emission surface decreases.

articleTitle: Progress of Microwave Power Combining Based on S-band Injection Locked CW Magnetrons
abstract: The progress of the microwave power combining systems based on S-band 20-kW continue wave (CW) magnetrons are presented, which is fulfilled at institute of applied electromagnetics, Sichuan University. A series of research and experiments about injection-locking and power-combining technique on magnetrons are conducted. The performance of injection-locked magnetron is improved and a power combining system with the output power of over 60.0 kW and combining efficiency of 91.5% is first realized. This system set a new performance record for S-band magnetron power combining systems for injection-locked magnetron with an output power of over 15 kW.

articleTitle: Test of Miniaturized Pseudo Spark Switch
abstract: The main size of the miniaturized pseudo spark switch is Φ 25mm × 32mm, the anode operating voltage range is 500V ~ 10kV, and the anode pulse current is 40kA. A number of routine tests were carried out on the samples, and the cumulative work was more than 20,000 times, but no end-of-life trend was found.

articleTitle: An ultra-broadband transmission terahertz device based on multi-layer ring aperture arrays
abstract: An ultra-broadband metamaterial device is proposed. This is accomplished by meticulously designing a multi-layer composite structure array consisting of metal and medium materials, in conjunction with the integration of periodic ring holes on the metal surface and the utilization of the inherent characteristics of metal column plasma to optimize structural parameters. Parametric scanning was conducted to evaluate the transmission spectrum, with the findings confirming the resonance characteristics of the optimized structure. Simulation results indicate that, at a center frequency of 1.5 THz, the transmission rate within the frequency band of 1.04-2.26 THz exceeds 80%, reaching a maximum transmission rate of 95%.

articleTitle: Effect of Ir on the emission property of Ba dispenser cathode
abstract: Ba dispenser cathode is the widely applied thermionic cathode at present. In order to improve the emission property of the cathode to meet the requirement for the high power vacuum electron devices, Ir was added in the dispenser cathode. It is found that the emission property could be improved after adding Ir since it enhances charge transfer from Ba to O and further stabilizes the interface configuration of Ba-O-W-Ir. It is also found that the composition of the surface layer change with the activation and operation time. IrW in the cathode would benefit for the improvement of the cathode performance.

articleTitle: Modified Dispersion Characteristics with Field Restricted Current Density Distribution for Dielectric Loaded Planar Rectangular Tape Helix TWTs
abstract: The current limiting function, along with the other field boundary conditions, is used to obtain the approximate modified dispersion equation for the dielectric-loaded rectangular planar tape helix (PTH). The additional boundary condition employing the current limiting function confines the current density distribution within the surface region of the tape helix, thereby nullifying the fields in the gap regions of the PTH. Despite the increase in complexity of the electromagnetic boundary value problem, the accurate dispersion equation is derived, simplified, and verified for mathematical symmetricity. The derived dispersion equation is numerically computed for <tex>$\beta_{0a}(k_{0a})$</tex> with a significant convergence rate for each root of the <tex>$\beta_{0a}$</tex> function. The dispersion characteristics consisting of fundamental harmonic and few additional harmonics is plotted from a finite number of simultaneous equations approximated from an infinite set.

articleTitle: Some Studies on Resistive-Wall Amplifier in a Silicon Carbide Coated Resistive Wall
abstract: Resistive-wall amplifier is a promising vacuum electronic device, and thin-films based on silicon carbide can be considered as the resistive wall. The band structure, conductivity and dielectric function of 3C-SiC are studied by first-principle calculation and the Boltzmann transport equation. The gain is studied in the case of small signals for further research.

articleTitle: A Mode-Suppression Circuit for the Ka-Band $\text{TE}_{01}$ Gyrotron Travelling Wave Tube: Design and Measurement
abstract: In this paper, the design and measurement of a mode-suppression circuit (MSC) applied in the nonlinear interaction region of a Ka-band gyrotron travelling wave tube (gyro-TWT) are presented. The proposed MSC is capable to suppress the spurious <tex>$\text{TE}_{11}$</tex> mode with no influence on the operating <tex>$\text{TE}_{01}$</tex> mode which helps to improve the tube stability for the high-power operation. Simulation result shows MSC can provide a loss of more than -5 dB around 23.1 GHz for the spurious <tex>$\text{TE}_{11}$</tex> mode which agrees well with the measured results.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Mode Converter for G band TE02 mode Gyro-TWT
abstract: A study of a broadband mode converter for a G band TE<inf>02</inf> mode gyro-TWT was presented. In the designed mode converter, the radius had been changed with an inhomogeneous period. By using this, a TE<inf>02</inf> mode could be converted to TE<inf>01</inf> mode. The simulation results indicated that the bandwidth is 16GHz with the conversion efficiency is greater than 95%.

articleTitle: Transformation and Adaptation of the Kiloampere Electron Beam Generated in the Linear Induction Accelerator for Pumping a Terahertz FEL
abstract: The project of a THz free electron laser (FEL) based on a high-current relativistic electron beam is under development at the BINP together with the IAP RAS. In order to drive this FEL it is planned to use the electron beam (energy up to <tex>$E_{e}=5-$</tex> 10 MeV, current up to <tex>$I_{b}=1\ \mathbf{kA}$</tex>, pulse duration up to <tex>$\tau_{b}=100$</tex> ns, normalized emittance <tex>$\sim 550\ \pi\cdot mm \cdot mrad$</tex>) generated at the new linear induction accelerator (LIA). In the framework of previous theoretical work, it was shown that such an electron beam is a suitable driver for an FEL-system based on Bragg reflectors [1]. The proposed FEL scheme allow us to generate coherent pulses of submillimeter radiation in the frequency range of 0.3 – 1.2 THz with a sub-gigawatt power level and high energy content (up to ~ 100 J). In the report, we will discuss the main tasks of the project, the methods for their solution and the overall technical project of the FEL.

articleTitle: The development of a miniature double focusing mass spectrometer
abstract: In this paper, a developed miniature Mattauch-Herzog mass spectrometer for space exploration is introduced. The instrument is mainly composed of electron ionization source, electrostatic and magnetic analyzer, focal plane detector, which ionizes substances and measures the intensities of various ion spectral peaks. The <tex>$\boldsymbol{90}^{\circ}$</tex> magnetic analyzer with asymmetric structure is employed where the magnetic flux density is 0.25T. According to the experiment, the width of H<inf>2</inf> at 50% peak height (FWHM) is 0.0875amu which is less than 0.1amu, that is to say, the resolution capability of the instrument meets the design requirements. Besides, the sensitivity of H<inf>2</inf> is <tex>$\boldsymbol{3.298\times 10^{5}}\mathbf{V}/\mathbf{Pa}$</tex> and the minimum detectable partial pressure of H<inf>2</inf> is <tex>$\boldsymbol{3.153 \times 10^{-7}}\mathbf{Pa}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Fin-line Based Double Layer Terahertz On-chip Phase Shifter
abstract: Terahertz phase shifter is a hot research direction in terahertz technology. Compared with a quasioptical terahertz phase shifter, an on-chip terahertz phase shifter has the advantages of low insertion loss, large phase shift range, and easy integration, but it is still poorly exploited. In this paper, a fin-line based double layer terahertz on-chip phase shifter is proposed, where the phase shift is obtained by controlling the on/off state of the GaAs diode in the microstructure phase shift units. The phase shift is achieved in steps of <tex>$22.5^{\circ}$</tex> in the 216–224 GHz frequency band, with a maximum phase shift of <tex>$176^{\circ}$</tex> and insertion loss below 3dB.

articleTitle: The First-principles Calculations of Composite Interfaces for a Robust Correction of Monte Carlo Simulation on Secondary Electron Yield
abstract: The multipactor effect in the microwave components of spacecrafts and satellites can be faded and prevented by suppressing the secondary electron emission (SEE) on the material surface. For many decades, researches on the suppression of SEE have been ongoing and vigorous. Among them, the Monte Carlo simulation on secondary electron yield (SEY) is a low-cost and efficient approach to investigate the SEE, which can improve the theoretical description of physical process for experimental researches and further give a prediction of new experimental results. In order to match and follow up specially designed multilayer film process used in practical engineering, a correction factor involved with emitting probability for the Monte Carlo simulation on secondary electron emission of multilayer thin films was studied in this paper. Based on the first-principles calculations, some microscopic results of several composite interfaces including vacuum potential distributions have been figured out, which can be subsequently applied to a robust correction for Monte Carlo simulations of SEY for the corresponding multilayer thin films.

articleTitle: Terahertz Topological Photonic Integrated Transmission Line Based On Valley Spin States
abstract: Topological photonics has been extensively investigated due to its extraordinary properties, such as the robustness of immunity to defects, single-mode transmission, and linear dispersion. However, conventional topological insulators in terahertz region are challenging to be compatible with the COMS process. Here, we demonstrate the topological valley spin states in the terahertz transmission line device with -1.5dB ohmic loss and minimal reflection loss <tex>$(\sim 0.3\text{dB})$</tex>, realizing a high mode conversion efficiency between topological propagation mode and microstrip quasi-TEM mode at a broadband width of <tex>$\sim 20\text{GHz} (>\sim$</tex> 15% of the relative bandwidth) which have never been achieved before and have great potential in the application of terahertz on-chip communication applications.

articleTitle: Design of a 110GHz to 170GHz terahertz wideband Low Noise Amplifier Chip
abstract: This paper presents a design of terahertz wideband low noise amplifier by simulation. On-chip capacitors are used for interstage isolation, sector lines are used for RF bypass, and microstrip lines are used for matching circuits. In order to improve the device gain, a multi-stage amplifier circuit is adopted, and finally a five-stage LNA is realized in the 110–170 GHz frequency band. HFSS and ADS simulation software are used to jointly simulate the whole LNA circuit. The simulation results show that at 140 GHz, the small signal gain is 28 dB, the noise figure is 4.6 dB, and the 3 dB bandwidth is 40 GHz (120–160 GHz), which validate of the design.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Second and Third Harmonic Cavity Relativistic Klystron Amplifier with a Genetic Algorithm in S-band
abstract: In order to high efficiency, a second and third harmonic cavity was introduced into the S-band relativistic klystron amplifier (RKA) which was simulated with a genetic algorithm in this article. Through multi-objectives and multi-parameters optimization, we have attained multiple high-efficiency RKAs. An RKA selected with the results above was simulated in AJDISK again, and an efficiency of 79 %, a gain of 56 dB, an output power of 56 MW, and a total interaction length of 857 mm were attained when the beam voltage and current, and input power are 500 kV, 140A, and 140 W, respectively. It is essential to the fabrication and growth of the high-efficiency RKA.

articleTitle: Improved Based on 9-fold helical corrugated waveguide high-power TM01-TE01 mode converter
abstract: A compact and broadband TM<inf>01</inf>-TE<inf>01</inf> mode converter is designed for high-power microwave (HPM) transmission system. For the compact design, a 9-fold helical corrugated waveguide (HCW) is introduced to realize the direct conversion of the TM<inf>01</inf> mode into the TE<inf>01</inf> mode. To further increase bandwidth and power capacity, Fourier expansion is applied to HCW and the conventional sine-shaped HCW is improved to U-shaped HCW with larger ridge area. After optimizing the structure parameters, the simulation results show that the maximum conversion efficiency of the proposed TM<inf>01</inf>-TE<inf>01</inf> mode converter reaches 99.6% at 8.6 GHz and a bandwidth of 15.7<sup>%</sup> with a conversion efficiency of over 95% (central frequency 9 GHz). Moreover, the overall longitudinal and transverse dimensions of the mode converter are less than 4 wavelengths and the power capacity reaches 3.53GW. The results show the excellent performance of this mode converter and provide a guidance for compact mode converter with high-power capacity.

articleTitle: 0.22THz Double-Beams Staggered Double-Blade Backward Wave Oscillator
abstract: This paper proposes a staggered double-blade slow-wave structure (SDB-SWS) with two circular electron beams. At the same time, a slow-wave structure with the working frequency of 220GHz is designed. The particle in cell (PIC) simulation of the proposed slow-wave structure was carried out, and the output power of 41W was obtained at the operating voltage of 23.8kV and the single electron beam current of 35mA.

articleTitle: Design of a Sheet Beam Electron Gun and a Depressed Collector for Terahertz TWT
abstract: A sheet beam electron gun and a depressed collector for a 0.34 THz sheet beam traveling wave tube amplifier are designed. The beam current of the designed sheet beam electron gun is 0.365 A at 23 kV voltage. The sheet beam size at the beam waist is 0.2 mm <tex>$\times$</tex> 0.05 mm. The transmission of the electron beam over 3.6 mm in distance can attain 100%. The beam compression ratio is 21 when the beam trajectory is relatively smooth with good laminarity. The final optimized results show that the efficiency of the axisymmetric five-stage depressed collector can reach about 80% which can meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: Study of Mode-Competition Processes in a High Power Multimode Gyrotron Using Modified Quasilinear Model
abstract: In this paper, the modified quasilinear model of an interaction of several modes with neighboring azimuthal indexes in the gyrotron injection locking by an external signal is presented. Since the maximum interaction efficiency is provided when the gyrotron is in the hard excitation mode, mode-competition processes are an important task to ensure stable single-mode generation with high efficiency. Using the developed model, we derive the stability conditions of the single-mode regimes and analyze the domain of stability of the operating mode on the cyclotron frequency mismatch - normalized beam current parameter plane. It is shown that by injection locking by an external signal, parasitic modes are suppressed and stable generation at the frequency of the external signal with an efficiency equal to the maximum efficiency of an autonomous gyrotron is obtained.

articleTitle: Investigation on E-Band Hybrid-Serpentine slow-wave circuit
abstract: A new E-band hybrid-serpentine slow-wave circuit is investigated by theoretical analysis and numerical simulation. The results show that the hybrid-serpentine slow-wave circuit achieves higher coupling impedance than basic serpentine circuit with greater design flexibility. By allowing the vertical distances between the upper and lower centers of bend curvature for both the inner and outer bends to be different, this hybrid-serpentine circuit gains an additional degree of freedom that can be used to widen or narrow the stopband and to tailor the dispersion near the 2π point to avoid backward wave oscillations (BWO). These results predicted that the E-band traveling wave tube(TWT) with hybrid-serpentine slow-wave circuit will achieve a better performance, including high-electron efficiency, high gain and good stability.

articleTitle: Multiple-Tunnel Microfabricated Slow-Wave Structures for Millimeter-Band Traveling-Wave Tubes With Multiple Sheet Electron Beams
abstract: Miniature O-type traveling-wave tubes (TWT) are very promising as compact sources of high-power coherent electromagnetic radiation of millimeter and THz band. To achieve high level of output power, using of multiple high-aspect-ratio sheet electron beams has been suggested. This, in turn, requires development of multiple-tunnel slow-wave structures (SWS) with the appropriate electromagnetic characteristics. In this paper, we present the results aimed at development of millimeter-band TWTs with multiple-tunnel SWSs. We consider several kinds of multiple-tunnel SWSs: meander line, interdigital line, ladder SWS, and metamaterial-inspired SWS based on complementary split-ring resonators. W-band SWSs with 10–15 kV synchronism voltage and high interaction impedance are designed. SWS samples are fabricated from a copper foil by using high-precision laser micromachining. In addition, a prototype electron gun with a 180-mA triple elliptic-shaped beam is developed and tested.

articleTitle: A Planar Extended Interaction Oscillator working at $\pi$- mode
abstract: A planarized extended interaction oscillator (EIO) is proposed, with a new structure of double-deck plane multi-gap slow wave structure. The EIO with output structure operating in <tex>$\boldsymbol{\pi -}$</tex> mode is analyzed and the parametric design has been accomplished. The particle-in-cell (PIC) results show that the output power is 188.76W at 56.5GHz under the conditions of lossy metal and ideal sheet beam of 6.1 kV and 0.4A.

articleTitle: Research on High Reliability 100MHz signal Generation and Distribution System
abstract: In order to solve the multi-channel demand for high-quality frequency signal in space electronic system, based on the idea of modularization and high reliability, this paper proposes a high-quality 100MHz signal generation and distribution system. The system consists of two rubidium atomic clock and a distribution module, which can output 12 channel high isolation signals. Besides, the fault detection and real-time monitoring are achieved by designing a build in test system and communication function in Microcontroller Unit. In addition, the main and backup design improves the reliability of this system. Finally, through the test, we can know that the system's output signal has a better performance, thereby this system has an important value in engineering application.

articleTitle: Beam-Wave Interaction and Electron Optical System Investigation for a W-Band Planar TWT
abstract: The beam-wave interaction characteristics of a novel planar SWS for W-band TWT is studied. The SWS is mainly composed by meander metal line, which leads a convenient fabrication process. The simulation results show that at 96 GHz the output power of 66 W could be obtained, the corresponding small signal gain is 21.2 dB, and the electronic efficiency is 11.7%, where the working voltage is 11.3 kV. In addition, the design of electron optical systems is also studied by using PCM focusing system. The simulation results show that 97.7<sup>%</sup> of the electron transmission rate can be achieved in a 20 mm long electron beam channel.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Electron Gun for an X-ray Tube
abstract: Electron gun is a key part for all kinds of vacuum tubes, which is used to generate, accelerate and converge high energy density electron beam. In this paper, a three-pole electron gun for an X-ray tube is simulated and optimized. The goal for the design is to obtain an electron beam with small spot size, small divergence angle, high brightness and high anode current. By analyzing the effects of parameters including the filament-grid spacing, the thickness of grid, grid voltage and grid-anode spacing etc. on the trajectory and quality of electron beam, the relationship between optimization parameters and target parameters are given as well as the optimization results.

articleTitle: Studies on Additive Microfabrication of the Millimeter-band Components by LCD 3D Printing and Magnetron Sputtering
abstract: We propose a technology based on the liquid crystal display (LCD) 3D printing and magnetron sputtering for rapid and low-cost fabrication of millimeter-band electromagnetic components. To verify the proposed approach, D- and H-band straight waveguide sections were fabricated. Magnetron sputtering was used to deposit a thin copper film onto the inner surface of the fabricated structures. Morphology and profilometry studies revealed that the fabrication tolerance corresponds to the pixel size of the LCD screen in the used 3D printer, while the surface roughness is less than 500 nm with a metallization layer thickness of 5 <tex>$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. For the D-band 3D-printed samples, measured reflection loss was not worse than 20 dB, while the transmission loss was around 1–2 dB/cm. The reflection loss for the H-band samples was found to be around 15 dB, while the transmission loss ranged from 3 to 5 dB/cm. Several ways to decrease the transmission loss will be discussed.

articleTitle: A Photonic Crystal Loaded Double Sinusoidal Plate Slow Wave Structure for Terahertz TWT
abstract: A broadside loaded photonic crystal (PhC) waveguide (BPCW) slow wave structure (SWS) for terahertz traveling wave tube (TWT) has been presented in this paper. The mode competition problem, which is severe in slow wave structures, can be suppressed by the bandgap characteristic of photonic crystals. The calculation results indicate that the proposed BPCW-TWT can produce a saturated output power of over 100 W ranging from 201 GHz to 231 GHz at the operating voltage of 22.7 kV and the operating current of 150 mA. The maximum electron efficiency and saturated output power reach 4% and 137 W at 210 GHz with an input power of 0.15 W, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on the electrostatic field calculation of double-sided dielectric-loaded parallel plate waveguide
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of the electrostatic field resulting from an arbitrary distribution of charges on the surface of a dielectric layer in a double-sided dielectric-loaded parallel plate waveguide. To this end, the potential distribution of a point charge on the dielectric layer is solved by employing numerical integration and interpolation methods due to the inherent complexity of the problem. Utilizing the superposition principle, both the electric field and the potential of any arbitrary dielectric charge can be determined. This research has potential applications in space technology by allowing for the computation of the electrostatic field to investigate the multiplicative effect of double-sided dielectric-loaded components.

articleTitle: Introduction of Recent Research Progress on RM At IAE, CAEP
abstract: This paper presents recent progress on relativistic magnetron (RM) in Institute of Applied Electronics (IAE), China Academy of Engineering Physics (CAEP), including RM with diffraction output (MDO), RM with all cavity axial extraction(ACAE) RM, rectangular vane-type eight-cavity (R8) MDO, permanent magnet packaged RM and axial tuning RM. The performance of RM advances significantly in high efficiency, reliability, minimization, light weight, and wide band tuning in IAE.

articleTitle: Microwave-assisted Reactive Distillation: Simulation and Experimental Validation
abstract: The traditional reactive distillation process is not applicable to all reactive systems due to the difficulty of reaction-separation matching. The effect of microwave on specific systems will break this limitation, hence microwave-assisted reactive distillation (MARD) will broaden the industrial application of the reactive distillation technology. This study will systematically research the synthesis of di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate via MARD. The MARD process is simulated by adding side heat exchangers into each reactive stage. A microwave-transparent structured packing using the porous silicon carbide foam is proposed, avoiding absorption or reflection of microwaves. Results of pilot-scale experimental under 10 <tex>$\text{kW}/2.45$</tex> GHz microwave demonstrate the accuracy of simulation, and the rapid removal of water by microwave will intensify the esterification reaction, indicating the advantage of MARD. The sensitivity analysis investigates the influence of operation parameters on reaction conversion, providing the basis of industrial application.

articleTitle: The Measurement of W-band Pulsed Traveling Wave Tubes' Phase Consistency
abstract: The W-Band traveling wave tube (TWT) has broad application prospects in high-resolution radar imaging. The output power of a single TWT can't meet the application requirements. So it's necessary to adopt multiple TWTs as arrays. The phase consistency is a key parameter to determine TWTs' synthesis efficiency. In this paper, the phase consistency of three W-band TWTs is tested under the same condition for the first time. The test result show that the phase consistency of the three TWTs can reach <tex>$\pm \mathbf{30}^{\circ}$</tex> at 91–97 GHz, except for individual points. The test results make the foundation for the synthesis of multiple TWTs.

articleTitle: Research on a Wideband High Power Microwave Planar Antenna Array
abstract: A novel wideband microwave planar antenna array for high-power microwave (HPM) is proposed. The antenna array is composed entirely of metal and has a layered structure that is compatible with microelectromechanical system (MEMS) technology. After the antenna radomes are mounted externally, the overall breakdown pressure is enhanced by adding SF6 gas. To lower the electric field strength at the feed end and boost peak power, a tapered structure is adopted for the feed. The advantages of the structure include its high power capacity, ease of processing and installation, and compact design. At the center frequency of 2.1 GHz, the relative bandwidth (VSWR< 2) of the antenna element is 19.05%. The antenna array model with 60 elements is established, and the simulation results reveal that its overall power capacity is above 170 MW under a nanosecond pulse. At 2.1GHz, the gain of the antenna array is 24.53 dBi, and the antenna efficiency is 91.61 %.

articleTitle: The effect of Terahertz wave on neuron
abstract: The vibration and rotation frequency of biological macromolecules are in the terahertz wave band, and the terahertz wave with a specific frequency can cause the resonance of biological macromolecules, thus regulating their functions. Potassium channels play an important role in the repolarization of action potential of nerve cells, allowing potassium ions to pass through the cell membrane specifically, thus maintaining the resting potential of nerve cells. Molecular dynamics simulation shows that 53.7 THz can promote the flow of potassium ions. In the experiment, it is found that 53.7 THz laser can affect the membrane potential of nerve cells and their responses to external stimuli.

articleTitle: Study of microwave components fabricated by SLA 3D-printing and metallization
abstract: The development of the microwave devices requires testing of many variants of microwave components. Therefore, the additive technologies allowing fast and non-expensive component fabrication is of great interest. To evaluate the performance of the 3D printed and metalized millimeter-wave elements, manufactured by chemical metallization of photopolymer-based structures technology (CMPS), single-mode rectangular waveguides were fabricated and measured at the frequencies from 26 to 110 GHz. The measurement results show that the parameters of 3D-printed waveguides are close to the parameters of fully-metallic components produced by conventional techniques. Since the ohmic losses are low in the Ka, W-band, a closed cavity was used for accurate losses evaluation.

articleTitle: Research on Numerical Simulation Method of High-Power Microwave Breakdown Based on Fluid Mode
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic field finite-difference time-domain method is combined with the plasma fluid model to establish a theoretical model. A two-dimensional electromagnetic field and plasma coupling program is compiled to simulate the high-power microwave gas breakdown process, and compared with the theoretical calculation and particle simulation results.

articleTitle: Simulation and experimental study on secondary electron emission of magnesium oxide under electron incident
abstract: The trajectory of electrons in magnesium oxide was simulated based on Dekker model, and the calculation model of the SEY was established according to the motion law of electrons in magnesium oxide. The influence law of different film thickness on the SEY was calculated and analyzed. The simulation results show that the maximum SEY of magnesium oxide is between 12.0-12.5 at the incident electron energy between 800eV and 1000eV. The SEY reaches its maximum at the thickness of film about 70-90nm. The variation trend of the simulation results and the experimental data is basically the same. The experimental test results show that the maximum SEY is about 9.5-10.2 at the incident electron energy between 400eV and 600eV. The maximum SEY is obtained at the thickness of film about 55-70nm. The above results can provide guidance for the preparation of high SEY magnesium oxide film.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Electrical Characteristics of Vacuum Diode with Nanoscale Channel
abstract: A vacuum nano-diode with nanoscale channel formed from the square-hole was proposed and prepared via traditional semiconductor lithography and dry etching fabrication techniques in this paper. A thin dielectric layer with a thickness of about 20 nm corresponds to the channel length, this helps the diode operate in atmospheric environments. The effects of different vacuum channel apertures on the electrical properties of vacuum diodes were explored experimentally, and the reasons for the influence in electrical properties were elaborated in detail. The emission mechanism and working principle of the diode were analyzed through Fowler-Nordheim theory. Besides, the breakdown ability and emission current stability of vacuum diodes with different apertures were investigated by continuously voltage increasing test.

articleTitle: Analytical Investigation of I-V Characteristics of Gated Nanowire Field Emitters
abstract: The investigation of I-V characteristics of gated nanowire field emitters usually requires complicated calculation. In this study, we proposed analytical formulas to better analyze I-V characteristics of gated nanowire field emitters. This model has been validated by Comsol Multiphysics. This finding provides a simple and accurate method to optimize the structure parameters of gated nanowire field emitters and solve the calculation problems requiring enormous computational resources.

articleTitle: Simulation of RTD Material System
abstract: As a promising alternative in the development of a tunable and compact terahertz radiation source for terahertz wireless communication, semiconductor THz radiation sources have attracted many attentions. Among them, the resonant tunneling diode (RTD) is a kind of nano-device with negative resistance characteristics and becomes an important candidate for terahertz sources. It is very important to select the material before use to improve the performance of this kind of device. GaN materials have higher electron effective mass, wider bandgap and higher electron saturation velocities, the RTD based on GaN is more suitable for room temperature and high power THz source.

articleTitle: Efficient Waveguide Port Excitation for Symmetric Structures based on Conformal Non-uniform Mesh
abstract: In the full-wave numerical simulation, the use of the symmetry plane can effectively reduce the computational cost of the simulation when the model structure of the simulated device is symmetrical. In this paper, the method of imposing the symmetry plane based on conformal and non-uniform meshes when using the waveguide port is introduced, and combined with the transparent excitation source and appropriate boundary conditions, the simplified calculation of the structurally symmetric device is realized.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel High Power Octagonal Ring-Bar Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, an octagonal ring-bar slow wave structure (SWS) traveling-wave tube (TWT) operating in the Ka-band with high power and low gain fluctuation is presented. This SWS is designed as an octagonal where supported by four dielectric support rods. The electromagnetic characteristics and the beam-wave interaction of this structure are investigated by CST software and the simulation results show that this SWS can produce over 1kW average output power in a frequency range from 29 GHz to 34 GHz when the operating voltage and beam current are set to be 13.9kV and 0.7A respectively, and the corresponding conversion gain values vary from 45 to 47.6dB within this bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation for Three-Dimensional Integrated Electron Optics System
abstract: An integrated electron gun with the three-layer nine-beam array is designed based on the grid loaded method, which is a universal method to obtain multi-beam gun with narrow beam separation by one-dimensional (in y direction) compression. The characteristic of an integrated electron gun is <tex>$U_{a}=22\text{kV}, I=9\times 0.15$</tex> A. Then, a novel scheme of a three-layer with nine-beam array sharing a focusing structure is proposed to realize the stable transmission of nine-beam array, which can reduce the volume of VEDs and improve the power density. By continuously adjusting the relative positions of the integrated electron gun and the focusing structure along the z direction, a good matching state can be obtained with high beam transmission rate. The nine-beam array can transport 70 mm stably with the transmission rate of 98.6%.

articleTitle: An Noval High-efficiency Microwave Plasma Torch
abstract: The microwave plasma torch is widely used in industrial production due to its advantages of high energy density and high power. The microwave energy utilization and electric field distribution will affect the performance of the plasma torch, such as electron density, electron temperature, etc. The almost atmospheric pressure plasma torch device has low electric field intensity and poor energy utilization, which makes it difficult to excite and maintain. In this paper, a novel microwave plasma torch is designed based on a gradient index meta-surface, which can increase the electric field strength in the plasma region and allow more energy to flow into the plasma. First, the theory that meta-surfaces convert electromagnetic waves into surface waves is given, and a meta-surface that can manipulate the propagation of electromagnetic waves is designed. Secondly, the microwave driven argon plasma excitation model is established based on the finite element method. The results compared with the conventional compression waveguide show that the proposed method can increase the electric field strength by 3 times under the same input power. Third, a microwave plasma jet measurement system was built to test the excitation power, maintenance power and steady state energy utilization of different gas components. Compared with the traditional microwave plasma torch, the results show that the proposed method has higher performance and is more suitable for industrial applications.

articleTitle: W-Band Dielectric-Supported Suspended Ridged Micro-Strip Meander Line Slow-Wave Structure
abstract: In this paper, a suspended ridged microstrip meander line (SR-MML) slow-wave structure was studied for W-band miniaturized traveling wave tubes (TWTs). The high-frequency characteristics and beam-wave interaction characteristics have been investigated by using CST software. A sheet electron beam, with the cross-section of 0.42mm*0.12mm, the beam voltage of 11kV, and the current of 0.1A, is used to drive the SWS. The particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results show that the saturated output power of the SWS is 21.2W at 97GHz, corresponding gain of 11.8dB, and electronic efficiency of 1.93%.

articleTitle: Design of a Coupling Structure For Peer-to-Peer Phase-Locked All-Cavity-Extraction Multiport Relativistic Magnetron
abstract: A coupling structure is designed for phase-locked all-cavity-extraction multiport relativistic magnetron, which could transform the coaxial TEM mode into the radial rectangular TE<inf>10</inf> mode efficiently at 2.33 GHz. The coaxial port is connected with the upstream port of multiport relativistic magnetron, and the radial rectangular is used for energy coupling with another device. Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation of such coupling structure combined with a four-port relativistic magnetron is also carried out. When this device is applied a diode voltage of 550 kV, an average power of 308 MW in each downstream output port and 242 MW in coupling port can be obtain. This work lays a foundation for further researches on phase-locked relativistic magnetron with all-cavity-extraction structure.

articleTitle: Development of Visible Light Extraction System for High Energy Photon Source
abstract: Machining and fabrication of the extraction system to achieve smooth lead-in of visible light. As the core component of the extraction system, the main function of the reflector assembly is to reflect the visible light and change the direction of the beam. The surface roughness of the reflector is 0.53-0.94nm and the surface accuracy is 27.9-63nm. The vacuum of the extraction system is obtained and the leakage is checked through the ultra-high vacuum baking and exhausting process, so that the vacuum degree is better than <tex>$9.1\times 10^{-8}Pa$</tex>, the vacuum leakage rate is better than <tex>$1\times 10^{-11}\ Pa \cdot m^{3}/s$</tex> and the ultra-high vacuum storage is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of an H-Band Rectangular TE30 Mode Power Coupling Structure for High-Order Overmoded Multiple Sheet Electron Beam Devices
abstract: In this paper, an H-band (220–325 GHz) rectangular TE30 mode power coupling structure for high-order overmoded multiple sheet electron beam devices is designed. The structure mainly consists of a rectangular <tex>$\text{TE}_{30}$</tex> mode converter and an overmoded Y-shaped coupler with a Bragg reflector. A processing model for a power coupling structure joined back-to-back is designed for future manufacturing and measuring. Simulation results show that the port reflection <tex>$S_{1(1)}$</tex>, 1(1) is lower than the -15 dB over the bandwidth of 48.2 GHz (242.1-290.3 GHz), and the transmission <tex>$S_{2(3),\ 1(1)}$</tex> is higher than - 1 dB over the bandwidth of 38.6 GHz (241.7-280.3 GHz).

articleTitle: Preliminary study of a low-voltage W-band traveling-wave tube for high-data-rate wireless communication
abstract: W-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) is a good choice for high-data-rate wireless communication systems that can improve linearity, spectral efficiency, and channel bandwidth. In this paper, A novel low-voltage TWT for high-data-rate communications is presented. The proposed slow-wave structure (SWS) is capable of generating a coupling impedance of about 10 ohms at 94 GHz and with a synchronous voltage of only 10.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kV}$</tex>, Particle-in-cell (PIC) study is performed to evaluate the output power of the low-voltage TWT, and the proposed W-band TWT can reach an output power of 403.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}$</tex> with an electronic efficiency of 8.6% at the frequency of 94 GHz.

articleTitle: Development of A W-band High-power Spatial Harmonic Magnetron
abstract: It is well known that the magnetron is a kind of high-power vacuum devices but it could not effectively operate at high frequency above 90 GHz. It is an effective method to synchronize with spatial harmonic at high frequency. A W-band spatial harmonic magnetron which its electron interacts with the first backward harmonic of the radio-frequency field of <tex>$\pi$</tex> mode or its adjacent mode is presented. This kind magnetron has the advantages of large-power, high-efficiency and miniaturization. The simulation analysis, cold characteristic test and hot test experiment are detailedly introduced. The test data showed the device was able to deliver an output power of <tex>$\sim 10.0$</tex> kW and an efficiency of <tex>$\sim 8$</tex> % with a pulse width of 420ns and a duty factor of 0.1 %.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies of 75 GHz Relativistic Surface-Wave Oscillator of Planar Configuration
abstract: Based on three-dimensional particle-in-cell modeling results experimental studies of a W-band surface-wave oscillator powered by a ribbon high-current relativistic electron beam produced by SINUKI accelerator (Federal Research Center Institute of Applied Physics of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Nizhny Novgorod, 1 kA / 650 keV / 17 ns) were carried out. Efficient mode selection along a wide transverse coordinate was demonstrated by using an open planar waveguide with Fresnel parameter of 5. A stable regime of single-mode narrow-band generation is experimentally obtained. The output power measured by the calorimetric method reaches 25 MW. The radiation spectrum is measured based on the heterodyne scheme and the central frequency is 75 GHz.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized 220 GHz Circular Waveguide $\text{TE}_{01}- \text{Rectangular}$ Waveguide $\text{TE}_{10}$ Mode Converter
abstract: Mode converters are widely used in the field of electronic vacuum. Many scholars have carried out a lot of work on the theory and applications of mode converters. We designed a 220 GHz radial waveguide power combiner. In this study, a 220 GHz Circular waveguide TE<inf>01</inf>- Rectangular waveguide TE<inf>10</inf> mode converter is necessary. The miniaturized mode converter works at 220GHz and has a conversion efficiency of 99%, with bandwidth up to 20GHz. The total length of the mode converter is only 15.5mm, and the transverse diameter is 2.388mm. The miniaturized mode converter has good clutter-mode suppression ability and compact structure, which can meet the requirements of use.

articleTitle: Simulation of a MW level 140GHz Gyrotron Operating in TE28,8 Mode by CST PIC Code
abstract: This paper reports our simulation of the starting process of oscillation in a MW level 140 GHz gyrotron operating in TE28,8 mode using CST Particle Studio. The model of the gyrotron is setup using the similar parameters in Ref[1]. An 1D description of the magnetic field is used. The results of interaction are shown and give a lot of physical details of the starting progress. The wave-particle power transfer suggests a good agreement to Ref[1].

articleTitle: Development of a Ka-band 100-W Space TWT
abstract: Space traveling wave tube is widely used in satellite systems as the core device of microwave power amplification. Ka-band space TWT is primarily adopted for high-throughput satellites to provide broadband mobile communications and data transmission in air, sea, and land. This paper describes the development of a Ka-band space traveling-wave tube (TWT) at the Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences (AIRCAS). This Ka-band space TWT can produce more than 100-W continuous-wave output power and 60% minimum overall efficiency within 900 MHz bandwidth. It achieves a compact size less than <tex>$260 mm(L)\times 60 mm(W)\times 70 mm(H)$</tex> and weighs less than 0.85kg.

articleTitle: Advanced Developments for Gyrotrons Considering Designs, Tools and Test Facilities at KIT
abstract: Latest research and development on advanced gyrotron developments for Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) and plasma control performed at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) is presented. The status on the development of coaxial cavity gyrotrons for the future demonstration power plant (DEMO), on advanced gyrotron operation, key components, simulation tools and test facilities is reported. Finally, the upstarting research on future megawatt-class gyrotrons operating at the second harmonic of the electron cyclotron resonance frequency is discussed.

articleTitle: A high frequency characteristic test scheme of nanoscale vacuum channel triode
abstract: Nanoscale vacuum channel triodes are promising in the electronics field due to their high frequency, fast response and high reliability, and have attracted much attention in terms of structural design and optimization. Currently, the research on nanoscale vacuum channel triode is mainly focused on simulation and fabrication, but few tests for high frequency characteristics are carried out. In this paper, based on transmission line theory, a scheme of testing high frequency characteristics of nanoscale vacuum channel triodes is proposed. In the system, a vector network analyzer is used to measure the S-parameter of the triode, so as to further calculated the maximum oscillation frequency.

articleTitle: Duality-Based Error Estimation and Mesh Adaptation in Electromagnetic Modelling
abstract: In electromagnetic modeling, a proper computational mesh is important in analysis. In this paper, we develop a duality-based method for error estimation and mesh adaptation. Such method pays attention to the influence of error generation, propagation, and accumulation to a goal-oriented function, rather than numerical error itself. A numerical example of a 90 GHz stepped impedance resonator (SIR) filter is given, proving its capability in S-parameter-oriented computation.

articleTitle: Research on Simulation and Optimization of Micro-Heat Plate Structure of MEMS Gas Sensor
abstract: In this paper, the overall structure of the MEMS (micro electromechanical system) gas sensor suspended film micro-hot plate is optimized and improved by simulation software. Firstly, an unsupported cantilever beam structure is designed for the cantilevered film micro-heat plate. The design not only reduces the thermal stress of the micro-heat plate, but also reduces the heat loss caused by heat conduction. The result is that the power consumption of the sensor is also effectively reduced. Simulation results show that the maximum temperature near the test electrode is stable at 367.4°C, the thermal stress is 2.38 MPa, and the average power consumption is 8.9mW. Secondly, the manufacturing cost and process complexity of MEMS micro-hot plate gas sensors are greatly reduced by adopting the coplanar distribution of heating and test electrodes. Finally, the way to implement multi-channel gas detection is proposed based on the new micro-heat plate structure.

articleTitle: High-Selective Bragg Rezonators with 3D Distributed Feedback for Free-Electron Lasers of sub-THz/THz Band
abstract: Novel scheme of Bragg resonators forming three-dimensional distributed feedback has been proposed. Electrodynamic properties of resonators of this type were studied in the framework of a quasi-optical model of the coupled-waves approach, and their high selective properties with respect to the three mode indices were demonstrated under conditions of substantial oversize. Results of the theoretical analysis were confirmed by the CST simulations performed in the sub-THz range. Prospect of using these resonators in the project of super-powerful free-electron laser of sub-THz/THz band, which is currently under construction in collaboration between BINP RAS (Novosibirsk) and IAP RAS (Nizhny Novgorod), is discussed.

articleTitle: Two Surface Multipactor with Non-Sinusoidal RF Fields and Space Charge Effects
abstract: We investigate two-surface multipactor induced by non-sinusoidal Gaussian-type RF fields by employing 3D electromagnetic Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Particle Studio. We analyze the effects of the RF amplitude and the full width at half maximum (and/or half minimum) (FWHM) on multipactor susceptibility and the time dependent physics. We find that with Gaussian-type RF operation, the threshold peak RF voltage as well as the threshold time averaged RF power per unit area for multipactor development increases compared to that with sinusoidal RF operation. Shrinkage of multipactor susceptibility bands is observed in the presence of space-charge effects.

articleTitle: A new measurement method for secondary electron yield based on SEM platform
abstract: The paper proposed a new secondary electron yield measurement method based on a scanning electron microscope platform. The incident electron beam from the scan electron gun of the SEM is focused and then entirely collected by a Faraday cup matched to the SEM platform. The incident current flowing through the Faraday cup can be measured by the existing current measurement unit in the SEM platform. Then the sample is bombarded with the electron beam with the same electron gun controlling parameters and the current is read directly again using the SEM current measurement unit. The secondary electron yield can be obtained by subtracting the difference between the Faraday cup current and the sample current and dividing it by the Faraday cup current. Compared with experimental data on the secondary electron emission experimental platform existing in the laboratory, the results confirm the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An X-band Relativistic Triaxial Klystron Amplifier Towards Repetitive Phase-Locked High Power Microwave Generation
abstract: An X-band relativistic triaxial klystron amplifier is designed for the sake of operating in repetitive high power and long pulse mode. To address the issues of anode plasma and radio-frequency breakdown, a novel output cavity operating in hybrid TM<inf>01</inf>- TM<inf>02</inf> modes is particularly designed, which allows extracting microwave inwards with high power capacity and achieving the external quality factor required for optimal beam-wave interaction. A microwave of 2 GW at 9.375 GHz is generated with an efficiency of about 36%. Moreover, anode plasma due to collector erosion under repetitive high power operation can be suppressed by reducing the deposited energy density and incorporating external cooling.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of a Microstrip Meander-line Slow Wave Structure with Thermal Pyrolytic Graphite Layer
abstract: This paper explores the thermal characteristics of a microstrip meander-line slow wave structure (SWS) with thermal pyrolytic graphite (TPG) layer operating at W-band (90-100GHz). The simulation results indicate that when the a-direction of the TPG is parallel to the bottom of dielectric of SWS, the maximum temperature of the SWS is only 116.2°C after reaching steady state. A comparison of thermal characteristics of such SWS with that of the SWS without the TPG layer also shows that the maximum temperature of the former is about 40°C lower than that of the latter under the conditions of loading the same power of heat source.

articleTitle: Development of a 500W XKu-Band Miniaturized Pulse MPM
abstract: In this paper, a pulsed mode XKu-Band microwave power module (MPM) had been developed. The XKu-band MPM consists of a miniaturized helix traveling wave tube (TWT) and a miniaturized -6.SkV electronic power conditioner (EPC). The MPM could provide greater than 500W of output power from 8 to 18Ghz with 31% efficiency in 20% duty cycle. The maximum pulse width is 2ms. The dimension of the MPM is <tex>$180\text{mm}\times 90\text{mm}\times 20\text{mm}$</tex>, and the weight of the MPM is less than 800g.

articleTitle: Evaluating Mode Purity of Vortex Smith-Purcell Radiation
abstract: Vortex Smith-Purcell radiation (V-SPR) is a type of free-space free electron radiation with helical wavefront and orbital angular momentum, permitting flexible tunability in terms of topological charge and operation band based on chiral plasmons and harmonic diffractions. In this work, the criteria for assessing the mode purity of vortex modes are given. Besides, the relationship between mode dispersion and mode purity from the quantum point of view is derived according to the uncertainty relation between the azimuthal angle and the angular momentum. Mode purity allows effective evaluation of V-SPR performance and is expected to facilitate the design of compact vortex beam sources in hard-to-reach regimes.

articleTitle: Thermal Test of a Millimeter Wave Dual-mode TWT
abstract: A millimeter wave dual-mode traveling wave tube is developed in BVERI which is intended for active decoy system. It's able to work for at least 180s in poor cooling conditions which qualifies its application in missile-borne situations. Here we present the test results and mainly analyze the connection between its thermal stability and thermal structures.

articleTitle: Study of electron beam harmonic amplification methods
abstract: This paper shares a method to realize harmonic amplification of a linear electron beam and output terahertz signal. Three grating sections are used to realize the fundamental modulation, fundamental amplification and third harmonic amplification of the electron beam respectively. The field distribution characteristics of the fundamental grating and the electron beam modulation characteristics under different duty factor cases are analyzed and summarized, and the final optimization results are described. In the final structure the electron beam is loaded with a triplet amplification component in the harmonic section, in addition to the modulation by the fundamental. The final output is a high power fundamental and triplet terahertz signal.

articleTitle: Source of submm wave flux with multimegawatt pulse power based on relaxation of a relativistic electron beam in a plasma column
abstract: One of the possible approaches to generate high power (up to 100 MW) submm radiation flux is to apply mechanism of the plasma wave conversion into electromagnetic (EM) ones at intense beam-plasma interaction. Given report is devoted to study of such transformation process in case of generation radiation fluxes with multimegawatt power in the frequency range 0.1-0.6 THz. Experimental study on this approach is carried out at the GOL-PET facility when a relativistic electron beam (REB) with parameters 0.6MeV/10kA/6us is propagated in a plasma column. The plasma column with the density <tex>$\mathrm{n}\sim 10^{15}\text{cm}^{-3}$</tex> is created and confined in a multi-mirror magnetic trap (B = 4 T). In recent experiments, the energy content and power of a submm radiation flux of microsecond pulse duration achieved 7 J and 10 MW, respectively. Results of the spectral composition measurements of the flux generated by this radiation source will be presented and discussed in our report.

articleTitle: Sub-GW Power W-band Oversized Surface-Wave Oscillator with 2D-Periodical Slow-Wave Structure of Cylindrical Geometry
abstract: A powerful spatially-extended Cherenkov Surface-Wave Oscillator (SWO) of cylindrical geometry operating in the W-band was elaborated at the IAP RAS (N.Novgorod) based on the high-current explosive-emission accelerator SINUS-6 forming a tubular electron beam of 0.5 MeV / 5 kA / 25 ns with a diameter of about 40 mm. Electrodynamic system of this SWO is based on 2D-periodical structure, which combines the properties of a slow-wave system and a high-Q resonator that implements the mechanism of two-dimensional distributed feedback and provides selective excitation of the operating mode in the strongly oversized interaction space. In accordance with the simulations, in the proof-of-principal experiments a narrow-band generation was observed at the designed azimuthally-symmetrical mode with a frequency of about 74 GHz and an output power at the level of 0.15 - 0.2 GW was achieved under the oversize parameter (diameter) of about 10 wavelengths and a perimeter of the system of ~ 32 wavelengths.

articleTitle: Study of Optimizing Stable Work of Q-band Space TWT by Mearsuring the Hot-State Distance Variations of Cathode-Focusing Electrode
abstract: In this paper, the hot-state electrode distance measuring device based on 3D vision technology of Q-band space traveling wave tube (TWT) electron gun is designed and constructed, which is packaged into a planar diode structure. The optical measurement system is used to measure the hot state distance between the cathode and focusing electrodes. The test results show that the actual measured value hot state distance between the cathode and focusing electrodes of the electron gun is consistent with the simulation values, which is about 0.287mm~0.285mm. After 5000 times of switching on-off, the hot state distance between electrodes is further shortened by 0.006mm-0.11mm, which will change the electronic optical size of electron gun, the position of the injection waist and the radius of the injection waist changes from 13.23mm to 12.96mm and 0.1466mm to 0.1734mm, respectively. The changes in critical dimensions of electron beam can well explain the helix current changes of Q-band space traveling wave tube in the actual testing process.

articleTitle: Power Handling Capacity Analysis for Patch Antenna
abstract: In order to improve the performance of patch antenna in high power microwave (HPM) applications, the expanded edge for patch is proposed to reduce the electric field intensity of an all-metal rectangular patch antenna with a conical feeding structure. The PIC-MCC model is used for simulating the air breakdown around the patch. The simulation results of three different structures (unprocessed patch edge and corners, blended edge with chamfered corners, and expanded edge) are compared, and indicate that decreasing the curvature of the edge for patch antenna can effectively reduce the surface electric field strength and increase the power handling capacity.

articleTitle: Fabrication of sub-10 nm Gap by using Electron Beam Lithography
abstract: Nanogap is an important research tool in the field of sensitive photoelectric sensors. Based on the surface plasmon resonance effect, the local electromagnetic field generated by the interaction between light and matter in the nanogap will be greatly enhanced, which can realize more applications of nano-functional devices. Fabricating sub-10 nm nanogaps precisely is a difficult and laborious work due to the operational accuracy of the Electron beam lithography (EBL). In this work, we propose a new manufacturing process for the nanogap electrode pairs. The shape and size of electrode pairs were set overlapping/zero spacing/non-overlapping strategy in the layout pattern at different angles. By using electron beam evaporation technology, the adhesions of electrode pair tips with sub-10 nm gaps were mitigated. Our study demonstrates a reliable manufacturing process for sub-10 nm gaps.

articleTitle: Ge based nano-air-channel photodiode for NIR detector
abstract: In this paper, a Ge based nano-air-channel photodiode operated in near infrared band is proposed. It possesses a MOS-like structure composed of Ge substrate, oxide insulation layer/nano-air channel and metal electrode. The nano-air channel is formed between the Ge substrate and the metal electrode by removing the edge of the insulation layer, in which the ballistic transport of the electrons can be realized with. High electric field can be easily achieved on both sides of the nano-air channel at a low voltage, which enables the field emission of the photoelectrons and can be employed for photodetector. The experimental results show that a field emission photocurrent as high as 1.27mA can be abtained under a 850nm laser, which is about 25 times higher than the dark current.

articleTitle: Measurement of Electromagnetic Property of Dielectric Material Based on Transmission/Reflection Method
abstract: An improved transmission/reflection method for mm wave band is proposed in this paper. The derivation of the traditional transmission/reflection method is shown firstly. Then, the thickness resonance problem of the traditional transmission/reflection method in mm wave band is solved. The last, the improved method was used to measure the Ka band electromagnetic parameters of several materials. The experimental results were achieved, which verified the improved method in mm wave band. In the next, this method will be extended to W band.

articleTitle: A High Frequency Electronic Power Conditioner For MPM Using Series Connect Sine Amplitude Converters and SiC Power Semiconductors
abstract: A high frequency electronic power conditioner(EPC) using series connect sine amplitude converters and SiC power semiconductors is proposed in this paper, which makes currents flowing mosfets, transformers and rectifier diodes sinusoidal. According to the sinusoidal operating current of high voltage converter, the influence of the parasitic parameters from high voltage transformer and high voltage rectifier circuits is decreased, and the feedback loop becomes much more easier. By using Sine Amplitude Converters, the high voltage switch circuits realize soft-switching and the power loss is reduced. With the advantages providing by the series connect sine amplitude typology, and SiC mosfets is used for the primary converter while SiC Schottky Barrier Diode(SBD) is used for the high voltage rectifier circuits, switching frequency is increased a lot, the designed converter can provide 6.5kV output voltage with the switching frequency of over 400kHz.

articleTitle: Design and Test of Q/V Band TWT Linearizer
abstract: Based on analog predistortion technology, a broadband linearizer covering Q/V band is designed to linearize folded waveguide TWT amplifiers. The goal is to achieve amplitude expansion and phase expansion at 47GHz to 51GHz. It has the characteristics of miniaturization and integration, and has a certain gain control and nonlinear adjustment range in the band to meet the requirements of testing. According to the design results, the linearizer is developed and tested. Within the working bandwidth, the amplitude expansion is greater than 4 dB, the phase expansion is greater than 60 °, and the output gain equalization is greater than 7 dB. The development of Q/V broadband TWT linearizer provides strong technical support for LEO satellites.

articleTitle: GaN Nanoscale Air-Channel Diodes with High Rectification Ratio and Irradiation Resistance
abstract: Nanoscale air-channel transistors (NACTs) have drawn much attention due to their outstanding high-frequency properties and high switching speeds. However, NACTs remain limited by low currents and instabilities compared to solid-state devices. GaN has been one of the best cathode materials since its low electron affinity and many other excellent properties. Here, we report a vertical GaN nanoscale air-channel diode (NACD) prepared by IC-compatible technology. The device has a large field emission current of 5.02 mA@3 V and a field emission turn-on voltage of 0.6 V in an ambient environment. Importantly, the device possesses a high rectification ratio up to 10<sup>5</sup>. Furthermore, irradiation resistance of the device has been examined by fast neutron irradiation tests. Our work guides future applications of NACTs in logic circuits and radiation environments and will promote the progress of its practical applications.

articleTitle: Environmental Stability of 612-aluminate with Different Phase Structures
abstract: The 612-aluminate is widely applied as the active substance for thermionic cathodes in high-power vacuum electronic devices. Two different structures with different component phases, Ba<inf>3</inf>CaAl<inf>2</inf>O<inf>7</inf>, and Ba<inf>3</inf>Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>6</inf> + BaCO<inf>3</inf>, are acquired by sintering the precursor synthesized by the liquid-phase co-precipitation method. It is found that when exposed to moist air, the total weight gain and the gain rate of the dual-phase sample are smaller than the single-phase one. Better environmental stability favors the storage and fabrication of cathodes. This dual-phase 612-aluminate is worth being popularized for the thermionic cathodes.

articleTitle: Research on high-resolution displacement detection technology in space
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a developed high-precision displacement detector in space. It consists of two main parts, a capacitive type sensor and a displacement detection circuit system. Among them, the displacement detection circuit system consists of three main parts: the carrier signal source, the high-precision displacement detector, and the external power supply of the detector. The results show that the gain of the displacement detector is <tex>$7.129\times 10^{5}V/m$</tex>, and the resolution of the displacement can reach <tex>$6.84\times 10^{-12}m/Hz^{0.5}$</tex> at low frequency and 2. <tex>$74\times 10^{-12}m/Hz^{0.5}at$</tex> high frequency in the range of <tex>$5mHz\sim 1Hz$</tex>.

Author Keywords: the gain of the displacement detector

articleTitle: Design of a Low-Voltage Miniaturized Broadband TWT
abstract: The key design technology of a low-voltage miniaturized broadband traveling wave tube (TWT) is proposed in this paper, and the simulation and experimental test are carried out. The key points of this TWT are the electron gun with low cathode voltage, the periodic permanent magnet (PPM) matched with the beam at the channel and a slow-wave structure (SWS) with pitch of negative-positive-negative hopping. The output power has a significant improvement, and the flow performance of TWT is obviously improved. The TWT sample operates at 6--18GHz, with a working voltage of 2300V. Output power is more than 30W (more than 40W at 6-- 12GHz). Total power consumption is less than 140W, and second harmonic ratio is-10.2dBc. The TWT has overall dimensions of 25mm wide by 135mm long by 16mm tall and weighs less than 135g.

articleTitle: Experiment of a 140GHz quasi-optical mode converter
abstract: High power&short millimeter wavelength pulse gyrotron oscillators usually use high-order cavity modes as their operating modes. Quasi-optical mode converters play an important role in the high-efficiency output of high-power gyrotron oscillators. A quasi-optical mode converter designed for 140 GHz/TE28,8 mode gyrotron oscillator includes a Denisov-type launcher and three quasi-optical mirrors. By using the self-developed <tex>$\text{TE}_{28,8}$</tex> mode generator, a cold test experiment on the conversion performance of the quasi-optical mode converter was carried out. The experimental results show consistency with the design, which can be used as a design and verification method for engineering application of quasi-optical mode converters.

articleTitle: Amorphous ${Si}O_{2-x}$ nanoparticles synthesized by pulsed plasma in liquid method
abstract: Silicon oxide (SiO<inf>2</inf>-x) nanoparticles (NPs) have various applications includes bioimaging, Li-ion secondary batteries, catalyst carriers, low-dielectric materials, supercapacitors and drug deliveries. In this work, silicon oxide nanoparticles were synthesized using a one-step process, the pulsed plasma in liquid method. X-ray diffraction pattern showed the production of amorphous silicon oxide. The synthetic silicon oxide nanoparticles showed strong photoluminescence at the excitation wavelengths of 220 nm. It is expected that silicon oxide NPs synthesized by this method have potential applications including quantum dots for bioimaging and nano-ink for patterning. Considering the simplicity of this method, this synthesis method has great potential for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Simple Algorithm for Space Charge Limited Emission in a 1-D Particle-in-Cell Simulation
abstract: Cathode emission in most vacuum electronic devices (VEDs) operates in a space-charge limited regime where the current density drawn is limited by the self-fields of the space charges. In particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, the implementation of the space charge limited emission is not trivial and sometimes an over emission or nonphysical effects might be generated. In this paper, we present the implementation of the simple algorithm proposed by Stoltz et al. for space-charge limited emission in 1-D PIC simulations. The algorithm uses the value of the electric field in front of the cathode surface instead of attempting to zero the field at the surface, making the algorithm particularly well suited to the PIC simulations. For demonstration, the 1-D bounded electrostatic PIC code, XPDP1, developed by Plasma Theory and Simulation Group (PTSG), formerly at UC Berkeley, now at Michigan State University is used to simulate a space charge limited diode in which the steady-state limiting current should follow the Child-Langmuir law. After implementing the simple algorithm in the XPDP1 code, the surface electric field is computed accurately by applying the Gauss law to the surface grid and the turn on of the space charge limited emission in the planar diode is studied carefully. The simple algorithm can be further implemented to 2-D or 3-D PIC simulations for modeling VEDs with space charge limited emission. The detailed implementation and simulation results will be presented and discussed.

articleTitle: An X-band over-mode relativistic backward wave oscillator
abstract: An X-band over-mode high-efficiency relativistic backward wave oscillator (RBWO) is proposed. The main structure includes a dual resonant cavity reflector, a periodic slow wave structure and an inserted coaxial mode selector. The device uses an over-mode structure where the device operates using the pure TM<inf>02</inf> mode in the beam-wave interaction region and transmits a pure TM<inf>01</inf> mode in the output waveguide. The dual-mode reflection allows good isolation of the slow-wave structure from the diode region under over-mode conditions, while providing sufficient pre-modulation of the electron beam. The inclusion of the coaxial inner conductor allows the device to operate in pure TM<inf>02</inf> mode while eliminating other modes, and TM<inf>02</inf> has a higher power capacity. The device is capable of achieving higher microwave power output at low magnetic field conditions.

articleTitle: Keynote Speaker: Towards Miniaturized Vacuum Tubes for Millimeter and Terahertz Waves
