abstract: The new generation of highly integrated vacuum devices will benefit from functional electron sources that emit electron bunches with a temporal length of down to 1 ps. Two new laser-modulated emitters for the generation of ultrashort electron bunches are proposed. These will enable an innovative method for fabricating tunable high-frequency vacuum sources up to the THz range.

articleTitle: 32GHz Frequency Space Traveling-Wave Tubes for Deep Space Exploration TH4606/THL32070C / THL32150C
abstract: In the frame of deep space exploration missions and more particularly for the planet Venus, Thales AVS is developing two new Traveling-Wave Tubes (TWT) for the 32GHz frequency band. The first program VERITAS in partnership with CNES and JPL consists in developing a 70W output power conduction cooled TWT named THL32070C. The second program EnVision in partnership with ESA, consists in developing a 150W output power conduction cooled TWT named THL32150C. Thales AVS has a strong heritage with 32 GHz products for deep space exploration missions with the TH4606 model. This paper describes the main technical features of this 32 GHz family.

articleTitle: Thermal Design of Helix Configuration of High Power Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In order to improve waster heat handling capability of slow wave structure of traveling wave tube, optimum design of helix configuration was done by finite element method (FEM). By varying helix width and thickness, heat transfer from helix to barrel was investigated by ANSYS code. Simulation results are presented which would be useful for design of high power helix traveling wave tubes.

articleTitle: Design of A Broad-band and High-power Water-load for Q-band Gyro-TWT
abstract: The rapid development of gyro-TWT towards high power and broad bandwidth has put forward higher requirements for its supporting test equipment<sup>[1]</sup>, In this paper, we designed and processed a double cone structure water load for gyro-TWT output power measurement and absorption, and carried out simulation design and processing test. The simulation results show that the S11 is less than -40dB in Q-band, the continuous wave (CW) power capacity is 30 kw, the pulse power capacity is up to 1MW, and the S11 is less than - 26dB in Q-band in cold test.

articleTitle: The coherent Smith-Purcell radiation from composite subwavelength holes array
abstract: The moving electrons moves above the grating, the surface wave and Smith-Purcell radiation will both happen. In general, the frequency of surface wave is lower than the threshold of Smith-Purcell radiation, and it will not be radiated. With the development of nanofabrication technology, various complex micro-nano-metallic periodic or aperiodic structures have been adopted to improve the efficiency and coherence of Smith-Purcell radiation. Here, the surface wave will be transformed into Smith-Purcell radiation in a novel composite subwavelength hole array, and the Smith-Purcell radiation becomes coherent and tunable. This work provides a competitive approach to achieve a coherent and high-efficiency THz radiation, and this mechanism is particularly suitable for on-chip free electron terahertz sources with micro and nano structures.

articleTitle: A 0.65THz Extended Interaction Amplifier with Shifted Beam Tunnel
abstract: A 0.65 THz extended interaction amplifier (EIA) with shifted beam tunnel is studied. Since the closer to gratings the higher effective impedance <tex>$(\mathrm{M}^{2*}(\text{R/Q}))$</tex>, the electron beam can be modulated stronger in the shifted beam tunnel than the unshifted one, so the larger output power can be gained under the same condition. And the PIC results show that the output power of the shifted beam tunnel EIA is 1.76 W under input power of 1 mW, beam voltage of 18.2 kV and beam current of 25 mA. And the output power of the unshifted EIA is only 0.4 W in the same longitudinal distance with the same input power and beam parameters of shifted EIA.

articleTitle: Study of a 0.34THz Confocal Gyrotron Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: Gyrotron traveling wave tube (gyro-TWT) with Confocal waveguide structure can generate high power due to operating in higher order modes. In this paper, the linear and nonlinear theory of a 0.34THz confocal waveguide gyro-TWT is studied. a numerical code based on the self-consistent nonlinear theory is written to simulate the beam wave interaction. The predicted output power of 35kW can be achieved at an electron beam of 60kV, an efficiency of 12% with a saturated gain of at least 60dB.

articleTitle: KlyC expansion: Traveling wave module in Klystron simulation code
abstract: Since Klystron simulation code KlyC was released in 2017, it has been used for the design of series of high efficiency (HE) Klystron projects. Lots of new features such as coupling mode analysis, monotron diagnosis and complete small signal theory have been implemented into KlyC to facilitate sophisticated Klystron design. Nevertheless, Standing wave (SW) mode pattern is prerequisite condition in the beam-wave interaction analysis in well-established KlyC large signal simulations. In this report, the latest progress on upgrading KlyC by introducing Traveling-wave (TW) module is demonstrated for future analysis on TW or SW/TW hybrid device. It is proved that extended interaction Klystron (EIK) is still based on SW analysis so that for hybrid device development, pure Traveling wave (TW) module implementation is still necessary and essential. TW circuit model is then adopted in terms of the field excitation, based on which 2 types of exemplary TW tubes are simulated in updated KlyC. Benchmark results with CST PIC show that the accuracy could reach 5% level, taking advantage of KlyC's capability to precisely modeling the space charge effects, relativistic effects and radial stratification effects.

articleTitle: Modified Fold Waveguide Slow Wave Structure for W-band Dual-Beam TWT
abstract: Increasing the interaction current capacity and the interaction impedance is crucial to achieving high output power for traveling wave tubes (TWTs) in W-band and te-rahertz band. With the increased distance between the upper and lower metal wall of folded waveguide (FW), the slow-wave structure named dual-tunnel folded waveguide (DTFW) is formed. Compared with FW, due to its larger size, the DTFW has the same structural complexity and less manufacturing difficulty. In this paper, through the analysis of the high-frequency characteristics of the slow wave structure (SWS) using FW and DTFW, the physical mechanism of bandwidth and interaction impedance improvement of DTFW-SWS are revealed. Moreover, the particle-in-cell simulation results re-veal that, compared with a TWT using unprecedentedly excel-lent FW-SWS, the performance of TWT using DTFW-SWS has been significantly further improved in the aspects of satu-rated power, gain, and electron efficiency.

articleTitle: Particle-in-cell simulation of plasma wave excitation in two-dimensional electron gas
abstract: The excitation of plasma waves in a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) is an important mechanism for terahertz radiation and detection. In this paper, we verify the feasibility of simulating plasma waves in a 2DEG using particle-in-cell (PIC) method. To achieve the simulation model, the macro particles are filled in a thin layer and restrained by a strong field to prevent the motion in the normal direction. By perpendicularly launching an electron bunch onto the 2DEG, the processes of plasma wave generation, propagation, reflection, and nonlinear evolution are observed in phase space. It is found that the plasma wave spectrum coincides well with the theoretical dispersion relation.

articleTitle: Uniformity detection of covering layers for workpieces with Near-field microwave microscopy
abstract: The surface of workpieces has various covering layers, such as film packaging in the chip field and electroplating nickel gold in the hardware surface treatment process. It is necessary to detect the uniformity of the surface covering layer of workpieces, because the uniformity of the surface covering layer will directly affect the performance of the workpiece. We propose a method to detect covering layer uniformity using near field scanning microwave microscopy. By analyzing the dispersion of parameters such as resonant frequency and quality factor of near-field scanning microwave system, the uniformity of the sample covering can be achieved effectively without contacting the surface of workpieces.

articleTitle: Carbon nano materials vacuum electronics
abstract: Our research focuses on the vacuum electronics of carbon nano materials. Based on the unique vacuum electronics properties of low-dimensional nano materials, the progress following aspects will be introduced briefly. 1. The vacuum electronic performance of carbon nano materials. We have studied the electron emission from individual carbon nanotubes with specified chiral index, and found the size and conductance effect of electron emission. Stable carbon nanotube field emitter has developed, and for the first time in the world used the emitter to fulfil the neutralization task of a radio-frequency ion propeller in orbit for “Taiji-1” satellite. We have also investigated the performance of carbon nanotube film as a new kind of gate materials in vacuum electronic device, and reported the electron absorbance performance of carbon nanotube array. 2. Interaction of incident electrons with low dimensional nano materials. We have developed a fast crystallography characterization method and theory for large area graphene and the phenomena on its surface, and invented the related instrument, which has served for characterization of many kinds of materials. This method and instrument could be used to study the adsorption phenomena on the graphene surface. 3. The vacuum electronic effect during the synthesis of low-dimensional nano materials. By introducing the concept and analysis method of vacuum electronics, controlled synthesis of high purity semiconducting carbon nanotube array has been realized. The electric field enhancement effect and obvious difference of density of state between metallic and semiconducting carbon nanotube both play important roles. The applied external electric field has amplified the electrostatic energy difference between metallic and semiconducting carbon nanotubes, and semiconducting one is superior whatever from energy and growth dynamics. And a low voltage electric field and real time control has been further realized to synthesize high purity semiconductor carbon nanotube.

articleTitle: Terahertz high-speed on-chip modulator based on SRR
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a Terahertz high-speed on-chip modulator based on Split-Ring Resonator(SRR) by combining meta-unit, GaAs Schottky diodes and SRR. This method enhances the resonance intensity by SRR to realize higher modulation depth. The simulation results show that the maximum switching ratio of 33 dB is achieved with the insertion loss of 3 dB. In addition, the on-chip modulator based on SRR proposed in this paper provides an important development direction and concept for on-chip, integrated, high-performance terahertz dynamic devices.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Characteristics of an Interaction Extended Cavity
abstract: This paper studies the electromagnetic characteristics of an interaction extended cavity. Compared with the traditional cavity, this ladder circuit has the higher characteristic impedance, which can meet the required performance of the terahertz vacuum devices. Through the analysis of the electromagnetic characteristics of the cavity, the operating performance of the cavity could be deeply understood.

articleTitle: Study on Automated Design for Helix Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: Based on the given parameters of operating voltage, current, output power, and bandwidth, a program is developed to generate design that satisfies the given parameters for helix traveling wave tubes (TWTs). In varied bands from 2GHz to 40GHz, with targets of varied output power, bandwidth, operating voltage, and operating current, designs are automatically generated by the program to test the reliability of the program.

articleTitle: Effect of deposition temperature on Al2O3 films deposited by atomic layers deposition
abstract: In recent years, atomic layer deposition (ALD) fabrication process has attracted wide attention due to its advantages in thin film uniformity, conformity, compactness, composition, interface control and so on, and aliminum oxide (Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf>) is widely used in semiconductor field as many applications. The preparation technology of low temperature Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> film based on ALD technology was studied in this paper. Through the characterization of the surface roughness, growth per rate (GPC), dielectric constant and other properties of the films, the effects of deposition temperature on the properties of the films were studied, and the optimized Al<inf>2</inf>O<inf>3</inf> film preparation conditions were obtained.

articleTitle: Rising-Sun Relativistic Magnetron with Secondary Electron Material Axially Locally Composite Cathode
abstract: The secondary electrons of the cathode are important electrons source of the electron cloud in the conventional cold cathode magnetron. However, in relativistic magnetrons, these secondary electrons were considered harmful to microwave power and were wasted. Therefore, two schemes of secondary electron material axially locally composite cathode were proposed in this paper, and these cathodes used some wasted secondary electrons to improve the output performance of relativistic magnetron. PIC simulation in CST Studio was carried out to calculate the performance of rising-sun relativistic magnetron with this kind of cathodes. The result showed that the power increased by 15.5% and the efficiency increased by 5% with the local secondary electron material composite cathode, compared with using the solid cathode. This paper indicated the potential value of secondary electrons in improving the performance of the relativistic magnetron, and provides a reference scheme for the further development of the relativistic magnetron.

articleTitle: Multipactor Dynamic Modeling with Variable Secondary Emission Property Caused by Damage Accumulation
abstract: Surface treatments for suppressing secondary emission yield (SEY) are practically adopted for preventing multipactor occurrence within powerful microwave devices. Nonetheless, the damage accumulated in ground experiment test or during onboard operation is potential to cause unexpected SEY increment, which accordingly provokes the relapse risk of multipactor breakdown. In this research, we experimentally measures the SEY variance with energetic electron collisions and investigates the underlying mechanism. Furthermore, long-term dynamic evolution of multipactor with increasing SEY distribution is obtained with nonstationary statistical modeling to evaluate the effect of the damage accumulation on the multipactor onset condition. Meanwhile, the varying multipactor susceptibility zone and the multpactor threshold fluctuation versus the damage accumulation are calculated. This research is able to provide an evaluation method of spaceborne device lifetime with multipactor relapse risk caused by the damage accumulation.

articleTitle: Advanced Bragg Structures Open Laterally as a Way to Enhance Selectivity
abstract: Project of super-power long-pulse sub- THz/THz FEL is under development currently in collaboration between BINP RAS (Novosibirsk) and IAP RAS (Nizhny Novgorod). Advanced Bragg resonators involving quasi-cutoff feedback waves are considered as one of the variants of electrodynamic system capable to ensure stable narrow-band oscillation regime in this FEL. In this paper, we propose the use of such structures that are “open” in the transverse (lateral) direction to increase their selectivity. According to the results of theoretical analysis and 3D CST simulations, resonators of this type under conditions of substantial oversize allow formation of an operating high-Q mode with practically almost suppressed parasitic modes with high azimuthal indices. Studies and comparisons of structures of various geometries, including cylindrical and planar resonators, were carried out.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of S-band High-power Pulsed Helix TWTs
abstract: This paper mainly describes the development process of S-band pulsed helix traveling wave tube(TWT). The peak power of 12kW is achieved within 700MHz bandwidth. The average power of the test TWT is more than 1.2kW at 10<sup>%</sup> duty ratio, and the overall efficiency of the TWT is more than 50%. The power level of the S-band helix TWT is greatly increased within relatively wide band.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of Terahertz Pillbox Window
abstract: In this paper, the simulation and experiments of a beryllium oxide (BeO) pillbox windows in D-band and G-band are carried out. The physical model is established using HFSS software, and the size parameters of the model are simulated and optimized. The metallized BeO ceramics is assembled by two-steps brazing to complete the pillbox window. It has been tested that the reflection coefficient of the D-band BeO window in the 148GHz~168GHz is lower than -20dB, and the transmission coefficient is higher than -0.17 dB. The G-band BeO pill box window achieves a reflection coefficient lower than -20dB and a transmission coefficient higher than -0.17dB in the 205GHz~241GHz passband. The pillbox window has been applied to D-band and G-band traveling wave tubes (TWT) respectively, and the performance meets the device requirements.

articleTitle: Development of Cr Doped M-type Dispenser Cathode
abstract: In this paper, we doped Cr into the emission materials of M type dispenser cathodes, and then studied the existing form of Cr in different stages of emission materials and the emission performance of corresponding M type cathodes. The results show that the emission performance of Cr doped M-type cathode is related to the amount of Cr. The Cr-doped cathode with the best emission performance has a pulse emission current of 44.59A/cm<sup>2</sup>at <tex>$1050^{\circ}\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{B}}$</tex>. In the high-temperature solid state reaction products of the emission materials, Cr mainly exists in the form of chromates composed of Ba, Cr and O. The composition and valence of Cr are related to the doping amount.

articleTitle: High Power 340GHz $\mathsf{TM}_{31}$ Mode Extended Interaction Klystron
abstract: The design of <tex>$\mathbf{TM}_{\mathbf{31}}$</tex> mode 0.34 THz extended interaction klystron (EIK) with peak power greater than 100W is introduced. <tex>$\mathbf{TM}_{\mathbf{31}}$</tex> mode has a large cavity structure, which can reduce the processing difficulty. The analysis of competition risk from <tex>$\mathbf{Q}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex> shows that there is no competition risk in the designed structure. The field distribution proves that the designed structure works in <tex>$\mathbf{TM}_{\mathbf{31}}$</tex> mode, and the field increases gradually in each cavity. In the three-dimensional Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulation, at 337.6GHz, the peak output power of 113.4 W is generated. The corresponding gain, electronic efficiency and 3dB bandwidth are 39.4 dB, 2.17% and 0.32GHz respectively.

articleTitle: Research on S-band High Efficiency Air Cooled Pulse TWT
abstract: To meet the requirements of a new electronic countermeasure radar system for higher output power and higher efficiency of <tex>$\mathbf{TWT,}$</tex> an S-band high efficiency air-cooled pulse <tex>$\mathbf{TWT,}$</tex> was developed. This paper introduces the main components of the <tex>$\mathbf{TWT.}$</tex> Through the simulation design of each component and combined with the design of high-power heat dissipation structure, the development of S-band <tex>$\mathbf{TWT}$</tex> sample tube with pulse output power of <tex>$12\mathbf{kW,}$</tex> duty cycle of 10%, total efficiency of 50% and air cooling heat dissipation is realized.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Power W-band Rising-Sun Spatial Harmonic Magnetron for Fusion Power Generation
abstract: To provide high-power microwave for the heating and current drive (HCD) in the UK fusion power programme Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production (STEP), we have designed a W-band spatial harmonic magnetron (SHM) as a high-power millimeter wave source. The magnetron has 24 side cavities (rising-sun structure) and a novel axial output structure consisting of a funnel connected with a circular waveguide. Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results show that the magnetron could operate at <tex>$\pi$</tex> mode and produce a high output power of 148 kW at 95 GHz, with an operation efficiency of 89.2%.

articleTitle: Third-Harmonic 1 THz Large-Orbit Gyrotron for Creation of a Point-Like Plasma Discharge in a Gas Media
abstract: The possibility of obtaining a powerful plasma discharge ensured by 1 THz gyrotron radiation is being investigated. A pulsed third-cyclotron-harmonic large-orbit gyrotron (LOG) implemented in 2008 and operating with a radiation power of 0.4 kW at a frequency of 1 THz, was taken as a radiation source. Modification of this LOG in the 80 kV/0.7A/10 microseconds version allowed to increase the output radiation power up to 1.3 kW by improving the quality of the electron beam and reducing the share of ohmic losses in a modified cavity. The conditions for the appearance of an initiated discharge created by focused 1 THz LOG radiation in a stationary gas media are studied.

articleTitle: Thermal Characteristics of Modulation Gate in Cold Cathode X-ray Source
abstract: A static electricity-heat transfer-structural mechanics finite element simulation model of the cold cathode X-ray tube has been proposed. The gate interception characteristics has been analyzed from material, the number of grid mesh and its shape. Concerning thermal deformation, oxygen free copper UNS C10200 has advantages over SUS304 and Mo, with excellent coefficient of thermal conductivity and temperature expansion coefficient. To optimize the electronic transmittance, the number of gate grid mesh and its shape are studied. It is found that the number of gate grid mesh needs to be optimized to balance emission performance and lifetime. And among the circular, square and octagonal gate grid mesh, the circular grid mesh has the highest electron transmittance and minimum thermal deformation.

articleTitle: First principles investigation on the work function of osmium-coated Ba-W dispenser cathode
abstract: Os-coated barium-tungsten dispenser cathodes have attracted attention due to their low operating temperature, high current density and long lifetime. The tungsten in the substrate will continue to diffuse into the coating during the working process of the coated barium tungsten cathodes. In order to investigate the effect of Os coating on the emission performance of Ba-W dispenser cathodes, the work function of Os surface, Os-O-Ba surface, Os3W-O-Ba surface and W (Some atoms are replaced by Os atoms) - O-Ba surface were calculated by density functional theory (DFT). And the influence of Os on the emission properties of impregnated barium tungsten cathodes is discussed by the calculation results.

articleTitle: How to Effectively Collect Emission Current from a Horizontal-tunneling-junction Electron Source?
abstract: Horizontal-tunneling-junction electron source (HTJES) is an emerging on-chip electron source with balanced performance. The direction of conduction current is perpendicular to that of emission current in an HTJES, bringing about the competition of emission current between the anode and the collector. How to effectively collect the emission current in an HTJES? By adding a gate electrode in an HTJES, a quantitative answer is given that an electric field of over <tex>$1\times 10^{6}\ \text{V/m}$</tex> is required for over 70% collecting efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on High Power and High Efficiency X-band Pulse Space Traveling Wave Tube for Spaceborne S*R
abstract: This paper studies the main components of the high-power and high-efficiency X-band pulsed space traveling wave tube for spaceborne S*R, such as electron gun, slow wave system and multi-stage step-down collector. Through theoretical analysis and simulation design, combined with our company's high-power pulsed space traveling wave tube technology foundation, the whole tube structure of the tube is designed to achieve X-band, 3.6GHz bandwidth, pulse output power of 6000W, duty cycle of 15% The design of 54% total efficiency sample tube can further verify the design compliance of each component, and accumulate design and process experience for the subsequent development and production of this product.

articleTitle: Q/V band 80W TWT Amplifier for Satellite to Groud Uplink
abstract: With the increasing demand of communication satellite for communication capacity and bandwidth, Q/V band communication payload has become an important direction of communication satellite development, and the corresponding satellite ground forwarding link uplink has also become an important research object. For satellite ground applications, a 46.5GHz to 51.5GHz TWT amplifier for satellite ground uplink was developed, and its basic principles and parameters was introduced in this paper. Within the 5G bandwidth of Q/V band, 80W saturated power output is achieved, providing a reference for the engineering design and application of the satellite ground link of the subsequent Q/V communication load.

articleTitle: Design of a High Efficiency Miniaturized W-band Pulsed Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, a high efficiency miniaturized pulsed traveling-wave tube (TWT) at W-band is designed by using the folded waveguide as the slow-wave structure. The output power, gain, and electronic efficiency are guaranteed by using velocity-step technology. Then a three-stage depressed collector is designed to achieve efficient recovery of the electron beam after the beam wave interaction. In the simulation design, the output power is more than 133W with gain of up to 34.2dB at 90GHz to 100GHz. Meanwhile, the design scheme achieves electronic efficiency of up to 8.7<sup>%</sup> and collector efficiency of up to 91.86% over the operating bandwidth, which means that the total efficiency is expected to reach 35.8%.

articleTitle: Tunable X-rays from free electrons interacting with van der Waals materials
abstract: We theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate highly tunable X-ray sources from free electrons - of kinetic energy ranging from a few kilovolts to a few hundred kilovolts - interacting with van der Waals (vdW) materials to generate Smith-Purcell radiation. The photon energy of the output X-rays is readily tuned via the energy of the free electrons, the composition of the vdW material target and the angle between the free electron beam and the vdW material target. As an application of this compact, tunable X-ray platform, we experimentally demonstrate the phenomenon of quantum recoil in free electron spontaneous emission.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Graphene oxide and used as a field emitter of Vacuum Electronics Devices
abstract: Generation of efficient and desired shaped electron beam is the key requirements for any kinds of vacuum electron devices (VED). Graphene based field emitter have several merits over conventional thermionic emitters due to its high emission current density, zero thermal loading, easy to mount etc. In this present work, a simple, cost effective, and high throughput graphene synthesis method has been demonstrated and emission capabilities has characterize in a closed spaced diode mode inside a vacuum chamber. The emission capabilities of graphene film has simulated and experimentally validated which shows that the synthesized graphene can deliver current density upto 500 A/cm<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of a Q-Band High Efficiency Helix TWT
abstract: A Q-band high efficiency helix traveling wave tube (TWT) is designed and simulated in this paper. By using appropriate slow wave structure and taking reasonable helix pitch tapering method, high electronic efficiency and output power can be obtained. The 3D electromagnetic simulation software CST is used for the calculation of the high frequency characteristics and beam-wave interaction. The preliminary simulation results show that no oscillation is observed in the output signal. The electronic efficiency of this helix TWT exceeds 25.8% within the frequency range of 37-42.5GHz, the output power is more than 220W, and the gain is greater than 51dB.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Analysis of Traveling-wave Tube Based on Integrated Framework
abstract: Reliability and stability of structure are important in TWTs design, especially space TWTs. To design the highly reliable and stable TWTs, it is necessary to understand their instabilities in current designs and predict material failure for future designs under all operating conditions which include thermal stress, vibration, and varying temperature environments. Therefore, designers need to study the reliability and stability of TWTs under the influence of multi-physics which include electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanics. In this paper, a multi-physics simulator system has been developed based on integrated framework, which provides a powerful pre-processing front end, graphical, and computational post-processing functionality. The high-frequency circuit simulator, electron optics simulator, mechanics simulator, and thermal simulator are integrated into multi-physics simulator system based on unified data architecture. The numerical results show that the technology proposed in this paper has the same accuracy as CST MPS.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Noise Electron Gun for Traveling Wave Tube Transmitter/Receiver
abstract: In this paper, we present a low-noise electron gun design for a new type device, traveling wave tube (TWT) transmitter/receiver. The low-noise electron gun is a key part of the TWT Transmitter/Receiver, which can provide a low-noise electron beam for amplifying the received RF signal. The simulation design of the low-noise electron gun, noise performance analysis, and experimental testing have been carried out in this paper. In the experimental test, when the TWT transceiver is operating in receiving mode and the beam current is 4.5 mA with 4992 V, the noise factor of the TWT transceiver is about 18 dB.

articleTitle: Simulation Investigation of a 3-GW X-Band Relativistic Backward Wave Oscillator with Low Magnetic Field
abstract: A simulation investigation of a gigawatt-class X-band relativistic backward wave oscillator (RBWO) with low magnetic field is presented in this article. The designed and optimized RBWO by the particle in cell (PIC) simulation code CHIPIC, the microwaves with a power of 3.4 GW, a frequency of 9.4 GHz were obtained with a guiding magnetic field of 0.7 T, in which the diode voltage and beam current were configured to be 950 kV and 10.4 kA, respectively, indicating a beam wave conversion efficiency of 34% from PIC simulation. In addition, the radial size of the end of the slow-wave structure is expanded to achieve the efficient flow of electron beams in the RBWO.

articleTitle: Non-adiabatic electron optic systems for high power and medium power gyrotrons
abstract: The principle of operation of the new non adiabatic electron guns forming helical electron beams (HEBs) for gyrotrons is described. The simple analytic formulas for preliminary estimations of the main electron optic system parameters are derived. Two examples of the non-adiabatic systems aimed to use in CW gyrotrons with operating frequency 24 GHz, power about tens kW and another one with a frequency 230 GHz, power about 1 MW are optimized and described. The efficiency of gyrotron operation is investigated.

articleTitle: Output Performance of Coaxial X-band Magnetron
abstract: The megawatt power level X-band coaxial magnetron is designed. This paper describes a simple approach to calculating the initial dimensions of the coaxial magnetron by using empirical equations. The CST microwave studio is used for Eigenmode and particle in cell simulation. The diode characteristic (current verse voltage) is obtained for an in-directly heated oxide-coated cathode at different operating temperatures. It is found from the I-V characteristic that the operating anode voltage of this magnetron lies in the space charge limiting region. The output power of ~2MW for the 37kV anode voltage with a total efficiency of ~63% is obtained in the PIC simulation.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 0.34THz traveling wave tube amplifier
abstract: Development of a 0.34THz traveling-wave tube is described in this paper. This device consists of folded waveguide slow wave structure with modified circular bends, Pierce-style electron gun, and periodical permanent magnet. It has achieved over 6W of output power at 0.334THz with the corresponding device gain over 39dB, and at the same time, it can also provide 3W with 10GHz when the voltage is 19kV and the beam current is 25mA.

articleTitle: The study of intensity of surface plasmon in a metal film excited by free electrons
abstract: The moving electron as a way of exciting surface plasma polaritons in metal film has attracted much interest in the field of vacuum electronics. In this paper, based on the Drude model, the intensity of excitation surface plasmon polaritons excited by parallel moving electron bunch is studied. Based on Maxwell equations, there are deduced the dispersion relation and basic characteristics of surface plasmon polaritons on the surface of metal film. By the theoretical analysis and CST simulation, SPPs are excited by high-energy electron bunch with a certain electron velocity on the surface of a metal. The width w of the metal film, the ratio of electron velocity to light velocity <tex>$\boldsymbol{\beta}$</tex> and the metal film thickness d are mainly discussed on the intensity of surface plasma polaritons.

articleTitle: Design and Electromagnetic Uniformity Study of a Novel Dual-Source Dual-Frequency Microwave Oven
abstract: In this research, a method for improving the uniformity of heating in domestic microwave ovens is provided in an effort to address the issue of heating inconsistency. The innovation of this design is to quantitatively analyze the field distribution of the dual source and dual frequency design. The standard deviation of the field distribution can more explicitly reflect the development of inconsistency. Concurrently, it can enhance food flavor and prevent localized overheating. The scheme is as described below: using two sources and dual frequency at the bottom of the heating cavity in an orthogonal configuration to create a double-frequency feeding strategy. The two feeds have a 20 MHz frequency gap. Better simulation results are achieved by characterising the homogeneity of electric field intensity while using CST microwave studio to build and simulate the design scheme; most notably, the new design has a 411.7 standard deviation in electric field intensity in the intended area, compared to a 1262.5 standard deviation in the case of a single source. Additional proof of the enhanced uniformity is provided by on-load simulation of the design concept.

articleTitle: A Rational Function Approximation Algorithm for the Frequency Sweep of Microwave Tube
abstract: Frequency response is an important content in the design of the input/output structures of microwave tubes. Therefore, accurate and efficient computation of the frequency response of the model will undoubtedly improve our work efficiency. In this paper, we introduce an existing rational function approximation algorithm called AAA (adaptive Antoulas-Anderson). It's a speed, flexibility, and robustness algorithm. And this algorithm is extended to the frequency sweep of input/output structures of microwave tubes, by enforcing the realness condition and using the block-AAA algorithm to approximate a matrix-valued function. Through an example of the frequency sweep of a coaxial window, it is proved that the block-AAA algorithm is more accurate and faster than the Vector Fitting.

articleTitle: An On-chip Vacuum Transistor Based on a Multiwalled Carbon Nanotube*
abstract: Vacuum transistors fabricated by microfabrication technologies have gained attention recently. A vacuum transistor based on field-assisted thermionic emission from a single carbon nanotube is an emerging on-chip vacuum transistor. The device exhibits an ON/OFF current ratio as high as 104, with a subthreshold slope of <tex>$\mathbf{\sim 4}\mathbf{V\cdot }\mathbf{dec^{-1}}$</tex>. Benefiting from field-assisted thermionic emission mechanism, it displays stable emission performances at ~10<sup>-2</sup>Pa. Herein, the essential results of this novel vacuum transistor are summarized.

articleTitle: Russian gyrotrons: overview and challenge
abstract: This paper present a number of the most striking achievements of the IAP RAS and GYCOM in the development of gyro devices. High power, high efficiency operation is demonstrated in the frequency range from 25 GHz to 250 GHz. The possibility of frequency increasing up to 1.25 THz has been discussed based on frequency multiplication effects and development of improved methods of mode selection.

articleTitle: Terahertz Cherenkov radiation based on hyperbolic metamaterials
abstract: Hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) provides an efficient way to develop low-energy free-electron radiation sources. However, the design of the HMM is limited by the plasma frequency of materials, and it is a long-standing challenge to achieve the HMM in the millimeter-terahertz wave region. In this paper, a method to construct the HMM by the waveguide metamaterial is proposed. The effective permittivity is tuned by the structural parameters, and the HMM is realized by filling the waveguide with multilayer dielectrics. The designed HMM shows a topological transition process in a wide frequency region, and the Cherenkov radiation in different types of HMM is verified. The work opens a new research pursuit toward compact and low-energy on-chip free-electron-driven radiation sources.

articleTitle: Study on a miniaturized microwave near-field probe based on Split Ring Resonator
abstract: One of the key research of microwave power application is to measure the dielectric constant of the medium. Near-field probe is a nondestructive testing method that can effectively measure the dielectric constant of a medium without damaging the sample. In order to reduce the size of microwave near-field probes, a miniaturized near-field probe with microstrip open split resonant ring (SRR) designed at 9GHz is investigated in this paper. Based on the finite element method analysis, HFSS software was used to simulate the model. The results show that the design has the advantages of small volume, high sensitivity, and feasibility and reliability in the measurement of dielectric constant.

articleTitle: Near-field Enhancement Resonance of Organophosphate-Functionalized Conjugated Polymer with Metastructure in Terahertz Region
abstract: Large <tex>$\pi$</tex>-conjugated polymers have attribute broad interests for functional soft matter especially in optoelectronic applications such as organic solar cells (OSC), organic field effect transistor (OFET), and organic light emitting diodes (OLED). The investigations of <tex>$\pi$</tex>-conjugated polymers in the terahertz range were lacking because the majority of conjugated polymer research was restricted to the visible to near-infrared area due to band gaps. In this study, a series of conjugated polymers decorated with polarized organophosphate groups were thoughtfully developed and synthesized. The transmission resonance has a red-shift of more than 40 GHz frequency when coupled with a split-ring resonator array, and increased transmission was discovered in the shifted peaks.

articleTitle: L-Band 20MW High Power Klystron
abstract: An L-band 20MW wide band Multi-Beam Klystron (MBK) had been successfully developed. The structure of seven-cavity, coaxial cavities and multi-beam was adopted and the klystron is fabricated and tested. Under the condition of the pulse width of <tex>$2.5\mu s$</tex>, the beam voltage of 146.8kV and the duty cycle of 0.1%, the maximum peak power of 23.1MW was obtained with instantaneous bandwidth of 4.6% and efficiency of 56%.

articleTitle: A 2.45 GHz Microwave-Excited Atmospheric Pressure Plasma Jet Source of Low Breakdown Power Threshold
abstract: Microwave coaxial resonators are widely used to generate atmospheric pressure plasma jets which have been applied in many fields such as biomedical treatment and material synthesis. A 2.45 GHz microwave-excited plasma jet source based on the coaxial resonator is designed to realize atmospheric pressure Ar plasma jet. It is found that the plasma does not disappear when we stop the gas flow keeping the microwave excitation unchanged after the plasma jet is generated. At this time, the air components including N<inf>2</inf>, O<inf>2</inf> and <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}}$</tex> will be used as new discharged gases. Active particles such as <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{N}_{2}}$</tex>, O, NO and OH will continue to collide with electrons to maintain a new ionized state as a plasma ball. On this basis, we propose a method of using Ar gas or He gas to assist other gases generating cold plasma jets. Finally we realize <tex>$\mathbf{CO_{2}, N_{2}, O_{2}}$</tex> plasma jets which are difficult to breakdown without providing high microwave power.

articleTitle: Simulation of Small Signal Characteristics of Open Planar Tape Helix Slow Wave Structure with Straight Edge Rectangular Connections
abstract: Dispersion characteristics of a Planar Tape Helix (PTH) slow-wave structure (SWS) composed of the planar helix with rectangular straight-edge connections are performed. The PTH consists of a set of parallel conducting lines in the transverse and longitudinal directions. A simulation study was conducted to analyze and compare the dispersion characteristics of the open PTH-SWS for rectangular straight-edge connections using the 3-D simulation tool CST microwave studio (CST-MWS). The simulated results obtained using the Eigenmode solver of the CST is compared with the numerically computed characteristics. For the PTH-SWS considered, the performance metrices such as the phase velocity, dispersion characteristics, and intrinsic impedances are simulated. The outcome of the present study exhibits results of rectangular straight edge type PTH for use in millimeter-wave frequency ranges. The results of this work will lead to the development of millimeter-wave PTH SWS that can be fabricated.

articleTitle: Study of W-band High Efficient Extended Interaction Devices
abstract: A high power Extended Interaction Oscillator (EIO) operating at 95GHz is designed and simulated using CST software. The cold-test simulation results show that the stable <tex>$\mathbf{TM}\mathbf{11}-\mathbf{2}\Pi$</tex> operating mode is achieved at 94.73GHz. Q and R/Q value are optimized by modifying the size of the resonant cavity and observing the characteristics of the high frequency structure. Furthermore, the conductor losses are considered to make the size shorter and enhance the output power and gain in the terahertz band. The 3D-PIC simulation are performed by applying high beam voltage of 51.5kV and permanent magnetic field of 01.3T. The PIC predicts the continuous wave output power of extended interactive oscillator tube at 95Ghz is 7.08kW.

articleTitle: The Design and Performance of an X-band Broadband Klystron With Peak Power of 1MW
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement results of an X-band broadband klystron with a peak power of 1MW developed at Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Science (AIRCAS). In the development of this klystron, the single electron beam with an electromagnetic focusing system was adopted to achieve a high beam transmission rate. Meanwhile, a filter-loaded over-lapping mode double gap coupling cavities output circuit (OMDGOC) and a pill-box output window were used to ensure the klystron has an operating bandwidth of 650MHz. The 1# klystron was tested under a 1 % duty ratio at 27 operating frequency points. The technical specifications of this klystron are as follows: peak power: over 1MW, efficiency: over 24.3 %, gain: over 37.1dB, beam transmission rate: over 96%, which meet the design requirements.

Author Keywords: over-lapping mode double gap coupling cavities

articleTitle: Uniform Electron Emission from $\text{SiO}_{\mathrm{X}}$ Tunneling Diode Arrays under Rough Vacuum
abstract: Uniform electron emission (EE) under rough vacuum of <tex>$\sim 10^{-2}$</tex> Pa from on-chip micro-emitter arrays based on <tex>$\text{SiO}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> tunneling diodes (STDs) in electroformed <tex>$\text{SiO}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> is reported. Here, we provide a unique means to visually resolve the spatial distribution of EE from STD arrays and emitter-to-emitter uniformity at the microscale resolution via accompanied light emission. Benefiting from good emitter-to-emitter uniformity and low pressure sensitivity of EE from STD arrays, improved emission performances is obtained.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis and Model Design of a Sub-Terahertz Band Rectangular TE10to TE30 Mode Converter
abstract: In this paper, a novel waveguide structure for converting rectangular TE<inf>10</inf> mode to <tex>$\text{TE}_{30}$</tex> mode is presented. The mode converter mainly compromises an H-plane T - junction power divider and a mode exciting structure based on two coupling apertures. The theoretical analysis of the magnetic current sources is carried out to study the mode converting structure. Two types of mode converters with different feeding structures are presented for different application occasions. Simulation results show that they both have a bandwidth of at least 41 GHz, in which the transmission is higher than -1 dB and the reflection is lower than -15 dB.

articleTitle: Frequency Multiplication in Relativistic Gyrotrons for Providing High-Power Submillimeter Radiation
abstract: In order to provide high-power radiation in the submillimeter wavelength range, it is proposed to use the effect of frequency multiplication in high-current relativistic gyrotrons. As is known, as the energy of rotating electrons increases to relativistic values, the maximum of the electronwave coupling coefficients shifts towards higher cyclotron harmonics. We demonstrate that by multiplying the frequencies by a factor of three in a gyrotron with an operating frequency of 100 GHz and an electron beam with a moderately relativistic energy (500 keV),it is possible to achieve a megawatt power level in the 300 GHz band. The results were obtained in numerical simulation both within the framework of the averaged equations of the electron-wave interaction and when using the particle-in-cell code.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized kW-Level Metamaterial-Inspired Extended Interaction Klystron at 650 MHz
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized kW-level meta material-inspired extended interaction klystron (EIK) at 650 MHz is proposed. The meta material-loaded extended interaction resonant cavity (EIRC) has the advantages of both miniaturization and high characteristic impedance due to the subwavelength characteristics of the metamaterial unit cell and the multi-gap cavity. An metamaterial-inspired EIK is studied based on the proposed metamaterial-loaded EIRC. The beam-wave interaction simulations show that the proposed EIK is capable of producing 650 kW of power output at 650 MHz with the beam voltage of 81.5 kV and beam current of 15.1 A, corresponding to an electronic efficiency of 52.8% and a gain of 35 dB. The volume of the interaction structure is only 0.25 of the conventional counterparts, which is expected to be applied in large-scale scientific facilities such as electron-positron collider and synchrotron radiation light source.

articleTitle: Research on the Length Design of Three-section Cylindrical Waveguide Resonator
abstract: The resonator is the place where the beam wave interaction occurs in the gyrotron. For the gyrotron with a three-section cylindrical waveguide resonator, the length of each section has different effects on the resonant frequency, quality factor, field distribution, etc. of the resonator. In this paper, the length design of the input section, output section, input transition section, output transition section and interaction section of the three-section cylindrical waveguide resonator working in 140GHz, TE28,8 mode is studied, and the influence of the length of each section on the performance of the resonator is analyzed, thus one reasonable length design of each section is given.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Study of the W-band TWT with Four-port Structure
abstract: The power of a conventional folded waveguide (FWG) traveling wave tube (TWT) at the sever region can't be measured, so relevant research is needed. In this paper, a W-band TWT with four-port structure is proposed and fabricated. Based on the output power and S-parameters of four ports, the power at the TWT sever region is analyzed and verified. The results show that estimated power was in an excellent agreement with the measured data, which provide a practical and effective method for improving stability and reliability of a millimeter wave TWT.

articleTitle: Study of a 0.67 THz TWT Based on Slotted Quasi Sine Waveguide
abstract: A 670 GHz slotted quasi sine waveguide (S-QSWG) slow wave structure (SWS) has been designed and simulated in this article. The high frequency characteristics, transmission characteristic and beam-wave interaction are simulated by CST STUDIO SUITE software. A two-section circuit is proposed and the cold simulation result shows the reflection loss is less than -15 dB in the frequency range of 658–698 GHz. Results of beam-wave interaction demonstrates the circuit can produce maximum output power of 1.9 W at 670 GHz with operating voltage of 24.1 kV, operating current of 17 mA and input power of 3 mW, the corresponding maximum gain at 670 GHz is 28 dB.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Compact S-band Coaxial Multi-beam Relativistic Klystron Amplifier with Modular Periodic Permanent Magnet
abstract: A compact modular periodic permanent magnet system (MPPM) with a combination of inner and outer magnetic blocks and soft magnets is proposed in this paper. Its weight and maximum guided magnetic field strength is 50 kg and 0.3 T respectively. Compared with the uniform permanent magnet system, its weight is only about 1/10. Besides, we have simulated a coaxial multi-beam relativistic klystron amplifier (CMB-RKA) with the MPPM. The output microwave power of CMB-RKA with MPPM and the uniform ideal magnetic field is 0.78 GW and 0.84 GW respectively when the beam voltage and current are 525 kV and 4.62 kA. This demonstrated that a CMBRKA using MPPM is achievable. These results provide a new technical route for lightweight and small relativistic klystron amplifiers.

articleTitle: A review on recent progress of high-temperature direct-heated cathode
abstract: As the performance of the vacuum electron devices largely depends on the properties of their cathodes, developing efficient and durable thermionic cathode is necessary and highly desired to meet the boosting requirements of the vacuum electron devices. This paper mainly describes the research progress in W-Re base direct-heated cathodes used in high-power continuous wave magnetrons, which include the <tex>$\boldsymbol{Sc_{2}O_{3}}$</tex> doped Y-Gd-Hf-O pressed series cathodes and the <tex>$La_{2}Hf_{2}O_{7}$</tex> cathode. The current density of the pressed Y-Gd-Hf-O cathode can remain to 87.5% of the initial one after continuous electron bombardment for 480 <tex>$\boldsymbol{h}$</tex>, and the best emission ability of 2.79 <tex>$A/cm^{2}$</tex> has reached with the 5/2 molar ratio of the <tex>$\boldsymbol{Y_{2}O_{3}/HfO_{2}}$</tex> at <tex>$1500^{\circ}C$</tex>. The lifetime of the <tex>$\boldsymbol{L_{2}Hf_{2}O_{7}}$</tex> cathode is beyond 10000 <tex>$\boldsymbol{h}$</tex> at <tex>$155\theta{\ }^{\circ}C$</tex> with the loading of 0.65 <tex>$A/cm^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of a 36-Vane 2.5MW X-Band Coaxial Magnetron Interaction Cavity
abstract: In this paper, a 36-vane 2.5 MW X-band coaxial magnetron is studied by the empirical formulas calculation and PIC simulation methods. Based on the initial structural parameters obtained by empirical calculation, the coaxial magnetron interaction resonant cavity structure is optimized by PIC simulation method, and the results show that the output power, work frequency are ~2.65MW@9.3GHz, which match the design goals.

articleTitle: Study on Ballistic Transport Electronics—A Vacuum Field Emission Transistor with Carbon Nanotube Cold Cathode
abstract: Vacuum field emission transistors (VFETs) are emerging as promising alternatives to solid state electronic devices under high frequency environments. Here, we propose a VFET with back gate and carbon nanotube (CNT) arrays as cathode. The output characteristics, transfer characteristics and field emission properties of VFET are obtained by particle trajectory simulation method. The simulation results show that CNT arrays achieve high field enhanced factors, and the field emission current is increased by reducing the field shielding effect. The device has 33 nS transconductance at 8 V anode voltage, which shows fast signal response and low operating voltage. Moreover, VFET based on CNT arrays can change the numbers of CNT emitters to control the properties of the devices and even achieving high power gain. Ulteriorly, considering the ballistic transport in nanogap, these devices are expected to realize power amplify applications in high frequency regime.

articleTitle: Final Version-Orbital Performance of L-band TWTA for BeiDou Navigation Satellites
abstract: This paper describes the on-orbit performance of downlink amplifiers (L-band TWTA) for Beidou Navigation Satellites. The integrator of TWTA is CAST Xi’ an, and the suppliers of TWT include AIRCAS, BVERI,and NanJing SanLe Group Co. Ltd. It Is very interesting to compare the variation of the helix current and anode voltage, and it is useful to predict the range of the helix current and anode voltage during the orbital life(ten to twelve years).

articleTitle: Introduction of recent research on Relativistic Magnetron at IAE
abstract: Relativistic magnetron (RM) is well known as a high efficiency, compact, tunable and robust high-power microwave source. It is expected to have applications in various fields such as pulsed radar, plasma heating, and particle acceleration. Institute of Applied Electronics (IAE) has investigated RM for several years including RM with diffraction output (MDO), RM with all cavity axial extraction(ACAE), multi-antenna extraction (MAE) RM, rectangular vane-type eight-cavity (R8) MDO and axial tuning RM. The performance of RM advances significantly in high efficiency, minimization, light weight, and wide band tuning in IAE. Microwave power of more than 2 GW had been radiated at L-band by both MDO and ACAE RM with inducing magnetic field of less than 0.4 T, corresponding to an efficiency of more than 30%. Microwave power of 1 GW had been radiated at S-band by R8 MDO with inducing magnetic field of less than 0.5 T, corresponding to an efficiency of more than 50%. For long term operation of RM, MDO had achieve sequent radiation for about an hour in 10 Hz repetitive rate. For permanent magnet packaged ACAE RM whose whole weight is only about 94kg, microwave power of more than 1.5GW have been detected with repetitive rate of 30Hz. For tunable RM, axial tuning RM with high efficiency had been presented including axial tuning MAE and ACAE RM. Tuning range of more than 30% had been realized for both of these two types of tubes in gigawatt level power.

articleTitle: Design of Ka-Band Single-Anode Magnetron Injection Gun with Low Velocity Spread
abstract: The velocity spread of electron beam is an important parameter of electron gun. In order to obtain high quality electron beam, a single-anode magnetron injection gun(MIG) with low velocity spread is designed in this paper. The MIG works in the Ka-band, with the beam voltage of 60kV, beam current of 10A, and transverse to longitudinal velocity ratio of 1.2. And it can provide a electron beam with a transverse velocity spread of 1.6%.

articleTitle: Study on Mutual Coupling of Two Magnetrons for Multi-Source Heating System
abstract: Industrial equipment mostly uses multi-source heating, but multi-source heating system has the problem of mutual coupling, which affects the efficiency. The mutual coupling of two magnetrons for multi-source heating system is studied in this paper. With different lengths of water load, a magnetron with a stable output spectrum is used to influence a magnetron of which the performance of the output spectrum and phase noise is poor. The experimental results show that the output frequency of the magnetron with unstable output spectrum can be trapped to the center frequency of the other one. The phase noise of the output signal is greatly reduced and injected locking is achieved.

articleTitle: Study on the Efficiency of Two-Beam Extended Interaction Oscillator toward 200 kW at Ka-band
abstract: A compact high-efficiency two-beam extended interaction oscillator (EIO) with an improved ladder structure is proposed to achieve a high output power of 200 kW. The Ka-band continuous wave two-beam EIO with five gaps is designed to operate in the <tex>$\mathbf{TM}\mathbf{31}-\mathbf{2}\boldsymbol{\pi}$</tex> mode. The effects of the external quality factor <tex>$(\mathbf{Q}_{\mathbf{e}})$</tex>, perveance <tex>$(\mathbf{P}_{\mathbf{t}})$</tex> and phase velocity changes in the last period on the efficiency improvement of the EIO are analyzed. The efficiency improvement from 28 % to 41 % is predicted by the 3-D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations performed in CST. A stable output power of 205 kW and 41% efficiency are obtained at 52 kV and <tex>$\mathbf{4.8}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> A. An effective method for dramatically increasing the efficiency of millimetre-wave EIOs is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Consistency Control of The Ka-Band Switching Tube Resonant Window
abstract: In this paper, the resonance window consistency of Ka-band switching tube is investigated. The Ka-band switching tube resonance window was successfully prepared by using screen printing technology to coat the metallized layer of small size sapphire window, and by controlling the surface state and thickness uniformity of the solder layer of the resonance window. the resonant frequency is located at 34.72-35.26 GHz, <tex>$\Delta\ \mathbf{f} < \mathbf{600}\ \mathbf{MHz}$</tex>, the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) is between 1.20-1.40, and the consistency is good. This study provides a basis for the research and development of higher frequency switching tube resonant Windows.

articleTitle: Sub-THz CW Clinotron Cavity Design
abstract: The results of the research and development of the interaction cavity of sub-THz clinotrons together with the experimental tests several modifications of the tubes are presented and discussed. The surface wave resonator scheme is used to describe the mechanical frequency tuning in the millimeter-wave clinotron tubes by using the plunger while the resonances in the THz range are described by the transformations and reflections of bulk and surface waves. Explanations of the advantages of the modification of the sub-THz clinotron based on the hybrid bulk-surface modes have been provided.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis of Radius Changing Coaxial Waveguide
abstract: Coaxial waveguide is a common microwave device which is used to transmit electromagnetic waves widely. In this paper, the relationship between the cutoff wavenumber of TM mode of coaxial waveguide and the radius changing is analyzed. We found that when the <tex>$\Delta \mathbf{R}/\mathbf{a}$</tex> is less than 1/10, the cut-off wavenumber of TM wave will become stable gradually, Which means if we keep the <tex>$\Delta \mathbf{R}$</tex> stable and increase radius, the power capacity will increase steeply while the cut-off wavenumber will keep stable. Besides, the S-parameters studies indicate that this radius changing coaxial waveguide can only couple out TM mode, and the transmission effective of TE mode is pretty low. It means we can get pure TM and TEM mode.

articleTitle: Design and Cold Test of a Mode-Suppression Circuit for the G-Band Gyro-TWT
abstract: In this paper, the design and measurement of a mode-suppression circuit used in the nonlinear interaction region for a G-band gyrotron travelling wave tube (gyro-TWT) are presented. By achieving sufficient coupling losses, this circuit can effectively suppress the parasitic oscillations without affecting the operating mode, thus improving the tube stability during high power operation. The measured results agree well with the simulated results, which can provide a loss of 5.6 dB/cm to suppress the backward-wave oscillation (BWO) of the TE21 mode. This proves that the circuit can be used as a new scheme for gyro- TWTs to achieve high stability and high power.

articleTitle: A Wideband 340GHz Backward Wave Oscillator with Sine-Shaped Ridge Waveguide Slow Wave Structure
abstract: This paper pertinently investigates the Backward wave oscillator (BWO) based upon a novel sine-shaped ridge waveguide (SSRWG) slow wave structure (SWS) which works in the frequency range of 300-350GHz. The dispersion characteristics and interaction impedance of SSRWG and normal sine waveguide (SWG) are compared. The results show that SSRWG has a wider bandwidth at the same size and a higher interaction impedance at the same phase velocity than those of SWG. The beam-wave interaction is then simulated by CST Particle Studio. The results show that this BWO loaded by pencil electron can produce more than 2.5W output power in 300-350GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Oscillation Threshold in the Recirculating Planar Crossed-Field Amplifier
abstract: The transition from amplifier to oscillator of the Recirculating Planar Crossed-Field Amplifier (RPCFA) is examined in simulation and experiment. Initially, the RPCFA is zero-drive stable and operates as a high power amplifier with an input signal. By changing the anode-cathode gap, the RPCFA can exhibit oscillations. We explore the cold-tube and beam-loaded device characteristics that cause the transition to oscillation.

articleTitle: A High-power, Broadband Gas-filled Microwave Switching Tube in Millimeter-wave Band
abstract: This paper introduces a high-power broadband gas-filled microwave switching tube (TR tube) based on WR28 waveguide in Ka-band. This tube adopts the structure of ceramic-metal composite resonant sealing windows and three-stage discharge gaps, filling with argon, water vapor and other mixed gases. Through simulation and optimization using CST, as well as actual production verification, the bandwidth of the tube achieves 8GHz (relative bandwidth > 22%), the total insertion loss < 1.2dB, and when the input power is greater than or equal to 400W, the peak leakage power < 1.6W, the flat leakage power < 30mW, and the recovery time < 400ns. This product can be used not only for the protection of the receiver during radar transmission, but also for the protection of the receiver from external high-power electromagnetic pulse attacks.

articleTitle: Continuous disinfection and sterilization system based on ultra-strong ultraviolet electrodeless lamp
abstract: Microwave driven electrodeless ultraviolet lamps are widely used in industrial and medical fields. However, the ultraviolet intensity of traditional ultraviolet lamps is uneven, and the service life of ultraviolet lamps is not long. In this paper, a new type of electrodeless ultraviolet lamp driven by microwave is proposed, which greatly improves the ultraviolet irradiance and can realize high-efficiency disinfection and sterilization. Based on the electromagnetic theory and Drude model, the electromagnetic simulation of the reaction chamber was carried out, and the experimental device was successfully built. The influence of internal fillers and other factors on the ultraviolet irradiation intensity was discussed through experiments.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional parallel particle simulation software based on the Linux system
abstract: On the Milky Way High Performance Computing Platform of National University of Defense Science and Technology<inf>[1]</inf>, the core computing module of particle simulation based on LINUX system is designed using FDTD(Finite-different Time-domain) and PIC(Particle-in-cell) algorlthms<inf>[2]</inf>; MPI(Message Passing Interface) standard is adopted to complete the design of large-scale parallel algorithm module based on LINUX system, forming a 3D parallel particle simulation software that can adapt to high-performance computing platform. Finally, a large-scale simulation of TWT(Traveling Wave Tube) and RKA(klystron) is carried out on the Milky Way high performance platform using the software, and the simulation results are credible and the acceleration ratio is more than 30.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of an L-band Ferrite Waveguide Circulator for Industrial Applications
abstract: Commercial L-band circulator (WR975) at <tex>$\mathbf{896}\pm \mathbf{10}\ \ \mathbf{MHz}$</tex> is available on markets. However, for a wider bandwidth (~ 30 MHz) application, we would need two units operated in dual frequencies between 896 MHz and 915 MHz to cover the frequency range required. A Finite Element Method (FEM) simulation study found that a broader bandwidth can be achieved by reducing the height of the waveguide circulator in half. This also leads to a reduction in overall fabrication cost. This paper discusses a detailed design and modelling of the L-band circulator operating at 915 MHz with a wide bandwidth of 55 MHz (895MZ to 950 MHz), an insertion loss of 0.195 dB for the entire bandwidth, and 0.173 dB at 915 MHz for a uniform applied bias field. The average transmission efficiency within the bandwidth is > 95.59% in the operating region, which reduces power reflections for improving the performance and reliability of magnetrons. This paper also discusses a realist magnetic circuit design for the proposed model to simulate a non-uniform applied bias for more accurate simulation results.

articleTitle: Electron-Beam Gate-Controlled Field-Effect Transistor
abstract: Innovative devices based on metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) have greatly promoted the development of science and technology. It is of great scientific significance and practical value to explore the new device and new control mechanism based on FET. In this paper, a novel electron-beam gate-controlled FET (E-FET) based on <tex>$\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{Si}$</tex> structure is proposed and verified by establishing the device model, simulating the device characteristic, and testing the device response. The results show that both the incident energy and the irradiation dose of electron-beam can control the switch and the channel current of E-FET, which could be used to monitor the potential and control the switch of spraying charged particles in the application of electrostatic discharge (ESD) active protection. Therefore, this work provides a new design of the FET controlled by the electron-beam induced charge accumulation that could be used as the monitoring of charge accumulation and the switch of spraying charged particles in ESD active protection for the vacuum electronics of spacecraft.

articleTitle: High-power terahertz source and transmission line for 400MHz DNP NMR system
abstract: A 263GHz frequency-tunable gyrotron is investigated experimentally, its frequency-tuning range is about 1.45GHz and the output power is from 26 W to 463 W when the operating magnetic field changes at a fixed operating voltage of 20 kV and a beam current of 0.8 A. The operating mode TE<inf>72</inf>mode is converted into a linearly gaussian beam efficiently with a Valsov-type quasi-optical mode converter. At the same time, the Gaussian beam is transmitted and focused with a low loss overmoded corrugated waveguides and quasi-optical units. The preliminary experiment on enhanced DNP-NMR system is carried out with the gyrotron and the transmission line.

articleTitle: Thermionic Emission Mechanism of a Novel Y2Hf2O7Ceramic Cathode Applied in High-Power Magnetron Tubes of Medical Linear Accelerator
abstract: In order to enhance output power and prolong lifetime of the high-power magnetron tubes of medical linear accelerator, a novel Y<inf>2</inf>Hf<inf>2</inf>O<inf>7</inf> Ceramic cathode had been developed. The thermionic emission characteristics of the Y<inf>2</inf>Hf<inf>2</inf>O<inf>7</inf> cathode had been measured. The experimental results show that the cathode can provide 3.5A/cm<sup>2</sup> current density for the space charge limitation at 1600 °C br under 300V anode voltage. At last, the thermionic emission mechanism of the Y<inf>2</inf>Hf<inf>2</inf>O<inf>7</inf> ceramic cathode had been researched by SEM, EDS and AES Analysis. The generation of the n-type semiconductor Y<inf>2</inf>Hf<inf>2</inf>O<inf>(7-X)</inf> is the reason which improved the emission property of the ceramic cathode.

articleTitle: Powerful Long-Pulse FEL based on Linac LIU: Simulations and Optimization of Parameters for Initial Experiments at 0.3 THz Range
abstract: Project of sub-THz/THz band FEL driven by induction linac LIU is under development in collaboration between BINP RAS (Novosibirsk) and IAP RAS (N.Novgorod) and aimed to achieve sub-GW power and a record pulse energy content of ~ 10 -100 J in these frequency band. Two alternative electrodynamic systems were proposed for this FEL to provide stable narrow-band generation regime: (1) advanced Bragg resonators with quasi-cutoff feedback waves and (2) quasi-optical resonators of the Talbot-type. Present paper is devoted to the results of simulations and optimization of parameters of the FEL with such resonators for conducting initial experiments at the 0.3 THz range.

articleTitle: Project of Pulsed Undulator with Millimeter Period for THz and X-ray Sources
abstract: In this paper, we propose and study a variant of a pulsed micro-undulator based on thin conducting plates with cuts. It seems that such a design should have sufficient mechanical rigidity and resistance to overheating. In the report, the parame-ters of the micro-undulator necessary for the generation of THz-and X-rays are discussed, and the design, analytical description and numerical simulation of the proposed system are considered.

articleTitle: Study on Multiphysical Fields of S-band Multi-beam Klystron Electron Gun
abstract: In this paper, the development of an electron gun for an S-band compact high-power multi beam klystron is introduced. The total number of electron beams is 18, and the working voltage is 16 kV with the 25 A average total current distributed on the 18 electron beams. The electron beam is confined by a wire-wrapped focusing system, and the magnetic field is 0.129 T in the uniform magnetic field region. The magnetic field distribution and focusing trajectory are studied by using the three-dimensional structure calculation software, and the pass rate of multi-beam electron gun is 100%. In addition, the heat distribution was obtained by thermal analysis of the electron gun structure. The heat is mainly concentrated near the heat source. The maximum temperature of the structure is 1232.5 (K), and the ambient temperature gradually decreased to 315.09 (K).

articleTitle: Study of a G-band Magnetron Injection Gun with High Transportation Stability
abstract: Beam transportation stability is important to the stable operation of gyro-traveling-wave tube (gyro-Twt).The transportation performance of TE01 mode magnetron injection gun (MIG) is unsatisfactory, so a <tex>$\mathbf{TE}_{13}$</tex> mode MIG with high transportation stability is designed in this paper. Its velocity ratio and transverse velocity spread are 1.15 and 0.58%, respectively. Then the influence of stray electrons and magnetic field misalignment is analyzed in detail. Considering both stray electrons and misalignment, the gap between beam and interaction waveguide wall is 0.61 mm, and the velocity spread of emitter strip beam is 0.99%.

articleTitle: Research on Efficient Testing of W-band High-power Sheet Beam Extended Interaction Oscillator
abstract: The sheet beam extended interaction oscillator (SBEIO) is one of the miniaturized vacuum electronic devices that can provide high power output in millimeter wave and terahertz bands. In this paper, an experimental study of a high-power W-band SBEIO is carried out. According to its characteristics of high power and miniaturization, an experimental test scheme with adjustable mode and controllable stages was designed, and the WSBEIO was successfully operated in the 95 GHz frequency band with an average power of 2.05 kW for more than 1 hour, which verifies the reliability of the system and the high efficiency of the test strategy.

articleTitle: Design and experimental study on a 263 GHz frequency-tunable gyrotron
abstract: A 263 GHz frequency-tunable gyrotron has been designed and experimental studied. The gyrotron resonator is traditional three-section cavity. The operating frequency and the output power with respect to the operating voltage, operating magnetic field and the beam current are investigated experimentally. It is found that the operating frequency changes from 263.39 GHz to 264.84 GHz and the frequency-tuning range is about 1.45 GHz, the variation of the output power is from 26 W to 463 W when the operating voltage is fixed at 20 kV and the beam current is fixed at 0.8 A but the operating magnetic field changes from 9.59 T to 9.82 T. When the operating voltage increases from 14.4 kV to 22.2 kV at a fixed operating magnetic field of 9.65 T, the operating frequency decreases from 263.68 GHz to 263.40 GHz and the and the frequency-tuning range is 0.28 GHz. Meanwhile, the output power is changed from 52 W to 424 W. When the beam current increases from 120 mA to 880 mA but the operating magnetic field is fixed at 9.65 T and the operating voltage is fixed at 20 kV, the output power increases from 21 W to 277 W and the operating frequency increases from 263.396 GHz to 263.425 GHz, the frequency-tunable range is 0.029 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Ku-band Traveling-Wave Tube Based on Optimization Design Tool
abstract: In this paper, the pitch profile of a traveling-wave tube (TWT) at Ku-band is designed by using the multiobjective optimization design tool. The simulation indicators of the TWT require that the output power reaches 220W (the electronic efficiency reaches 39%) and the power variation is less than 5W over the operating band. The phase distortion should be less than 45 degrees at the same time. By using the optimization design tool, the optimized solutions achieve all the design objectives through eight hours of automatic optimization. Then, the final design scheme is obtained by selecting the scheme with lower power variation.

articleTitle: Development of Ka-Band 300W CW Helix TWT
abstract: This paper introduced development of a Ka-Band 300W helix TWT for satellite communications systems, which is fulfilled at Beijing Vacuum Electronics Research Institute. Measurements show that the TWT is capable to deliver output power of more than 300W with a overall efficiency of 30% among the frequency of 30-38GHz. The maximum dimensions of the TWT were <tex>$330\text{mm}(\mathrm{L})\times 67\text{mm}(\mathrm{W})\times 60\text{mm}(\mathrm{H})$</tex> with a weight of 3.0kg(typical).

articleTitle: Low-Power Field Emission Arrays with Sharp Emitters
abstract: Fabrication and characterization of high-density silicon field emitter arrays with dull and sharp tips are presented using high-throughput electron-beam lithography. Both arrays achieved a maximum current density of 4.5 A.cm<sup>−2</sup>. The array with sharp tips had a turn-on voltage of 45 V while the one with dull emitters had a turn-on voltage of 108 V. The required voltage to achieve a 4 <tex>$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex> emission current for the sharp emitter array was 120 V, less than half of the required voltage for the array with dull emitters. The field enhancement factors for the arrays with dull and sharp emitters are calculated as 92 and 267, respectively.

articleTitle: Resistant To Ion Bombardment Field Emitters Of A New Type And Features Of Electron Flows Formed By Electron-Optical Systems With Such Emitters
abstract: The article reports on the results of a study of new type multi-tip and multi-layer field emitters that are promising for use in subterahertz spectroscopic gyrotrons, as well as on the specific features of electron flows formed by electron-optical systems with such emitters.

articleTitle: High Mode Purity TE01 Input Coupler for Ka-band Gyro-TWT
abstract: A study of a high mode purity TE<inf>01</inf> input coupler for Ka-band gyrotron traveling wave tubes (gyro-Twt) has been presented. The input coupler has two T-type power-deviding sections. It can obtain high purity TE<inf>01</inf> cylindrical waveguide mode which is converted from TE<inf>01</inf> rectangular waveguide mode. On the basis of theoretical calculation, the main structural parameters were optimized by high frequency simulation software. Simulations predicts that the transmission of TE<inf>01</inf> mode was over −1.5dB from 32GHz to 37GHz and the transmission of other modes of competition was less than −30dB.

articleTitle: Research on a terahertz transmission line used for solid-state 400MHz DNP-NMR spectrometer
abstract: In this paper, transmission characteristics of a terahertz transmission line used for solid-state 400 MHz dynamic nuclear polarization enhanced nuclear magnetic resonance (DNP-NMR) spectrometer are presented. The result shows that the transmission system can achieve stable and efficient transmission at a distance of about 3 m.

articleTitle: A Sheet Beam Electron Gun Using Thermal Emission with Large Beam Current for 0.22 THz Traveling-Wave Tubes
abstract: In this paper, a sheet beam electron gun with large beam current based on thermal emission mechanism is designed and simulated for developing 0.22 THz traveling-wave tubes (TWTs). A pencil beam of the electron gun can be compressed into a sheet beam by utilizing a novel focusing electrode. The CST simulation results show that the beam current of the sheet beam electron gun is 137.9 mA at beam voltage 24.6 kV, and the emission beam current density is <tex>$27.45 \mathbf{A}/\mathbf{cm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>. The distance between the beam waist position and the cathode emission surface is ~12 mm, and the size of sheet beam waist is <tex>$\mathbf{0.42}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{0.06} \mathbf{mm}$</tex>. In addition, the sensitivity analysis for the sheet beam electron gun is investigated. The research work reported here lays a foundation for the development of 0.22 THz TWTs.
