articleTitle: A suspended micro-bridge structure nano-air-channel triode with a deformable anode
abstract: In this paper, a suspended micro-bridge structure nano-air-channel triode with a deformable anode is proposed. The triode removes the insulating dielectric used for inter-electrode supporting in conventional vertical structure nanoscale air-channel devices, in order to improve the effective emission area of the cathode and reduce the capacitance, as well as avoiding the influence of the dielectric on the performance of the triode. In addition, the anode deformation can be modulated to change the length of the nanoscale air-channel by adjusting the bias voltage, which contributes to an enhancement of the cathode electric field strength and a stronger emission current density.

articleTitle: Bioimaging experiment based on terahertz near-field scanning system
abstract: Terahertz near-field scanning system uses high-power vacuum electron device as power output source, combined with nano-scale probe, has measurement accuracy of tens of nanometers imaging effect. Combined with the characteristics of terahertz penetration, the inner and surface of the sample can be imaged at the same time. In this paper, terahertz near-field scanning system is used to image human sperm in the field of biological samples. The shape, acrosome, nucleus and tail of human sperm are imaged on the surface or inside. The problems needing attention during the experiment are discussed. Finally, the significance of imaging experiment to biological research is prospected.

articleTitle: Hot Electron Light Assisted Cathode by Electronically Tunable Negative Electron Affinity
abstract: Currently, negative electron affinity cathodes are considered as a potential high frequency photoemitters due to their relatively high external quantum efficiency and low mean transverse energies, however, they face challenges in terms of stability and complexity in their manufacturing process. In this research, we have developed an electronically adjustable cathode called Hot Electron Laser Assisted Cathode (HELAC) which uses negative electron surfaces and is fabricated using a simple and ex-situ technique. Despite not being fully optimized, the proof-of-concept device has demonstrated great air stability and an external quantum efficiency of around 0.5%. This work can give an idea of the possibilities and difficulties of designing new photocathodes with high quantum efficiency by using the negative electron affinity technique.

articleTitle: A Novel Rectangular Groove Sine Waveguide TWT Operating at 0.34 THz
abstract: A novel slow-wave structure (SWS) named rectangular groove sine waveguide (RGSWG) is proposed for traveling-wave tube (TWT) operating at 0.34 THz in this article. The novel RGSWG is derived from the conventional SWG SWS which has the advantages of low loss, natural sheet beam tunnel and easy fabrication. RGSWG SWS has higher interaction impedance than conventional SWG SWS under the condition of consistent normalized phase velocity. The slow-wave characteristics of RGSWG and beam-wave interaction results of RGSWG TWT have been investigated. In the frequency range of 0.332 - 0.36 THz, the output power is greater than 5 W, and the maximum output power is 10 W at 0.344 THz.

articleTitle: Optimization of 340GHz EIK high-frequency Structure
abstract: In this paper, the high-frequency structure of the EIK is optimized, and the input and output ports are optimized according to the S-parameters to make the ports meet the application requirements. Furthermore, the conductor losses are considered to make the size shorter and enhance the output power and gain in the terahertz band. The particle simulation results show that the continuous wave output power of the extended interactive klystron tube at 339.85 GHz is 151.38W with a corresponding gain of 38.79dB and an electronic efficiency of 3.18% at an operating voltage of 19kV. The applied magnetic field and the beam current is set to 0.69 T, and 0.25 A respectively.

articleTitle: X-Band High-Gain Wide-Angle Beam Scanning Phased Array-Fed Reflector Antenna
abstract: Phased array-fed reflector (PAFR) antennas combine the advantages of high gain and low cost of reflector antenna and the flexibility of phased array antenna beam scanning. A novel X-band PAFR antenna has been designed using seven discrete small parabolic reflectors instead of the parabolic torus, and the array feeder consists of eight resonant series-fed patch arrays. Compared with the traditional design, the proposed novel PAFR antenna has a higher gain, which increases from 27.16dBi to 32.48dBi at <tex>$0^{\circ}$</tex> and from 23.57dBi to 29.48dBi at <tex>$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex>. And the gain was improved by an average of 5.60dB between <tex>$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> without changing the size of reflector and the wide-angle beam scanning. Simulation results confirmed the potential of this antenna for the future wireless systems.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Technological Gyrotron System with Magnetically Shielded Solenoid
abstract: In this report, we present the first results of testing a new technological gyrotron at the first cyclotron harmonic with a radiation frequency of 28 GHz and a power of over 20 kW. The generation efficiency reaches 55% at a power level of 6 kW without a system for recuperating the residual electron energy. The efficiency of the entire installation is above 35% in the mode of maximum radiation power, which is achieved by using a magnetically shielded oil-cooled solenoid. The results obtained confirm the operability of the developed electron-optical system under conditions of a sharp drop in the magnetic field of the main solenoid outside the magnet bore. Experimental data are consistent with the results of numerical simulation. This is to hope for the implementation of generators up to the W frequency band using the same magnetic system and high-voltage power supplies.

articleTitle: A 5.0 MW, 805 MHz, Long Pulsed Klystron for Spallation Neutron Source at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory
abstract: The 5 MW, 805 MHz L-band long pulse klystron E37506 is developed for the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). The 1<sup>st</sup> prototype is operating at ORNL. The 2<sup>nd</sup> prototype E37506 is brushed up and is currently undergoing assembly at Canon Electron Tube & Devices (CETD). This paper provides overview of the E37506 design results.

articleTitle: A MEMS-Type Hot-cathode Ionization Gauge With Carbon Nanotube-based Electron Emitters
abstract: Traditional hot-cathode ionization gauge usually suffers from bulky size, fragile glass enclosure, integration difficulties and etc. Here, an ionization vacuum gauge is scaled down to nail size based on vertical integration of a microminiaturized hot-cathode and multilayer gate electrodes on a single chip. Besides the merit of miniaturization, exploiting carbon nanotube as microscopic filament also brings the cathode endurance to rough vacuum and anti-poisoning property. Thus vacuum packaging is excluded, improving the robustness of the device. The ionization gauge demonstrates high and reliable tunability and shows good measurement linearity from <tex>$2\times 10^{-2}$</tex> to 4 Pa. All above advantages over bulky thermionic counterparts make it promising in future vacuum measurements.

articleTitle: Research on Thickness Measurement Technology Based on FMCW Radar
abstract: With the rapid development of microwave and millimeter wave solid-state devices and digital signal processors, Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave (FMCW) radar has been widely used in various fields. This paper studies the thickness measurement technology of FMCW, and a FMCW radar front-end working in C-band was designed and implemented. To improve the precision for thickness measurement, a Chirp-Z transform (CZT) algorithm is applied in this paper. Finally, a FMCW radar with a center frequency of 5.8 GHz and a bandwidth of 1 GHz were established, and thickness measurement experiments were carried out. The experimental results demonstrate that the FMCW radar can obtain the sample thickness with low error.

articleTitle: Calculation of coil magnetic field by finite element method in MFS
abstract: The coil current creates a magnetic field in free space. At present, the coil magnetic field calculation method used by MFS (magnetic focusing simulator) is an analytical method to solve the magnetic field distribution of spatial static coil based on Biot-Saval law. This method has high accuracy, but disagrees with the subject method finite element method used by MFS. In order to facilitate the subsequent simulation function of new vortex field in MFS and the consistency of MFS code, in this paper, the finite element calculation method of 3D coil magnetic field is derived, and the results are compared with Maxwell, and the consistency is high.

articleTitle: Preparation of Miniature Thermionic Cathode to be Used in THz Devices
abstract: A kind of miniature thermionic cathode is prepared by depositing an anti-emission Ta-Zr composite coating on impregnated scandate cathode surface via dual Ion-Beam-Assisted Deposition (Dual IBAD) and then etching in the center of the anti-emission coating a mini electron emission zone with a diameter of <tex>$\mathbf{100}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> via Focus Ion Beam(FIB). Experimental results show that dense coating prepared by Dual IBAD is more effective than loose coating prepared by magnetron sputtering in suppressing electron emission, that Ta/Zr coating is more effective than Zr coating in suppressing electron emission, and that the average current density of the cathode can reach 43A/cm<sup>2</sup> at 950 °C.

articleTitle: Investigation of Photocathodes Based on Phosphorus Doped Nanocrystalline Diamond Films
abstract: The report presents the results of a study of photo-cathodes based on phosphorus-doped nanocrystalline diamond films grown on conductive silicon substrates using the CVD method. The quantum efficiency of such cathodes was studied under the action of laser radiation with a wavelength of 266 nm and pulse duration of 15 ns. It has been found that the quantum efficiency increases with a decrease in the thickness of the diamond film, reaching a maximum at a thickness of 100 nm. In this case, the quantum efficiency was found to be 2.4 <tex>$\cdot 10^{-5}$</tex> electrons per photon.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Cyclotron Wave Protector Cavity at 5.54GHz
abstract: In this paper, the research and design of the cyclotron wave protector (CPWr) cavity at 5.54 GHz is proposed; and uses the CST to simulate the cavity's field distribution; and the cavity is also optimized on the basis of prior works; the CST PIC is adopted to solve the influences of the electronic injection on characteristics of the resonator, and a cyclotron wave protector cavity is designed. The normal operation mode and protection mode of the cyclotron wave protector (CWPr) are simulated at the same time. The cyclotron wave protector (CWPr) can work normally at 5.54GHz and has the advantages of linearity, high input power, high efficiency, and self-protection.

articleTitle: The Design of Electron Optical System for X-band Klystron
abstract: In this paper, the simulation of X-band klystron electronic optical system is completed, and the size part of the electron gun and the focusing system are partially optimized. The electron gun uses a single beam axially symmetric beam scheme. The voltage and current of the electron beam are 95kV and 45A, and the average emission current density of the cathode is 5 <tex>$A$</tex> / cm<sup>2</sup>. The focus system is designed with a uniform magnetic focusing system. The maximum magnetic field in the uniform area is about 0.57T. The calculation results show that the electric field lines are evenly distributed in the electron gun area, the electron beam fluctuations are even, and the DC current pass rate of the electron current reaches 100%, which meets the design requirements.

articleTitle: Folded Waveugide Traveling-Wave Tube with Frequency-Selective Attenuator
abstract: This paper reports a beam-wave interaction model with folded waveguide and frequency-selective attenuator. Four-cut split ring resonator and metal-substrate-metal structure are adopted to form the frequency-selective structure. The attenuator is designed to selectively attenuate the backward wave. Favorable transmission around the operating frequency can be achieved by the proposed attenuator. The wave in the input section can participate in the interaction in the output section. The PIC simulation shows that 66.7 W stable output power can be achieved by metamaterial-loaded interaction circuit. The output and reflection signals are stable for more than 20 ns without obvious oscillation, meaning for the effective suppression of the backward-wave oscillation.

articleTitle: Numerical Synthesis Method of a Dual Frequency Waveguide Directional Coupler for Miter Bend
abstract: A numerical synthesis method of the waveguide direction coupler(WGDC) for the miter bend is proposed in this paper. The concept of the synthesis method stems from the diffraction grating, which allows pattern control with the arbitrary incident angle when the waveguide operates at dual frequency. As an example, a power monitor has been designed for a 28/35GHz coupler with an incident angle of <tex>$55^{\circ}$</tex>. An arrangement of the holes array has been obtained to get the desired array pattern at a given angle, and the directivity of the power monitor is larger than 40dB at 28/35GHz.

articleTitle: Theoretical study on the effect of THz waves on nerve action potential
abstract: With the development of vacuum electronics, the generation of high-power THz sources promotes the further development of the THz biological effect. The generation and conduction of neural electrical signals accompanied by the generation of THz electromagnetic signals have been reported by a large number of studies. Further research on the relationship between neural electrical activity and THz signal, including how the THz signal generated by neural activity is transmitted and the effect of THz stimulation on neural electrical activity, is expected to reveal a new physical mechanism to explain the high-level signal transduction mechanism based on the traditional electrical signal theory. Based on the H-H model, this paper studies the effect of THz stimulation on nerve action potential. The results show that the THz wave can induce membrane excitation to generate an action potential.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Direction of Arrival Estimation of Sources in Impulsive Noise Environments
abstract: In Impulsive noise environments, the three-dimensional multiple signal classification (3D-MUSIC) algorithm would lose robustness to 3D direction of arrival (DOA) estimation of sources. In this paper, the correntropy-based correlation and correntropy-based operator replace the uniform circular array covariance matrix of 3D-MUSIC, respectively, which achieves 3D-DOA estimation in impulsive noise environments. The simulations indicate that the two proposed methods are effective.

articleTitle: Research Progress of oxide Cathode
abstract: In this paper we mainly describe the research progress of oxide cathode and its application in vacuum electron device, which includes a Ni-Sc sponge oxide cathode, a reservior oxide cathode, and a NiMoFe alloy direct-heated oxide cathode.

articleTitle: Recent Test Results on the Terahertz Gyrotron under Development in the WHMFC
abstract: In this paper, we report the recent experimental results of a terahertz gyrotron prototype under development at the Wuhan National High Magnetic Field Center (WHMFC). This gyrotron is equipped with a 15 T superconducting magnet, and it has achieved stable fundamental operation at 368.242 GHz. By varying the magnetic field, a frequency tuning range of 2.9GHz can be achieved.

articleTitle: Five-stage Depressed Collector for High Electronic Efficiency Space TWT
abstract: Traveling wave tubes (TWTs) are wideband microwave amplifiers offering high gain and efficiency. TWTs are the preferred choice of microwave amplifier in satellite transponder, and such TWTs are popularly called as space TWTs. Space TWTs have several special requirements, such as high efficiency, high gain, long life, and high linearity, etc. In order to achieve high overall TWT efficiency, each of the constituent efficiencies, namely the electronic, circuit, and collector efficiency, has to be maximized. However, it is not straightforward as it appears, as for example, when the electronic efficiency of the tube is increased, the spent beam becomes highly turbulent and chaotic, thereby placing a limit on the maximum achievable collector efficiency with a finite number of electrodes. Hence, collector efficiency enhancement in a high electronic efficiency space TWT requires adequate investigation. In this present work, the authors have designed a five-stage depressed collector for a high electronic efficiency space TWT and have compared the performance with a four-stage equivalent collector, which justifies the need for more number of collector electrodes for such a scenario.

articleTitle: Novel Extra-wide Tunnel Rectangular Folded Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, a novel Extra-Wide beam Tunnel rectangular Folded Waveguide (EWT-RFWG) traveling wave tube (TWT) is proposed. The structure not only has a larger electron beam tunnel to accommodate a higher current beam, but also achieves a wider operating bandwidth. The TWT adopting EWT-RFWG SWS can produce more than 5 W of output power in the frequency range of 245 GHz to 254 GHz. This novel SWS is also convenient for parallel connection to further improve the device output power. Integrating two slow wave structure arrays allows the total output power to be enhanced to 14.70 W from 8.19 W at 245 GHz. Meanwhile, the output power of the parallel high-frequency circuit exceeds 10 W in the frequency range of 243 GHz to 251 GHz.

articleTitle: Research on Phase-Locking of Ten-Vane 2.45GHz Microwave Oven Magnetron
abstract: This paper presents the phase locking and frequency locking of two 10-vane 2.45GHz magnetrons for microwave oven. The locking was achieved between two proposed magnetrons by a specifically designed coupled bridge structure which connects to one cavity of magnetrons. Based on this structure, two identical ten-vane magnetrons are successfully locked (both in phase and frequency), and both operate in π-mode. With a working voltage of 4.2kV and a magnetic flux density of 0.18T, the average anode current of two free-running magnetrons is 1.03A, the peak output power is 3.52kW at 2.4615GHz, and the efficiency is about 79.45%, before phase-locking. After locking, the two magnetrons produced peak power of 3.59kW and 3.51kW at 2.4541GHz, respectively, with anode current of about 1.05A and electronic efficiency of about 81%.

articleTitle: Fold Staggered Grating Waveguide Slow Wave Struc-ture for G-band TWT
abstract: A novel slow wave structure, folded staggered grating waveguide (FSGW), has been proposed for terahertz traveling wave tube. Compared to a conventional folded waveguide (FW), with slight modification FSGW provides a stronger longitudinal electric field, higher interaction impedance and lower ohmic losses. Further particle-in-cell simulation results verified that, driven by an 18.6 kV and 0.08 A electron beam, FSGW-TWT can be achieved with a gain of up to 26.0 dB at 190 GHz, as well as maximum output power of 119.2 W at 203 GHz. Moreover, the bandwidth, saturated power, gain and electron efficiency of FSGW-TWT has been significantly improved over those of FW-TWT.

articleTitle: Room temperature terahertz emission from biased AlGaN/GaN grating-gate HEMT Array
abstract: In this paper, the terahertz power radiation of AlGaN/GaN heterostructures with metal grating gate will be studied at room temperature. Terahertz radiation at different gate and drain bias voltages was applied. The calculated output power increases linearly with the drain input power. This kind of radiation emission can be understood as a combination of thermal radiation and electrical excitation. This finding implies that the grating-gate array can generate higher power even have less number of devices per unit area. The study of the radiation power has implications for the design and optimization of future terahertz sources.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Spectrum and Resonance of Grating-gate GaN/AlGaN HEMTs
abstract: In this work, the plasmonic spectrum and resonance of grating-gate GaN/AlGaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) are studied. The energy bands of the plasmonic crystal in the HEMT are simulated and compared with the theoretical formula. The THz transmission and absorption spectra of the plasmonic crystal under different temperatures are simulated. The spatial dependences of the plasma wave in the two-dimensional electron gas at different resonant modes are analyzed. It is found that the excitation of plasma oscillation in ungated region could improve the THz absorption of plasmonic crystal.

articleTitle: Space Pulsed Terahertz Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier
abstract: Terahertz (THz) technology is widely used in military and aerospace fields due to its high frequency, and high bandwidth. By taking advantage of its short wavelength nature, a matching antenna can be used to achieve higher azimuth resolution, with a high frame rate in SAR mode operation and its larger access bandwidth resulting in higher range resolution. In this paper, a space pulsed THZ traveling-wave tube (TWT) amplifier with a frequency range of 210GHz~220GHz and a maximum pulse output power of more than 15W is introduced. The design and analysis of the 25kV high voltage power supply, the folded waveguide traveling wave tube, and the whole device are carried out. Within 10G bandwidth, pulse repetition frequency is 100Hz~10kHz, and within 50% duty cycle range, 10W saturated power output power in the full bandwidth range can be achieved, providing a reference for the subsequent aerospace design and application of THZ products.

articleTitle: Terahertz Gauss-Bessel beam generation using free electrons to drive an axicon
abstract: Gauss-Bessel beams have the attractive properties of low diffraction loss, self-reconstruction, and small energy divergence, which have promising application prospects in various fields. Here we propose and investigate a scheme to directly generate a terahertz Gauss-Bessel beam by using an electron bunch to drive an axicon, from which the focused Cherenkov radiation is obtained. Compared with the previous optical driven methods, which are all indirect methods, the proposed scheme is a direction method of generating a terahertz Gauss-Bessel beam. In addition, the focusing depth, spectrum, and field intensity of the terahertz Gauss-Bessel beam can be readily adjusted by changing the parameters of the electron bunch and axicon. This proposed scheme has potential in terahertz spectroscopy, imaging, and communication systems.

articleTitle: Scattering Matrix Analysis for Main and Parasitic Oscillations of a Gyrotron Oscillator Cavity with Disc Type Output Window
abstract: This paper introduces the scattering matrix method to calculate the resonance of main and parasitic oscillation in the gyrotron beam-wave interaction cavity and after-cavity when the effect of the disc-type output window is taken into account. The results show that the resonance of the main mode in the cavity has been obtained precisely with the scattering matrix analysis comparing that obtained by solving the inhomogeneous string equation, and the paper also shows the influence of the output window on the S-parameter.

articleTitle: 220-GHz Extended Interaction Klystron Based on Single-mode and Multimode Operation
abstract: We have developed a compact 220-GHz extended interaction klystron (EIK) based on single-mode operation, which can generate 120W output power at around 220 GHz, the 1dB bandwidth is greater than 180MHz, the gain is greater than 30dB, and the duty cycle is 5%. The test results may be interesting. However, the bandwidth of EIK is insufficient, which affects its application fields. Therefore, we propose a G-band EIK based on multimode operation. PIC simulation shows that when the input power is 70mW, the EIK can provide 195W output power at around 220 GHz, and the 3dB bandwidth is greater than 4GHz.

articleTitle: Illustration of A Novel 220GHz Symmetrical Double Slots Elliptical-Like Coupled-Cavity Slow Wave Structure
abstract: In this paper, a novel elliptical-like cavity symmetrical double slots coupled-cavity (EC-SDSCC) slow wave structure (SWS) is presented. The cross section of the cavity is two symmetrical semi-ellipses in two sides and a rectangle in the center. The dispersion characteristics of the novel SWS is studied. This novel SWS is suitable for G-band high-power sheet electron beam traveling wave tube (SB TWT) due to its <tex>$\mathbf{1.25}\times \mathbf{0.3}\ \mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> large sheet electron beam tunnel and <tex>$\sim \mathbf{11}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex> high coupling impedance. Compared with the corresponding cuboid cavity structure, the EC-SDSCC reduces about 30dB/m of metal losses which could increase the saturation output power and saturation gain significantly.

articleTitle: Sheet Beam Traveling Wave Tube Focused by Cross-Field
abstract: In this paper, cross-field is tried to focus a sheet beam traveling wave tube (TWT) for obtaining both high gain and high net efficiency due to electron selection. The device is analyzed by a non-linear code. And the results show that, at the input power of 0.8W and in varied operation bands from 8GHz to 250GHz, compared with traditional cross-field amplifiers, higher gains are obtained, and compared with the same sheet beam TWT without cross-field focusing, higher efficiency is obtained. At 12GHz, the sheet beam TWT focused by cross-field gets both high gain and high efficiency when the input power varied from 0.01W to 0.8W.

articleTitle: Study on Spindle Waveguide SWS for Sheet Beam
abstract: A novel spindle waveguide SWS suitable for sheet beam is proposed. By optimizing the spindle waveguide SWS, the working bandwidth is increased. And then, the deformation of straight waveguide in the new SWS is conducive to increasing the area of the electron beam channel and improving the longitudinal field of the beam wave interaction area. Compared with the traditional folded waveguide, the bandwidth and coupling impedance of the spindle waveguide SWS are improved. The spindle TWT has the potential of wide bandwidth and high power. At 340 GHz, the spindle SWS has a higher operating frequency under the same dimensions. The coupling impedance of the spindle SWS is more than 50 % higher than FWG.

articleTitle: Final version-Numerical Studies on Superradiant Relativistic Backward-wave Oscillator with Coupling Output of $\text{TE}_{11}$ Mode
abstract: An X-band superradiant relativistic backward wave oscillator (SR-RBWO) using a structure combining resonant reflector and coupling gap is designed in this paper. This structure can realize the spatial mode coupling from coaxial waveguide TEM mode to TM<inf>01</inf> mode in circular waveguide, and in output circular waveguide, a plate-insert TM01- TE<inf>11</inf> mode converter is introduced. Finally, the superradiant (SR) microwave can directly output with radiation mode <tex>$\text{TE}_{11}$</tex> in circular waveguide. The particle in cell (PIC) simulation results reval that when this structure applied with a low guiding magnetic field 0.37 T, SR pulse with peak power 1.05 GW corresponding to power conversion efficiency 180% can be obtained.

articleTitle: The Discussion on the Multimode Extended Interaction Circuit
abstract: A multimode extended interaction circuit was proposed in our previous work to overcome bandwidth limitation of the conventional single-mode extended interaction circuits. Several issues on this newly proposed multimode circuit are discussed, including its naming principle, the differences between this multimode circuit and the other circuits, and the evolution from conventional single-mode circuit to this multimode circuit.

articleTitle: 198GHz 140W Pulsed EIK Subsystem
abstract: This paper presents the development and test of a 198 GHz pulsed Extended Interaction Klystron (EIK) subsystem for THz markets including Dynamic Nuclear Polarization (DNP). The EIK amplifies a 30 mW input signal to 140 Watts with a - 3dB bandwidth of ~275 MHz. The operating cathode voltage is 17.7 kV and the cathode current is 178 mA. With electron beam transmission of 84 %, the subsystem is capable of operating with a duty cycle up to 5%. Liquid cooling is used to maintain the radio frequency (RF) signal stability required for DNP applications.

articleTitle: Design of a circular electron injection gun for terahertz traveling wave tubes
abstract: The electron gun is one of the core components of the traveling wave tube, and the performance of the traveling wave tube depends on the design quality of the electron gun. In this paper, a high compression ratio electron gun for a 0.34 THz traveling wave tube is investigated. The designed electron gun produces an electron beam with a beam waist radius of 0.047 mm and good electron laminar flow by simulation with CST Particle Studio. Analyzing the simulation results, the corresponding beam voltage is 21.9 kV, the beam current is 112 mA, and the obtained electron beam compression ratio is 68, and the obtained simulation results meet the requirements.

articleTitle: Ka-band Dual-port Coaxial Magnetron for Array Application
abstract: Magnetron is an oscillator with poor frequency stability and could not be applied in phase coherent system. Using the CST Particle Studio, the coaxial magnetron model with an additional coupling port set in outer cavity was built. Simulation analysis was conducted by using a coupling bridge to connect two magnetron coupling ports. Then, a prototype of Ka-band coaxial magnetron was successfully fabricated. From the experiment, the total output power of 32kW with the duty cycle of 1%o was obtained at the operating voltage of 12kVkV and the pulse-width of 500ns. Within a bandwidth of 1GHz, the phase difference of dual-ports is stable around <tex>$22.5^{\circ}$</tex>, the phase fluctuation amplitude is less than <tex>$2.5^{\circ}$</tex>, and so the phase between the two ports is coherent. This kind magnetron could be applied at the field of millimeter wave high power microwave synthesis arrays application.

articleTitle: Work function mapping of single-crystal graphene
abstract: Kelvin potential force microscopy (KPFM) was used to study the surface potential of single-crystal graphene transferred to silicon dioxide substrate and calculate the work function of single-crystal graphene. It was observed that when graphene on copper substrate was directly scanned, the surface potential distribution of normal graphene appeared to be more disordered compared to that of single-crystal graphene. This feature is used to determine the single-crystal property of graphene grown on copper foil by chemical vapor deposition without transfer. The surface potential of the multilayer graphene area at the nucleation point of single-crystal graphene and the surrounding single-layer area is analyzed. It is found that the work function of the multilayer graphene area is slightly lower than that of the single-layer graphene, which provides guidance for the application of single-crystal graphene and multilayer graphene in field emission.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of the Effects of THz-IR Modulation of Ion Channel Permeability on Neuronal Electrical Activity
abstract: Both theoretical simulations and experimental studies have tentatively shown that terahertz(THz) or mid-infrared(IR) electromagnetic waves are capable of modifying the permeability of specific ion channels. Vacuum electronics are an indispensable high-power source for conducting terahertz bioeffects experiments. However, there is currently a lack of theoretical tools to link kinetic simulations with electrophysiological experiments on relevant biological effects. Based on a modified Hodgkin-Huxley model, this paper analyzes the effect of the altered channel permeability properties on the electrical activity of neurons. Simulations showed that the alteration of ion channel permeability could directly trigger the action potential of neurons. This study bridges the interconnection between the phenomena in relevant theoretical simulations and experimental studies.

articleTitle: Terahertz Broadband Frequency Doubler Based on GaAs Monolithic
abstract: This paper focuses on how to realize the large bandwidth input power coupling diode and a large bandwidth waveguide output probe. Based on the balanced structure, we focus on comparing the effects of different reduced height waveguide structures on input matching, a broadband terahertz multiplier is designed. The simulation satisfies the power output of WR-7 waveguide bandwidth, achieves the efficiency of about 30% of 110~170GHz and the typical value output of more than 100mW at 350mW input.

articleTitle: State Feedback Control of Distributed radar system with Packet dropouts and Time-varying delays
abstract: In this paper, we present state feedback control for the distributed radar with packet dropouts and time-varying delays. The delays are time-varying. The packet dropouts mean the loss of the state measurement data. Firstly, the state feedback control design is transformed into stability analysis for a 2D stochastic system. Secondly, we obtain the stability condition based on linear matrix inequality (LMI) of mean-square asymptotic stability of the 2D stochastic system. And we give the method to get the law for the state feedback control design. The proposed method can stabilize the distributed radar with packet dropouts and time-varying delays. Finally, a numerical example is to show the validity of the methods.

articleTitle: Design of Side-coupled Absorption Cavity to Suppress the Oscillation of Sheet Beam Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: The stability of a sheet beam (SB) traveling wave tube (TWT) in Ka-band is investigated, in which the origin of self-oscillation and its impact on the high-power traveling wave tube are analyzed. To suppress the self-oscillations in the high-power device, the side coupling structure of the absorption cavity was designed with the absorption filtering method. The simulation results by electromagnetic simulation software show that the absorption cavities can efficiently suppress the self-oscillations generated by the traveling wave tube structure under the simulation condition of no input signal. Furthermore, in the condition with input signal, the single-stage Ka-band traveling wave tube with absorption cavities loaded can stably produce high power without instabilities.

articleTitle: Tunable Optical Topological Transition of Free-Electron-Based Cherenkov Radiation
abstract: Efficient and flexible methods to generate and manipulate free-electron radiations are of great importance for modern science and technology. Using the brilliant optical properties of customized metamaterials, we could control the free-electron radiations as required. In this pioneering work, as a standard example, we use the graphene hyperbolic metamaterial to realize tunable optical topological transitions of Cherenkov radiation and reveal the physical mechanism inside. Specifically, we utilize the ultrafast photothermal and nonlocal properties of graphene to achieve two novel optical topological transitions. Our works show that the properties of free-electron radiations can be tailored by the topological optical and photonic properties of electromagnetic mediums.

articleTitle: Study of influence of magnetic shielding on Penning Ion source
abstract: In this paper, the dynamic behaviors of electrons in a small Penning ion source model are analyzed by Particle In Cell plus Monte Carlo Collision(PIC/MCC) particle simulation method combined with the Scalar Magnetic Potential finite-difference Method(SMPM). Mainly, the influence of magnetic shielding on the trajectory and spatial distribution of electrons in the discharge process is taken into consideration. The influence of magnetic shielding on the plasma impedance during the excitation discharge of Penning source is further discussed. The results show that the addition of magnetic shielding promotes the uniformity of both electron spatial distribution and radial velocity distribution in the source, which can be beneficial to the sufficient ionization of electrons and hydrogen background gas. Moreover, the plasma impedance stabilization zone II is extended by about 3 times compared with the previous one, which helps to enhance the source discharge stability and provide a reference for improving the source performance. In particle simulation, parallel algorithms are added to speed up particle simulation.

articleTitle: Qualitative analysis of heavy metals in onion epidermal cells by near-field microwave microscopy
abstract: Near-field microwave microscopy has the ability to penetrate into the sample and achieve the detection of electromagnetic properties inside the object, which is the basis for the detection of physical and chemical properties inside the cell and the imaging of the surface morphology. We propose a method to qualitatively analyze the presence or absence of specific heavy metal ions inside the cells by measuring the quality factor <tex>$Q$</tex> of normal cell samples and those containing heavy metal ions using near-field scanning microscopy. The quality factors <tex>$Q$</tex> in the test of the two kinds of cells are compared. Results show that quality factor <tex>$Q$</tex> of the cells can be distinguished, both in the comparison of the same plant cells and the comparison of different plant cells. The qualitative distinction between normal cells and polluted cells containing heavy metal ions can be achieved.

articleTitle: Study on Wide-band Elliptic Staggered Vane Slow-wave Structure
abstract: A wideband elliptic staggered vane slow-wave structure (ESVSWS) operating in terahertz is proposed and studied in this paper. The calculation demonstrates that the ESVSWS possesses weak dispersion, flat phase velocity curve, low circuit loss of only 0.05--0.06dB/period, and wide beam channel. Based on the ESVSWS, an beam-wave interaction circuit of sheet electron beam TWT for G-band is designed and particle-in-cell (PIC) analysis is carried out. The simulation results show that, with a sheet electron beam voltage of 20.9kV and current of 135mA, the output power of 116.9W can be obtained at 225GHz, and the corresponding gain and electronic efficiency are 28.2dB and 3.48%, respectively. The instantaneous 3dB bandwidth reaches 50GHz under equal excitation of 180mW, with the relative bandwidth of 22.7% from 210GHz to 260GHz.

articleTitle: Design of the W-band smooth Gaussian radiator
abstract: In this paper, a smooth Gaussian radiator from a rectangular waveguide TE<inf>10</inf> mode to a circular waveguide HE<inf>11</inf> mode for W-band is proposed. The W-band smooth Gaussian radiator consists of two parts: one is to convert the TE<inf>10</inf> mode in the rectangular waveguide into the TE<inf>11</inf> mode in the circular waveguide using a square-circle transition; the other part is the TE<inf>11</inf> mode converted into a Gaussian distributed HE<inf>11</inf> mode using the waveguide wall smooth radius structure. The simulation results show that conversion efficiency of TE<inf>10</inf>-TE<inf>11</inf> is over 99.6% from the 84GHz-104GHz. The coupling efficiency of the TE<inf>11</inf>-HE<inf>11</inf> is more than 96% in the frequency range of <tex>$92\text{GHz}\sim 98\text{GHz}$</tex>. Meanwhile, the energy transmission efficiency can reach more than 98%. The smooth Gaussian radiator has a simple structure, easy to machine, and avoids the disadvantage of the corrugated Gaussian radiator.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of Sapphire Output Window for 170 GHz Gyrotron
abstract: In order to satisfy the energy transmission requirements of 170GHz gyrotron, sapphire output window with low reflectivity of 100mm in diameter and 1.44mm in thickness was selected. Through the experimental test, the output power of 170 GHz gyrotron is approximately 0.3MW under the condition of 0.25% duty ratio. Under the pulse width of 2.5ms and pulse repetition frequency of 1Hz, the sapphire output window is broken and damaged. According to the thermal and structure simulation, the reason for the damage of the window is that the temperature difference between the centre and the edge exceeds the bearing limit of sapphire material. By comparing theoretical analysis with experimental phenomenon, it provides a reliable theoretical basis for the gyrotron experiment and the optimization of the structure of the output window.

articleTitle: A Novel Denoising Algorithm for Detection Signal of Gyro-TWT
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low SNR of detection signal due to noise interference in the burn-in test of Ka-band gyrotron traveling wave tube, a novel denoising algorithm combining wavelet threshold and ant colony optimization was proposed in this paper. The novel denoising algorithm adopts the wavelet GCV threshold selection function and uses the ant colony optimization, which iterates the GCV threshold selection function to select the optimal wavelet threshold. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm improves the signal-to-noise ratio of the detection signal and guarantees the accuracy of the burn-in test, which successfully solve the exiting problem.

articleTitle: Design of a Ladder-type W-band Extended Interaction Circuit for Facilitating Dual $2\pi$-Mode Switching
abstract: The development of multimode amplifier research for broadband and mode switching applications presents significant new challenges, as it brings into mode design, manufacturing implementation and measurement issues that are not particularly significant in single-mode operation. In this paper we describe our design approach to these challenges, with emphasis on the mode switching implementation of a W-band dual-mode extended interaction amplifier. This device was designed to produce peak power of about 1 to 1.5 KW with a dual-mode spacing of about 900 MHz. The circuit will be driven by a 2 A, 15 kV electron beam. Early results demonstrate a promising dual-mode circuit with a typical ladder-type output cavity for ease of processing and measurement.

articleTitle: Heat Dissipation Design based on Porous Medium Structure for Gyro-TWT Collector
abstract: A study of the gyro-TWT collector with porous medium heat dissipation structure has been presented. In the design, a lot of rings with good thermal conductivity were used to fill the heat dissipation area, which was forming the porous medium structure. Cooling water flows through the channels formed by the gap to cool collector. The simulation results indicated that the structure collector was able to achieve higher power capacity.

articleTitle: Investigation of Trapezoid Double Staggered Grating SWS for G-band CW TWT
abstract: A Trapezoid Double Staggered Grating (TDSG) slow-wave structure (SWS) traveling-wave tube (TWT) is proposed to a high-power continuous wave (CW) amplifier. TDSG has high interaction impedance, high structural strength and good heat dissipation performance. Therefore, the PIC method is used to obtain the transmission and interaction characteristics of the electromagnetic wave in this structure. the calculation results indicate that the traveling wave tube can produce over 66.5 W output power and 34.25 dB gain at the center frequency of 216 GHz, the gain is greater than 30.8 dB from 212 GHz to 218 GHz and the maximum electronic efficiency is 6.04 %.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Study of C-band Ridge-Loaded Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator
abstract: In this paper, a C-band magnetically insulated line oscillator incorporated with a ridge-loaded vanes slow wave structure is designed and simulated in CST. Ridge-loaded SWS provides higher interaction impedance than conventional SWS hence efficiency is enhanced. Eigenmode simulation is done to find the resonant frequency, the effect of ridges on the dispersion curve, and interaction impedance. PIC simulation results reveal that 4.5GW output power of 5GHz with an efficiency of 15% is obtained by applying 500k V.

articleTitle: Progress of European Industrial Gyrotron Developments for Nuclear Fusion
abstract: The progress of industrial gyrotron developments at Thales, that are done in collaboration with its European partners, are presented in this report. Recent test results are discussed and the design status of new industrial units under development is presented.

articleTitle: Development of high efficiency klystron at IHEP*
abstract: After the discovery of the Higgs boson at LHC, Chinese scientists have planned to build a “Great Collider,” which is a next-generation multinational particle accelerator research facility proposed as a circular electron-positron collider (CEPC) and a super proton-proton collider (SPPC). The CEPC synchrotron radiation power is supposed to be more than 60MW. The efficiency from direct current (DC) to beam power is a very important aspect of the cost of project implementation. Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP) is developing a higher efficiency klystron of frequency 650 MHz/800 kW with an efficiency goal of around 80%. Different klystron prototypes have been manufactured in the last five years to achieve this goal. Moreover, the beam dynamics of 2860MHz (80MW) klystron is completed and will be manufactured in 2023. The design of 5720 MHz (80 MW &50 MW) klystron for CEPC Linac is also in progress.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized and Wideband Transmitarray Using 1 Bit Magnetoelectric Dipole Elements
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized and wideband transmitarray unit structure is proposed. The element proposes a new electric dipole working mode based on the magnetoelectric dipole unit structure. Circular polarization wave transmission and polarization torsion are realized due to the addition of the working mode. This unit structure has the advantages of circularly polarization, central feeding configuration, structural symmetry, and can achieve 1 <tex>$\mathbf{dB}$</tex> insertion-loss bandwidth of 31% in Ka-band. The basic structure of the unit using two-layer substrate can effectively reduce the production cost. These advantages show that the proposed unit has great potential in the application of millimeter wave satellite communications.

articleTitle: Online Measurement Approach of the Transformer Parasitics for the LCLC Resonant Converter in the Space TWTA Applications
abstract: The LCLC resonant converter is universally applied in the space travelling-wave tube amplifiers (TWTA). Normally, the open-loop control is utilized in the LCLC resonant converter, where the switching frequency and duty cycle are set to the exact values to achieve soft switching characteristics. However, since the switching frequency and duty cycle are calculated by the transformer parasitics, it is crucial to measure the real transformer parasitic parameters precisely. The classical way to measure the transformer parasitics is by an impedance analyzer, however, the transformer parasitics under real operating conditions may deviate from the offline measured results. In order to solve the above problem, an online measurement method is proposed in this paper. With this online measurement approach, all the real transformer parasitic values can be easily obtained in a low cost and simple implementation way. The proposed method is validated by the experiments as well.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Testing Based on Near Field THz SAR Imaging
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a nondestructive testing technique based on terahertz frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) synthetic aperture radar (SAR), combined with range migration algorithm (RMA) for imaging detection of PMI insulating foam applied to aerospace field. The results show that the method is capable of detecting and imaging the interior of the foam and can improve the image resolution.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of a Low voltage, 100s'-kW, X-Band, Multiport Magnetron for Phased Array Applications
abstract: A low voltage, 100s'-kW, X-band magnetron with specifically designed power distribution in an output port and two coupling ports is proposed for highly efficient phase locking in array magnetrons toward <tex>$\boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{s}$</tex>-, MW-level microwave pulse generation. The efficient phase-locked magnetron array can be equivalent to the configuration of the single magnetron with its three ports connected to three matched loads. The test results show (1) the total power can reach 110kW with <tex>$1\mu\mathrm{s}-\text{pulses}$</tex>, low repetitive frequency of 500Hz, voltage of <tex>$\sim \mathbf{22}\mathbf{kV}$</tex>, and (2) the power from two coupling ports are much smaller than the power from the output port, which offers the opportunity to realize efficient phase locking between multiple magnetrons. The proposed magnetron is a promising unit for constructing a compact, highly efficient phased array toward high power applications.

articleTitle: A Terahertz Magnetless Circulator Based on Spatia-Temporal Modulated Varactor Diodes with Microstrip Resonators
abstract: This study presents a new design for a magnetless terahertz circulator. The proposed device is based on the combination of spatiotemporal modulated varactor diodes and microstrip resonators. A Y-shaped resonator is created by connecting three stepped-impedance microstrip resonators in series with three varactor diodes. The resonator is modulated by applying three low-frequency signals with a phase difference of <tex>$\pi/3$</tex> to the reverse-biased varactor diodes, resulting in a magnetless terahertz circulator. The theoretical analysis shows that the circulator can provide transmission with an insertion loss of 6.01 dB, a return loss of 8.14 dB, and an isolation of 20.95 dB at 0.14 THz.

articleTitle: Fast microfocus cold cathode x-ray tube based on carbon nanotube array
abstract: A cold cathode x-ray tube based on carbon nanotube (CNT) with a vertically-aligned morphology has been fabricated for miniature X-ray source application. The vertically-aligned carbon nanotube was grown by microwave plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition method. A maximum emission current of 200 <tex>$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex> is achieved with a maximum current density of more than 10 A/cm<sup>2</sup> from the CNT emitter. We have optimized the beam convergence on the target of the microfocus X-ray tube and a focal spot size of 5 μm was achieved. X-ray images of JIMA card, chips, multilayer printed circuit board and field programmable gate array were demonstrated with approximately 5 μm width.

Author Keywords: microwave plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition

articleTitle: Simulation of Sub-THz Backward-Wave Oscillators With a Self-Focused Pseudospark-Sourced Sheet Electron Beam
abstract: The results of simulation of the two previously proposed millimeter-band backward-wave oscillators (BWO) driven by a self-focused pseudospark-sourced sheet electron beams are presented. Plasma focusing makes possible beam transmission through a slow-wave structure (SWS) over distances of the order of several cm while providing effective beam-wave interaction. Two models of beam focusing by plasma in SWS are considered. A simplified approach, in which the electrodynamic structure is pre-filled with fully ionized plasma, allows assessing beam transport with effective beam wave interaction. A more accurate model, in which the plasma is formed as a result of impact ionization of the gas by beam electrons allows simulation of non-stationary processes of plasma channel formation. It describes not only plasma focusing in the interaction region, but also the consequent transport of the spent beam to collector via the plasma channel, which remains intact at the exit of the SWS.

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigation of a 1.16 THz Fourth-Harmonic Large-Orbit Gyrotron
abstract: A large-orbit electron beam can be considered as a special small-orbit beam with its guiding center on the axis. In this paper, we study the self-consistent nonlinear theory of large-orbit gyrotron in the guiding center coordinate system by deducing the self-consistent nonlinear theory of small-orbit gyrotron. We design a three-stage beam-wave interaction cavity through theoretical analysis. A 1.16THz fourth-harmonic large-orbit gyrotron is theoretically investigated based on the self-consistent nonlinear theory. <tex>$\mathbf{TE}_{\mathbf{47}}$</tex> is selected as the operating mode, when the gyrotron operates at 1.16THz with a beam of 40kV and 1.6A, and a magnetic field of 11.192T, the beam-wave interaction efficiency is 1.81%.

articleTitle: Micro composite vacuum gauge for space applications
abstract: A configuration of micro vacuum gauge combined the benefits of capacitive gauge (CDG) and Pirani gauge was proposed for space exploration. The reading of the CDG is independent of gas composition to be measured, which can be used as a calibration standard. The Pirani gauge, with strong discrimination against different gases, is adopted as a gas composition analyzer in this configuration. With this design, the partial pressure of certain gas components can be analyzed qualitatively or even quantitatively. Considering its small size, weight and power consumption, it has significant advantages in space applications.

articleTitle: Design of X-band RBWO output system
abstract: In order to realize the output requirements of RBWO, a high-power microwave radiation system is designed for the X-band placed in the outer cavity, including a mode converter and a compact antenna output structure. The electromagnetic simulation software was used to numerically simulate and optimize the mode converter and antenna structure. The results show that the X-band coaxial TEM-circular waveguide <tex>$TM_{01}$</tex> mode converter structure has high conversion efficiency within the frequency range of interest, and the conversion efficiency of the mode converter is 99.54% at the center frequency of 10.1GHz, and the conversion efficiency of the mode converter is greater than 98% in the 500MHz frequency range. Through the numerical simulation and optimization of the antenna output structure, the antenna pattern gain simulation result is 18.86dB at 10.1GHz (center frequency), which meets the requirements of antenna miniaturization and lightweight design. The design idea and structure can be applied to the dual-frequency antenna radiation system of RBWO.

articleTitle: THz Absorption Properties of Three Kidney Stone Components
abstract: The terahertz (THz) absorption properties of calcium oxalate, calcium phosphate and calcium carbonate, which are the main components of kidney stone, are investigated experimentally in the frequency bands of 0.12 THz-8 THz and 12 THz-120 THz by using the vector network analyzer (VNA), the terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) and the infrared (IR) spectrometer. The measured results have demonstrated the absorption difference with frequency. The results of VNA and THz-TDS are consistent that calcium oxalate has weaker absorption and calcium phosphate exhibits stronger absorption when frequency is below 1 THz. The absorption of calcium phosphate is higher than calcium carbonate until frequency is greater than 2 THz. The result of IR spectrometer shows that calcium oxalate has main characteristic absorption peak at 48.8 THz, calcium phosphate and calcium carbonate are 31 THz and 42.8 THz respectively. The results provide a reference and may help to the analysis and identification of kidney stone in the future.

articleTitle: Terahertz reflective phase shifter based on HEMT
abstract: Terahertz phase shifter is a key research direction of terahertz technology. Phase shifter is a device that can change the phase of the output signal, but terahertz phase shifter suffers from the problems of small phase shift angle, large insertion loss, slow speed, and small power capacity. HEMT (High Electron Mobility Transistor) possesses high electron mobility and high power capacity. In this paper, we design a terahertz phase shifter based on a 3dB directional coupler and HEMT. By controlling the “0” and “1” states of HEMT, the phase shifter can reach 180° and the insertion loss is less than 8dB.

articleTitle: Effect of Ultra Violet Light on Planar Field Emitters
abstract: Two different types of planar nano-scale (4–5 nm) field emitters, bowtie and diode devices, were characterized for use as electron sources for vacuum nano-transistors. I-V measurements were performed before and after Ultra-violet (UV) light exposure. Experiments showed that the field emission current was <tex>$\approx 2.7 \text{nA}$</tex> before the UV exposure and was <tex>$\approx 1.8\text{nA}$</tex> after the exposure for the bow-die devices. Experiments also showed that the field emission current was <tex>$\approx 5.6\text{nA}$</tex> before the UV exposure and was <tex>$\approx 3.6 \text{nA}$</tex> after the exposure for the diode devices. This reduction in current could be attributed to the removal of water vapor by UV exposure resulting in the reduction in the surface leakage current. A long-term stability tests conducted after the UV exposure showed both the bow-tie and diode devices emitted a stable current (<5% drop) for > 1100 hrs. of continuous operation at a DC bias of 5 V.

articleTitle: The optimization of a miniature mattauch herzog mass spectrometer
abstract: In recent years, miniature mass spectrometer (MS) play an important role in the space exploration and environmental monitoring fields. In this paper, A miniature Mattauch-Herzog double focusing mass spectrometer is developed for mass analysis. The software SIMION8.1 is mainly used to study the fringing field of the magnetic analyzer where the magnetic flux density is 0.85T. From that, we know the distribution of the fringing field can be greatly compressed by adding ideal magnetic shielding material at the entrance of the magnetic analyzer. Besides, the experiment shows the instrument has a good performance and the mass resolution of He is 39.643.

articleTitle: A Compact Ku-band Relativistic Triaxial Klystron Amplifier
abstract: A compact relativistic triaxial klystron amplifier (TKA) with two cascaded single-gap bunching cavities is presented. For the faster modulation of electron beam and the shorter length of the device, the input cavity and cascaded single-gap bunching cavities with energy coupling are employed. Moreover, the length from the input cavity to the output cavity is about 114 mm in Ku-band. The simulation results demonstrate that the peak output power can reach 649 MW at 14.0 GHz. The corresponding efficiency is about 37.9%, and the gain is 42.1dB.

articleTitle: Angle-controlled Simth-Purcell Radiation Excited by Free Electron Beam
abstract: When an electron beam passes through the surface of a periodic grating, electromagnetic radiation is generated, and this radiation is referred to as Smith-Purcell radiation. The main methods for modulating Smith-Purcell radiation are changing the grating period and the electron beam voltage. In this study, it is proposed that the Smith-Purcell radiation frequency can be controlled by changing the observation angle, and the experimental observation frequency is consistent with the theory. This has important application significance for the development of free electron radiation sources around Smith-Purcell radiation.

articleTitle: Design and experiment of the pill-box window for 0.67THz TWT
abstract: This paper described the design and tested results of the pill-box window for the 0.67THz travelling wave tube (TWT) with the help of 3-D simulation software. The test results show that the design of the pill-box window satisfied the need of the TWT. The S21 parameter is -3.1 dB, and the S11 parameter is less than -10 dB from 649GHz to 672GHz. It bases the manufacture of the 0.67THz travelling wave tube.

articleTitle: Novel Broadband Dual-Polarization Four-way Power Divider for Waveguide Array Antennas
abstract: In this paper, a broadband dual-circular-polarization four-way power divider based on a novel topology is presented. This design consists of a feeding waveguide, a power divider network, and a radiating horn. The simulation result for a Ka-band (25.9-32.2 GHz) four-way power divider is presented, demonstrating that the input port return loss is better than 20 dB, the input-output isolation is better than 20 dB, four-way equal amplitude and in-phase outputs can be achieved over a bandwidth of 6.3GHz.

articleTitle: Free-electron radiation nanophotonics
abstract: Free-electron radiation lies at the heart of fundamental physics and photonics. It is currently opening up new frontiers across many areas of science, and it enables vast applications as varied as high-energy particle detectors, free-electron lasers, electron microscopies, medical imaging, and security scanning. In this work, we will introduce several exotic phenomena of free-electron radiation from inhomogeneous nanostructures [1]–[10]. First, we report a new mechanism that uses the constructive interference of resonance transition radiation from photonic crystals to create both the effective Cherenkov radiation [1], [2]. This reported mechanism could tailor the radiation angles in a flexible way with high sensitivity, feasible for arbitrary desired range of velocities. Therefore, the photonic crystals could overcome the material limit for Cherenkov detectors and offer an enticing platform well-suited for identification of particles at high energy with enhanced sensitivity. Second, a new paradigm is proposed for Cherenkov detectors that utilizes the broadband angular filter made from stacks of variable one-dimensional photonic crystals [3], [4]. Owing to the Brewster effect, the angular filter is transparent only to Cherenkov photons from a precise incident angle. Particle identification is achieved by mapping each Cherenkov angle to the peak-intensity position of transmitted photons in the detection plane. Such angular filtering effect, although decreases the photon number collected in the detection plane, enables the realization of a non-dispersive pseudo refractive index over the entire visible spectrum. Moreover, the pseudo refractive index can be flexibly designed to different values close to unity. Our angular-selective Brewster paradigm offers a feasible solution to implement compact and highly sensitive Cherenkov detectors especially in beam lines with a small angular divergence using regular dielectrics. Third, we report a general approach to enhance the photon yield of Cherenkov radiation using dispersionless plasmons [5], [6]. Broadband dispersionless plasmons can be realized by exploiting either the acoustic nature of terahertz plasmons in a graphene-based heterostructure or the nonlocal property of optical plasmons in a metallodielectric structure. When coupled to moving electrons, such dispersionless plasmons give rise to a radiation enhancement rate more than two orders of magnitude (as compared with conventional Cherenkov radiation) over an ultrabroad frequency band. Moreover, since the phase velocity of dispersionless plasmons can be made as small as the Fermi velocity, giant radiation enhancements can be readily induced by ultralow-energy free electrons (e.g. with a kinetic energy down to 3 electronvolts), without resorting to relativistic particles. Fourth, we reveal the emergence of anomalous free-electron radiation beyond the conventional formation time by exploring the penetration of a fast electron through the interface of a plasmonic medium [7]. This anomalous radiation originates from a long tail of bulk plasmons, which follows the electron trajectory into the plasmonic medium but can attach to the interface for a very long time. As a result, this tail offers a unique route to mix the bulk and surface effects, largely extend the electron-interface interaction, and create the light emission far beyond the conventional formation time. Therefore, this anomalous free-electron radiation is a mixture of surface-bulk effect, different from Cherenkov radiation as purely a bulk effect or transition radiation as purely a surface effect. Our finding also offers a new perspective for Ferrell radiation and is able to settle the historical debate regarding its physical origin. Moreover exotic phenomena of free-electron radiation will be introduced, if time allowed [8]–[10].

articleTitle: Analysis of a W-Band Microstrip Meander-Line TWT with Novel Focusing Structure
abstract: In this paper, based on a novel focusing structure, the characteristics of a W-Band microstrip meander-line traveling wave tube (MML-TWT) are simulated and analyzed. Compared with the traditional approach, the novel focusing structure can achieve the purpose of stable sheet electron beam (SEB) transport with lower magnetic field. The simulation results show that the novel focusing structure for MML-TWT is beneficial to balance the potential distribution and evidently reduce the operating magnetic field, while it barely affects the high frequency characteristics of the whole device. Furthermore, the lower magnetic field can contribute to a miniaturization of the bulkiness of the MML-TWTs.

articleTitle: Design of a Coherent Smith-Purcell Superradiation Source at W-band
abstract: When the surface wave interacts with the electron beam, the group gathers to form the periodic electron beam group, and radiates the frequency doubling signal of the surface wave, namely the so-called “coherent”. In this paper, a coherent Smith-Purcell superradiation (SPR) source at W-band is proposed. By using cylindrical periodic metal gratings with period of 1.03 mm and groove depth of 0.857mm, and a hollow pulsed electron beam with voltage of 18.4kV, repetition frequency of 47GHz, the radiation power reaches 2W at 93.784GHz. The result shows that the triple-mirror quasi-optical cavity plays a very important role in the resonance and energy feedback of coherent SPR. The system provides a new way for the development of tunable terahertz radiation sources.

articleTitle: Q-Band MPM for LEO Satellite Application
abstract: In recent years, the demand for high-capacity and high-speed has led to the rapid development of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite systems and technologies. Q-band linearized travelling wave tube amplifier with broadband, high efficiency, low non-linear distortion and high confidentiality are widely used. The design and implementation of a Q-band compact Microwave Power Module (MPM), which integrates a Q-band linearized travelling wave tube amplifier with each other as cold backup, band-pass filter and microwave switch, meets the functional and high integration requirements of LEO satellite payloads. This paper presents the main specifications, functions, design solutions and test data of the MPM. The measurement of specification include in-band gain flatness of less than 0.6dB, saturation third order inter modulation distortion (IM3) is 13dBc, and Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) is 5.5% at OBO4.5dB.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of a Ka-band Phase-locked High Power Microwave Amplifier Operating in Hybrid Theory
abstract: To achieve the coherent power combination of Ka-band HPM generators, a Phase-locked High Power Microwave amplifier (PHPMA) operating in hybrid theory is proposed and simulated in this paper. The PHPMA is made up of two parts: pre-modulation region and energy exchange region. The pre-modulation region is only used for preliminary modulation of the intense relativistic electron beams (IREB), in which the IREB barely lose any energy. The energy exchange region is used for further modulation of the IREB and realize the beam-wave energy conversion. The PHPMA combines the phase-locking characteristics of amplifiers with the high parameters' tolerance of oscillators. By the proposed Ka-band PHPMA, a HPM with power of 550 MW at the frequency of 29.0 GHz is obtained. The diode voltage, current, magnetic field and the input RF microwave power are 440 kV, 5.35 kA, 1 T and 5 kW, respectively, corresponding to a gain of 50.4 dB.

articleTitle: Research on terahertz near-field irrnging device for broadband electronics based on probe scattering
abstract: In this paper, based on the probe scattering method, a broadband terahertz near-field imaging system of 0.22-0.325THz is designed and built by using the electronic terahertz S parameter test module. The system uses an integrated optical path to transmit and receive terahertz signals effectively. The modulation of terahertz weak evanescent field, which carries the local information of nanometer scale of the sample, is realized through the tapping technology of nano probe. The weak scattering signal of terahertz near field in strong background noise is successfully extracted by using phase-locked amplification technology. The system is used to scan and image the optical disc sample, and the terahertz amplitude imaging and phase imaging of the optical disc sample are realized, the imaging resolution of the disc sample reaches 315nm. The test results are consistent with the atomic force microscope test results, which verifies the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: Influence of the boron-doped layer on the secondary electron emission and morphology of diamond film
abstract: In this paper, diamond films with different thickness of surface boron-doped were prepared by microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition (MPCVD). The effects of the thickness of boron doping layer on surface morphology, crystal quality and secondary electron emission performance of the diamond films were investigated. The results show that the grain size of the film with boron-doping layer is larger than that of the film without boron-doping layer, but the grain size of the film changes little along with the increase of the thickness of the boron-doping layer. Raman spectra show that the crystal quality of the film is the best situation when the thickness of boron doping layer is 0.5 μm and a higher secondary electron emission coefficient of 7.17 at the incident electron energy 200 <tex>$\text{eV}$</tex> is obtained in this case.

articleTitle: Holographic Encryption Applications Using Multichannel Bessel Beam
abstract: Holography provides a method for reconstructing both intensity and phase distribution, that can be used for microwave encryption. In this paper, we report a holographic encryption system featuring a multichannel Bessel beam as encryption key and phase distribution of special characters caring information as the output. The main component of the system consists of two quasi-optical mirrors, and the deformation of the mirrors is optimized by using a modified Katsenelenbaum-Semenov algorithm. The output field of system with different inputs is obtained by commercial software simulation. The feasibility of this encryption method as well as high security is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Research on the Non-Linear Response Characteristic of Magnetron to Anode Voltage Ripple
abstract: This paper proves that a 2.45 GHz band continuous-wave magnetron has the non-linear response characteristic to the frequency of anode voltage ripple. We deduce the output voltage and frequency expression of a free oscillating magnetron under the influence of high-frequency anode voltage ripple. The output reveals that a magnetron can realize frequency shifting of high-frequency ripple. Sidebands will appear on the both sides of the central frequency of free oscillating magnetron. The frequency difference between sideband and the center is the ripple frequency. Finally, an experimental system is accomplished to testify the theoretical derivation. This research is promised to apply to the simultaneous information and power transfer system based on magnetron.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a 90° Compact TE01-Mode Bend Based on the Corrugated Waveguide Structure for Gyrotron Traveling-wave Tube System
abstract: A X-band 90° TE<inf>01</inf>-mode corrugated waveguide bend is designed for the high-power transmission line. To suppress the generation of parasitic modes, a waveguide bend based on the corrugated waveguide is used to minimize the coupling capacity between the operating modes and the undesired modes. The calculation results show that the transmission efficiency of the TE<inf>01</inf> mode is over 95% from 9 to 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-station traveling wave tube aging test information-based system
abstract: In view of some problems exposed by manual monitoring in the existing traveling wave tube aging test, this paper takes the TWT aging test as the research object, combines the instrument communication, data anomaly analysis and composite database system, builds the multi-station TWT automatic aging test and data storage analysis test scheme. The program not only realizes the automatic collection of the data of the traveling wave tube refining, but also the information management of the data of the traveling wave tube aging test.

articleTitle: Investigation of photonic crystal structure for staggered double grating slow wave structure
abstract: A staggered double grid (SDG) slow wave structure (SWS) loaded with photonic crystals (PhC) operating at 220GHz is designed, and the problem of decreasing the dispersion caused by PhC is studied in this paper. In this paper the effects of the filling ratio and period of photonic crystals on the dispersion curve are presented and the SDG SWS loaded with PhC is designed. By observing the S parameter, it can operate stably at 220GHz, and the transmission loss is less than - 20dB. Compared with the traditional SDG SWS, this structure overcomes the mode competition and improves the stability of traveling wave tube (TWT).

Author Keywords: Staggered double grid slow wave structure

articleTitle: A fast MGAWE method based on MORe
abstract: Microwave equipment often needs to get some electromagnetic parameters so that better designs and simulations. At present, transmission parameters of microwave tube can be obtained by fast frequency sweep technologies. Although the traditional multipoint Galerkin asymptotic waveform evaluation (MGAWE) is very popular, it exists some insufficient on the large frequency band and derivation. To remedy the above problems, this paper proposed a fast MGAWE method based on Model Order Reduction (MORe) technology and vector finite element method (FEM). For the global matrix function of FEM, we apply Chebyshev function approximation instead of Taylor expansion, which can avoid derivation. Then we define two error determinations so that can adaptively divide the whole frequency band. To verify the reliability and accuracy of the proposed method, numerical examples are simulated. The results show that this proposed method is in good agreement with HFSS software, which illustrate that the proposed method is effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Phase Synchronization Principle in 5.8 GHz Magnetron Phased Array
abstract: This paper analyzes the influence parameters of the phase control of the magnetron in detail and proposes a method to realize the frequency locking and phase synchronization of the magnetron. The noise-inhibition of the magnetron has made great progress in previous research, and the power and phase can be simultaneously controlled. Based on this principle, the phases of multiple magnetrons are synchronized and successfully applied to phased arrays. A <tex>$2 \times 2$</tex> 5.8GHz magnetron phased array was constructed with a maximum output power of 1680W and the beam-forming experiment of the magnetron phased array was demonstrated for wireless power transfer.

articleTitle: Follower Jamming to UAV FH Communication System Based on Simulink
abstract: With the vigorous rise of the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) market, the “black flight” of UAVs has seriously threatened public safety, flight safety and even air defense safety. Therefore, the research of anti UAV technology is very urgent. The UAV is mainly equipped with the frequency-hopping (FH) communication system which has a strong anti-jamming capability. This paper establishes the structure diagram of the UAV FH communication system based on Simulink. And then the follower jamming of different power and interference dwell ratio (IDR) are set to interfere with the system respectively. We use the error rate to evaluate the interference effect of the model. The simulation results show that in the case of high jamming to signal ratio (JSR), follower jamming can effectively interfere with the UAV FH communication system.

articleTitle: Experiments on a Dual-Frequency, Harmonic, Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator
abstract: Magnetically insulated line oscillators (MILOs) are crossed-field devices that generate high-power microwaves at the design frequencies without the use of external magnets. We present experimental data that demonstrates operation of a dual-frequency, Harmonic, Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator (HMILO). This harmonic operation occurs in L-band (~1 GHz) and S-band (~2 GHz).

articleTitle: Multi-frequency THz source based on Coherent Smith-Purcell Radiation
abstract: Here we present the design of a compact multi-frequency THz source with narrow spectral linewidth based on coherent Smith-Purcell Radiation (SPR). The device generates the 3<sup>rd</sup>, 4th and 5<sup>th</sup> harmonic signals achieving frequency conversion. This work paves a way for compact and high-frequency signal generation by free electrons and SPR scheme.

articleTitle: A New Vertical Structure Gate-All-Around Nano Air Channel Transistor
abstract: A new vertical structure gate-all-around nano-air-channel transistor (GAA-NACT) is proposed in this paper, which can be fabricated by photolithography and deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) with simple process, low cost and excellent consistency. The previous issue of such transistors' gates involved in electron emission was solved by optimizing the distance between the gate and the source-drain. In addition, modifying the gate structure improves gate control capability. The experimental results show that this transistor performs at a low voltage (<2.2V), provides a high drive current <tex>$( > \mathbf{110}\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{A})$</tex> and an on/off ratio of over 10<sup>4</sup>. The transistor has promising applications in vacuum nanoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Recent Activity and Results on Gyro-TWT at the IAP
abstract: An overview of recent researches at the Institute of Applied Physics (IAP) involving the broadband gyrotron-traveling-wave tubes will be presented. A cascade of two helically corrugated waveguide (HCW) gyro-TWTs is under development, one of which possesses high gain whereas the second tube with about 20 dB gain is designed to produce 200–400 kW pulsed power in W-band. A high-gain tube has been “hot” tested in pulsed and CW modes. An appropriate cusp electron gun and an input/output microwave system for the high-power tube have been designed.
