Periodical sequences of short high-peak-power microwave pulses with wide spectrum were generated in HCW gyro-TWT experiments on K-band CW tube with high external reflections and Ka-band pulse tube with a cyclotron saturable absorber in the feedback loop. A recently proposed gyro-TWT using a quasi-optical zigzag-like transmission line enabling amplification within more than octave frequency band (with adjusting the B-field) will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Design of Field Emission Electron Gun for W-Band Photonic Crystal (PhC) based High Power Source
abstract: This article reports, the design of a field emission electron gun for W-band Photonic crystal <tex>$(\mathbf{PhC})$</tex> based high power source. A graphene emitter-based and a Lanthanum Hexaboride <tex>$(\mathbf{LaB}_{6})$</tex> emitter-based electron guns are designed and analyzed using CST particle tracking studio suite. At <tex>$\mathbf{3kV}$</tex> anode voltage, beam current <tex>$> 50\text{mA}$</tex> were achieved for both graphene-based electron gun and <tex>$\mathbf{LaB}_{6}$</tex> based electron gun. The beam transported (100%) <tex>$\geq 10$</tex> mm through the hollow anode with square aperture of 1.8 mm <tex>$\mathrm{x}\ 1.8$</tex> mm without applying any magnetic field for both the design.

articleTitle: Exploration of new Self-limiting Atomic Layer Etching Methods for Molybdenum
abstract: In recent years, molybdenum (Mo) is used more and more in the semiconductor industry as a low-resistivity metal material. The Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) process is commonly used to obtain molybdenum thin films. The exploration of molybdenum thin films’ etching method will allow more flexibility in its applications. At present, the etching technology commonly used in industry is mainly atomic layer etching. Atomic layer etching is an advanced technique that can precisely control the amount of material etched. The key to achieving this technique is to divide the etching process into two steps: modification and removal. In this paper, a self-limiting molybdenum etching method based on oxidative and denature-wet removal combined treatment is obtained by comparing 7 schemes.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Temperature Plasma Generator
abstract: The excitation modes of plasma usually include gas discharge, dielectric barrier discharge, capacitor discharge and so on. Atmospheric pressure nonequilibrium plasma can be produced under non-vacuum conditions, which makes plasma in biomedicine, sewage treatment, aerospace, food sterilization and other directions have more applications. In this paper, a small size low-temperature plasma jet device is proposed. Based on the principle of gas discharge, the device is simulated and then tested. It is found that the voltage required to excite plasma, the length of plasma after excitation and the maintenance time are different under different cathode tip lengths. Based on the design size of the device, when the length of cathode is 18.5mm, atmospheric pressure is 0.5atm, voltage is 85V,the effect of producing low-temperature plasma is remarkable.

articleTitle: Research on parallel algorithms for high-power microwave devices based on GPU
abstract: In this paper, on the CHIPIC-3D software platform independently developed by the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, the original electromagnetic field algorithm and particle simulation algorithm in the software are improved, and the CUDA-based particle simulation core computing module is completed, which can accelerate the simulation of high-power microwave devices in a heterogeneous CPU-GPU manner. Finally, taking the rectangular waveguide (GUIDE) and the relativistic return wave tube (RBWO) as examples, the simulation test shows that the electromagnetic field algorithm can achieve up to 36 times the acceleration, and the particle simulation algorithm can achieve up to 10 times the acceleration.

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigation on a W-Band High-Power Gyrotron
abstract: The theoretical investigation of a 94GHz high-power gyrotron with output power of l00kW is presented in this paper. TE<inf>03</inf> mode is selected as the operating mode. The efficiency of the electron beam wave interaction is calculated based on the self-consistent nonlinear theory. In addition, the efficiency of the operating mode and the other two main parasitic modes versus the operating magnetic field Bo is analyzed. Finally, PIC simulation is carried out.

articleTitle: THz Pulse Compressors
abstract: Quasioptical resonant rings with internal switches offer the possibility of generating high power output pulses of short temporal duration from lower power, longer duration pulses. A low power example at 250 GHz with a gain of 16 is described along with plans for a higher power demonstration at 110 GHz. Efficient operation of a compressor will also require a full understanding of the properties of the switch.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of a Low Perveance and High Current Density Pierce Gun for Ka-Band TWT
abstract: This paper presents an optimized design of a pierce gun for Ka-Band TWTs. Low-frequency TWTs like Ka-Band can reach powers up to tens of kilowatts and thus require high current, low perveance, and high-density electron beams. A pierce gun having a beam radius of 0.6 mm, perveance of <tex>$\mathbf{0.7}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \boldsymbol{P}$</tex> and current density of <tex>$\mathbf{7} \boldsymbol{A} /\boldsymbol{mm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> has been proposed in this paper. A stranded electromagnetic focusing coil has been used to provide the necessary magnetic field for beam focusing.

articleTitle: Research on Emission Performance of TiO2 Modified Graphite
abstract: Graphite was widely used in explosive emission cathode due to its stability operation, long life, and low gas emission, but the high emission threshold limits the performance of graphite cathode. This paper proposed a scheme of TiO<inf>2</inf> composited graphite. The First Principles Simulation in Materials Studio and the tracking simulation in CST Studio are carried out to verify the low emission threshold of TiO<inf>2</inf> modified graphite. The results show that doping of TiO<inf>2</inf> can decrease the work function of composite cathode materials and can effectively reduce the emission threshold of graphite. Especially, the effect of reducing emission threshold is more obvious with the increase of TiO<inf>2</inf> doping proportion.

articleTitle: Formation and Electromagnetic radiation of ion-focused virtual cathode oscillation
abstract: Due to the ability of enhancing the space-charge-limited current, the ion-focus regime of electron beam-plasma system can lead to virtual cathode (VC) oscillations with a much higher frequency than that in vacuum. Based on particle-in-cell simulation including Mont-Carlo collision model, the self-consistent formation and radiation process of the ion-focused VC is studied. It is found that the virtual cathode has a multistage structure caused by the plasma wave modulation, and an ion cavity where almost all the plasma electrons are evacuated is found at the second stage, which is significant for electron trapping. Under the demonstrated parameters, the radiation frequency of VC reaches the sub-terahertz band.

articleTitle: High Density ECR Discharge with Gyrotron Plasma Heating as a Multipurpose Ion Source
abstract: The use of the powerful millimeter wavelength range gyrotron radiation for the plasma heating allowed us to create a concept of a unique gasdynamic ion sources at IAP RAS. The gasdynamic electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) ion source is a type of the device in which the ionization efficiency is achieved primarily due to a high plasma density. Because of a high particle collision rate, the confinement is determined by a gasdynamic plasma outflow from a magnetic trap. Due to high efficiency of resonant heating, electrons gain energy significantly higher than that in inductively or capacitively coupled plasmas. As a consequence of such a parameter combination, the gasdynamic ECR plasma can be a unique source of low to medium charged ions, providing a high current and an ultimate quality of an ion beam. One of the most demanded directions of its application today is a development of high-current proton injectors for modern accelerators and neutron sources of different intensities.

articleTitle: Development of MBK based LINAC in BVERI
abstract: With the help of high efficiency klystron technique, 2-3MW multi-beam klystron (MBK) under the voltage of 40-50kV can be achieved. Along with the integration of compact modulator, dimension and weight of whole accelerator module is acceptable for installation inside the gantry or cabinet of LINAC system. BVERI has dedicated in application of MBK based LINAC recent years, remarkable advantages come along with the mechanism of klystron. Product series and operation parameters are given, further work and potential application scenario are also been discussed.

articleTitle: Micro-focus electron source based on high current density carbon nanotube emitters
abstract: A high current density micro-focus cathode based on carbon nanotube (CNT) field emission was developed. The CNT film was grown directly on the nickel alloy substrate with a diameter of <tex>$\mathbf{70}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> by chemical vapor deposition. The effect of the cathode-grid spacing on the field emission properties was investigated, and improved field emission performances were demonstrated for the 1.4 mm spacing with a lower threshold field of <tex>$\mathbf{1.6}\ \mathbf{V}/\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> and higher emission current (up to 19 A/cm<sup>2</sup>) comparing with spacing of 0.4 mm, indicating that increasing the electrode spacing could enhance the field emission characteristics of the CNT cathode. The X-ray tube based on the CNT micro-focus electron source reached the imaging resolution of about <tex>$\mathbf{80}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of High-Power Annular Beam Extended Interaction Device
abstract: In order to develop high power millimeter wave and terahertz radiation sources, the simulation research of high-current over-mode annular beam extended interaction device is carried out in this paper. By embedding a concentric metal cylinder with periodic array holes in a circular waveguide with periodic radial grooves, the radial electric field distribution of TM<inf>02</inf>-like mode is optimized. The annular electron beam interacts with <tex>$TM_{02}$</tex> mode between the cylinder and the waveguide. In the output section, the microwave is coupled to extractor in TM<inf>01</inf> mode through a circular aperture in the axial direction. The applied voltage is 28.6 kV, the current is 1 A, the inside radius of the electron beam is 2.54 mm, the outside radius is 2.75 mm, and the current density is <tex>$28.65\ \mathrm{A}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>. The particle in cell simulation results show that the device can generate 9.38 kW at 0.1 THz, and the beam-wave interaction efficiency is 32.81%.

articleTitle: Theoretical Study on Life Ion Flow via Cell Membrane Under Symmetrical and Unsymmetrical Terahertz Stimulation
abstract: Terahertz stimulation causes the information transmission of the cells. It is found that the stimulation can activate voltage-gated ion channels and hydrophilic pores in cell membrane. However, the effect of the hydrophilic pores on the ion flow via voltage-gated ion channels is unclear. This paper theoretically studies the ion flow via the ion channels and the hydrophilic pores under both symmetrical and unsymmetrical terahertz stimulations. Based on the study results, the calcium ion flow via hydrophilic pores causes significant increase in intracellular calcium concentration under the unsymmetrical terahertz stimulation. In contrast, hydrophilic pores have no impact on the voltage-gated ion channel flow under symmetrical terahertz stimulation, since there is no formation of the pores. And the power dissipation of cell metabolic energy in calcium flow via the physiological calcium channels is pretty low at around the level of <tex>$\boldsymbol{10^{-18}}$</tex> W. The results lay the basis for further studies for the applications in future artificial intelligence like terahertz-rate brain-machine communications.

articleTitle: Electric Properties of GaAs PCSSs with Ni/Ge/Au/Ni/Au Electrodes under Different Annealing Conditions
abstract: The fabricating process of photoconductive semiconductor switch (PCSS) directly influences the electric properties. In order to determine appropriate process parameters for rapid thermal annealing (RTA) for GaAs PCSSs with <tex>$\text{Ni}/\text{Ge}/\text{Au}/\text{Ni}/\text{Au}$</tex> electrodes, a test route is designed, and the tests about contact properties of Metal/SI-GaAs, off-state and on-state characteristics of the PCSSs were performed, separately. The results show that the PCSS with a higher hold-off voltage and a lower on-state resistance can be obtained by RTA at 400 <tex>${}^{\circ} \mathbf{C}$</tex>, compared to other temperatures. Meanwhile, the results also indicate that the test route is effective and comprehensive for determining the final process parameter directly.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra-Wideband G-Band Gyro-TWT with Nonlinearly Tapered Circuit
abstract: A collaborative optimization method is proposed to achieve effective wave-particle interaction over an ultra-wideband frequency through a nonlinearly tapered circuit and magnetic field profile, without limit of strict grazing magnetic field along the circuit position. Taking the design of a G-band gyrotron travelling wave tube (gyro-Twt)amplifier as an example, an output power of above 40 kW range from 195 GHz to 237 GHz is theoretically predicted. Three-dimentional particle-in-cell (3D-PIC) simulation demonstration is carried out and a stable output power of above 20 kW is observed, with an instantaneous bandwidth of 42 GHz that agrees well with the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Investigation on Scadium Thin Films on Dispenser Cathodes
abstract: The emission performance and mechanism of Ba-W cathode coated with Sc film were studied. Results show that the cathode coated with Sc layer 200 nm in thickness shows better performance. After heat treatment at <tex>$\boldsymbol{1500 \ ^{\circ}} \mathbf{C}$</tex> in hydrogen, the cathode could provide an emission current density of <tex>$\boldsymbol{21.07}\mathbf{A}/\mathbf{cm^{2}}$</tex> at <tex>$\boldsymbol{1150\ ^{\circ}}\mathbf{C}_{\mathbf{b}}$</tex>. The surface analysis shows that Sc is partially oxidized during heat treatment, indicating that oxidation improves performance. The experiment results are consistent with the DFT calculated results, where the work function of 25% O-25% Ba adsorbed on the Sc surface is the lowest, which is 1.4877 eV, 1.8228 eV and 1.8210 eV on the Sc (002), Sc (100) and Sc (101) respectively.

articleTitle: Symmetric Vlasov-type antenna for High Power Microwave applications
abstract: We present a novel Vlasov-type antenna operating at <tex>$2.5$</tex> GHz and composed of a circular waveguide with a double bevel-cut. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna is capable of providing a wider emission angle if compared to standard Vlasov configurations, while still maintaining an adequate gain level. For this reason, it could be of interest for those High-Power Microwave (HPM) applications in which a larger area need to be covered by the EM field.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Window for D Band Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: The diamond window was designed to meet the requirements of D band traveling wave tube (TWT) for the vacuum environment maintenance and the low loss transmission of RF signal in a wide band. The basic pill-box structure was adopted, and the main structural parameters were determined through parameters optimization by using CST microwave studio. As a simulation results, the window shows a good RF performance in full D band(110-170GHz), moreover, the VSWR of the window is less than 1.1 and the attenuation of the window is about 0.1dB within 123-168GHz.

articleTitle: Research on the Processing Technology of RF Shield Bellows for High Energy Photon Source Storage Ring
abstract: The RF shield bellows of storage ring is composed of circular structure and circular main body with slit structure. For every shield finger there is a mating spring finger that exerts <tex>$123\pm 25$</tex> grams of contact force. The surface of SS stube and spring finger is silver plated with a thickness of <tex>$5-10\mu m$</tex>. The silver plated spring finger has a good self-lubricating function. The spring finger, contact finger and SS stube form a good friction structure. The internal ultra-high vacuum degree of the shield bellows is better than <tex>$1.6\times 10^{-10}Torr$</tex>, and the vacuum leakage rate of the weld and the shield bellows is better than <tex>$1\times 10^{-11}\ Torr-L/s$</tex>.

articleTitle: Simulation of the starting process of a 94GHz cyclotron oscillator
abstract: A three-dimensional numerical simulation of the starting process of a 94GHz gyrotron is carried out carefully, based on the theories of PIC and electron cyclotron resonance maser, while the TE6,2 mode is selected as the operating mode of the gyrotron. The parameters such as the beam voltage, beam current and beam radius of the guiding center are set according to the measured data of the 94 GHz gyrotron in the National Key Laboratory of Science and Technology on Vacuum Electronics. As a result, an output power of the operating mode of 84kW, corresponding to 33.5% efficiency and an oscillation frequency of 94 GHz have been achieved with the working magnetic field of 3.56Tesla. The output power is in good agreement with the experimental test results, which is also consistent with the calculation results using the stable beam wave interaction code established by us.

articleTitle: Calculation of Qualification Gain for Terahertz Antennas
abstract: At present, terahertz (THz) technology is a hot research topic all over the world. As a key link of THz system, THz antenna has also attracted intense attentions. It is meaningful to recognize the qualification of the gain is good or bad for THz antenna in a specific environment. Under the same distance and transmission loss (TL), the requirements for THz antenna gain are calculated and analyzed with the microwave antenna (2.45GHz) as a reference based on the free space transmission loss model. This paper can offer a kind of method to judge the qualification of the gain for the THz antenna. In the wireless communication system, the gain of antennas is required for a definite infimum in a specific environment generally, various types of antennas are selected to meet the certain requirement for gain. This paper emphatically studies the gain of THz antenna, it is not limited to a specific antenna model, it is suitable for any antenna model.

articleTitle: Study on logarithmic dual gradient helix slow wave structure
abstract: In this paper, a novel logarithmic dual gradient helix slow wave structure (SWS) is proposed. Driven by a 6900 V, 50 mA pencil electron beam, the output power of the logarithmic dual gradient SWS circuit has been analyzed by the simulation tools. The maximum output power of the logarithmic dual gradient helix SWS circuit can reach 52 W. The output gain comes over 23.5 dB over 33~40 GHz. The electronic efficiency of the 50 mm long novel SWS circuit can be increased to more than 14%, which is a 50% improvement compared with the conventional helix SWS.

articleTitle: Free-Electron-Driven Terahertz Laser on a Micro-Nano-Grating Dielectric Waveguide
abstract: Recently, there has been a growing interest in integrated terahertz (THz) sources for various applications in communications, spectroscopy and sensing. Traditional THz sources are too large to adapt to the development of THz technology on chip, so miniaturized THz sources are urgently needed. A free-electron-driven THz laser based on a micro-nano-grating structure is elucidated in this paper. To achieve miniaturized terahertz sources, we study achievable THZ radiation from electrons and an array of electrons atop a micro-nano-grating dielectric waveguide. In our study, 35-keV electrons generates <tex>$\mathbf{9.5}-\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> THz radiation at the Bragg resonance of a <tex>$\mathbf{175}-\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> long silicon grating with a <tex>$\mathbf{1.5}-\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> thickness and <tex>$\mathbf{1.75}-\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> period. The vertical distance between the electron and the structure is 550 nanometers. The work is promising for developing efficient on-chip THz radiation sources and boosts advanced THz applications.

articleTitle: A Broad Bandwidth Microwave Window Based on Metamaterial
abstract: In this paper, a low voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) broad bandwidth microwave window based on metamaterial was presented for W-band gyro traveling wave tubes (Gyro-TWTs). The microwave window is designed on a dielectric surface, where the dielectric is boron nitride (BN). A sandwich-like structure is adopted, the top and the bottom layers are dielectrics, and the middle layer is metal. The thickness of each piece of dielectric is 0.4mm, and the thickness of metal is 0.0008mm. In the cold-test simulation, it achieves a bandwidth of 13.5GHz with VSWR below 1.2 at W-band, which is broader than that of pure BN dielectric.

articleTitle: R-band Backward Wave Oscillator based on Metamaterial Structure and Multi-electron Beams
abstract: R-band backward wave oscillator (BWO) based on metamaterial (MTMs) and Multi-electron Beams is presented as a novel high-power terahertz radiation source. We analyzed and retrieved the effective permittivity and permeability of the slow wave structure (SWS) by HFSS. And the Particle-in-cell (PIC) is performed to obtain the beam-wave interaction. Finally, the results show the radiation source can generate 65W output power with the interaction efficiency of 6% at the frequency of 230GHz on the condition of the beam voltage of 35kV and total current of 30mA.

articleTitle: Study on Reliability of Long-HV-OFF-Mode of Cathode Assembly in Space Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, the water-cooled anode diode is used as the test carrier to study the effect of different Long-High-Voltage on-off mode on the reliability of M-type cathode life. The results show that the cathode operating temperature is <tex>$1000^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, DC working load at 1 A/cm<sup>2</sup>, high-voltage on-off 31000 times(working time 6000h), the cathode emission current does not fall. The cathode operating temperature is <tex>$1040^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, DC working load at 4 A/cm<sup>2</sup>, working time 2000h, the cathode emission current drops 1.8%,and the cathode operating temperature is <tex>$1040^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, DC working load at 4 A/cm<sup>2</sup>, High-Voltage on-off 10000 times(working time 2000h), the cathode emission current drops 3.73 %, and the life reliability influence factor is about 0.482. These influencing parameters can be used as reliability factors for the selection of M-type cathode by starboard traveling wave tube in Long-High- Voltage on-off mode.

articleTitle: A Mode Perturbation Scheme for Suppressing Upper Sideband Oscillations of Sheet Beam Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: The problem of sideband oscillation has been a persistent challenge in the development of power and bandwidth for traveling wave tubes, particularly for high-power sheet beam traveling wave tubes (SB-TWTs). In this paper, a method of mode perturbation is proposed to suppress oscillation by interfering with the interaction field. To address this issue, a modified structure is designed, which differs from the traditional double staggered vanes slow-wave structure (SDV-SWS). The modified structure enables the high-frequency cut-off mode to couple a stronger transverse electric field component, replacing the original longitudinal component, thus avoiding the problem of upper sideband oscillation and freeing up bandwidth.

articleTitle: Optimization of Phase Nonlinear Characteristics of Folded Waveguide Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: When millimeter wave folded waveguide (FWG) traveling wave tube (TWT) operates near saturation, it is usually accompanied by some nonlinear phenomena. These nonlinear distortions generated in the process of beam-wave interaction will lead to phenomena such as phase distortion, which will reduce the output performance of FWG TWT and seriously affect the overall performance of the communication system. In this paper, a genetic algorithm is introduced to optimize the phase nonlinearity (AM/PM) of the FWG TWT, and an E-band FWG TWT is used as an example. Finally, the optimization results are given. The results show that the AM/PM conversion coefficient of the FWG TWT is reduced by 88.9% and the efficiency is improved by 36.6% at the optimum frequency point. In addition, the AM/PM in the bandwidth is reduced by more than 16% and the efficiency is also improved by more than 21.8%. These optimization results indicate that the use of genetic algorithm can provisionally guide the AM/PM structure optimization design of FWG TWT.

articleTitle: Application of Single Crystal Diamond in the Microwave Window of 3mm Wide Band TWT
abstract: Based on the requirements of low loss and sealing reliability for the microwave Windows of 3mm wide band TWT, the application technology of single crystal diamond was studied in this paper. The sealing quality of single crystal diamond was evaluated by microfocus industrial CT, SEM, EDS and other analytical methods.

articleTitle: High-Q Cavity With Distributed Bragg Reflector for Second-Harmonic Gyrotrons Driven by Low-Power Electron Beams
abstract: A cavity with distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) resonator is considered as a new design solution intended to improve output efficiencies of terahertz gyrotrons. The DBR is formed by a cylindrical sapphire tube and a hollow layer. It is optimized to provide ultra-low ohmic losses of a selected operating mode due to field shielding of the metal resonator wall. It is shown that the frequency of this mode and its coupling with an electron beam are slightly affected by the DBR. It is found that the DBR resonator initiates minor mode conversion, resulting in high output purity of the operating mode. Using a second-harmonic 0.5-THz gyrotron powered by a 1-kW electron beam as an example, it is shown that the sapphire DBR enables 10-fold increase in the peak output efficiency from 1% to 10%.

articleTitle: Research of a high average power G-band pulsed traveling wave tube
abstract: As Terahertz application technology developed, the research for G-band folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube (FWTWT) requires higher power in a wider band. The design and experiment on G-band pulsed FWTWT was presented, including electronic-optical system and transformed folded waveguide slow wave structure (TFWSWS). By the measurement, the G-band pulsed TFWTWT can reach over 50W maximum output power with 3GHz – 3dB bandwidth at 50% duty cycle. The average output power is 25.7W in 216. <tex>$5\text{GHz}$</tex>. The maximum efficiency of all tube is improved above 8.5%.

Author Keywords: transformed folded waveguide slow wave structure

articleTitle: High-order Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Vacuum Electron Device Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method, which is also called as the hybridizable DG (HDG) method, and successfully applies it to solve the drift-diffusion model in vacuum electron devices. Compared with classical numerical discretization schemes such as the Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme, this method permits arbitrary high-order node basis functions thus decreasing the requirement on mesh in the vortex electromagnetic wave radar electron device modeling, such as transmitter. The performance of the in-house solver is evaluated through the simulation of a PIN diode in the vortex electromagnetic wave radar transmitter. The result demonstrates that the proposed method possesses stability and convergence.

articleTitle: Development and Modeling of a V-Band Traveling-Wave Tube With a Microstrip Meander-Line Slow-Wave Structure
abstract: In this paper, we present the results aimed at development of a miniaturized traveling-wave tube (TWT) amplifier with a microstrip meander-line (MML) slow-wave structure (SWS) operating at V band. The MML SWS on quartz substrate was designed and fabricated using the technology based on laser ablation and magnetron sputtering. Cold-test electromagnetic parameters of the SWS are measured and compared with the simulations. An electron gun with high compression of a low-voltage (5 kV) sheet electron beam is designed and beam transmission in a uniform magnetic field is studied. Hot-test operation of the TWT is simulated by a 3-D particle-in-cell (PIC) code. The simulations predict small-signal gain of 28 dB and nearly 14 W saturated power.

articleTitle: Study on 1THz Staggered Double-Grating Backward Wave Oscillator
abstract: Backward wave oscillator (BWO) is one of the ideal devices for generating terahertz wave. BWO has many advantages, such as tunable frequency, high efficiency, and high frequency. Therefore, BWO is very popular in military and satellite fields. In our current work, we have carried out research on BWO operating at a frequency of 1 THz. We use a staggered double-grating structure with circular electron beam channels as high-frequency structure. When the operation voltage of the electron beam is 25 kV, the beam current is 15 mA, the stable output power of the BWO is 178mW, and the oscillation frequency is 1.044THz.

articleTitle: Frequency-Tunable Sub-THz Gyrotron with External Reflectors: Design and Simulations
abstract: We describe the design of a frequency-tunable gyrotron based on a combination of a low-Q irregular cavity and a frequency-tunable narrow-band external reflector. The frequency tuning in this device is provided by mechanical changing the operating frequency of the reflector placed outside the vacuum zone. The cavity profile is optimized from the point of view of ensuring broadband frequency tuning when the reflection of the output wave signal is provided. At the same time, self-excitation of any wave should be absent in the operating ranges of the magnetic field and the electron current in the case when the reflection is absent. The design is based on detailed simulations predicting possibilities for creation of a gyrotron with high (tens of percent) efficiencies provided in a wide 125–137 GHz) band of the continuous frequency tuning.

articleTitle: Modeling of a Complex Cavity Resonator with Unequal Cavity Lengths for the Frequency-Tunable Sub-THz Gyrotron
abstract: The possibility of improving mode selection properties and enhance of the frequency tunability by using the complex cavity resonator with unequal cavity lengths are considered. Second-harmonic 0.4 THz gyrotron is studied. Results of calculation of cold cavity electromagnetic parameters are presented.

articleTitle: A K-Band Waveguide With Integrated Reconfigurable Circular Polarizer
abstract: In the communication system, a device that can flexibly switch the polarization mode with broadband is necessary. In this paper, a K-Band waveguide with integrated reconfigurable circular polarize is proposed. It can switch between left-handed and right-handed polarization modes. To expand the operating bandwidth, a new waveguide structure is introduced at the output of device. The simulation results shows that a broadband operating bandwidth of 17.5-21.5 GHz, with the return loss better than 20 dB, and the axial ration under 1.1 dB, is obtained. The proposed integrated reconfigurable circular polarizer features broadband, high efficiency, and easy to matching.

articleTitle: A field emission performance testing device with adjustable electrode spacing
abstract: This work presents a device that can adjust electrode spacing inside a vacuum system to evaluate the field emission characteristics of the carbon nanotube array cathode grown on a stainless steel substrate. It was made by coaxial connection of the rear end of a screw micrometer, which acts as the anode, with a stepper motor. The distance between the anode and the cathode was controlled by altering the pitch of the stepper motor with an angle precision of 1 degree. Therefore, the electrode separation can be tuned in the range of 0∼15mm, at 1.388 μm incremental steps. Comparing with devices with a fixed electrode spacing, the advantage is that this device allows continuous regulation of the electrode spacing after it is placed in a vacuum system to test the emission properties under various electrical parameters in one process thus avoiding repeated breaking of the vacuum environment. Therefore, test efficiency is improved, hence saving manpower, material resources, testing time and greatly reducing the cost of experimentation. This device is simple in structure and relatively easy to prepare0

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of relativistic Backward-wave tubes
abstract: In this paper, a Ku band relativistic backwave oscillator based on annular strong current explosion emission is proposed. The modulation of ring relativistic electron beam is realized by adjusting the distance between anode and cathode of diode, adding reflection cavity in front of slow wave structure, adding drift section between two slow wave structure, adjusting the size of slow wave structure and so on. The numerical simulation results show that the Ku band microwave output power is 1.38 Gw, the frequency is about 12.5 Ghz, and the efficiency is about 40% under the conditions of 532 kV, 3150 A and 0.6 T.

articleTitle: Suppression of parasitic modes in gyrotrons with an additional resonator coil
abstract: The mode competition is a key factor limiting the development of gyrotrons towards higher power and higher frequencies. In the study, we propose to use a small additional solenoid to vary the magnetic field during the startup process to suppress the parasitic modes. The results show that by applying such a scheme, the desired mode can be selectively excited in a dense mode spectrum.

articleTitle: Wide-band Pulsed Travelling Wave Tube Amplifier of Kilowatt Scale for Space Application
abstract: To satisfy the requirements of new generation high resolution remote sensing satellite, the output power of pulse travelling wave tube (TWT) amplifier in space should be raised from hundred watt scale to kilowatt scale, while the bandwidth should be raised from MHz to GHz. For satellite ground applications, this paper proposed a pulsed TWT amplifier for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems, which achieved up to 3500 W radio frequency output power and operated at 8.2 GHz to 11.8 GHz. The pulsed TWT amplifier is composed of electronic power conditioner (EPC) and travelling wave tube (TWT). And to improve power density and solve the elements overheating problem, the parallel interleaved power converter topology is adopted to the EPC, which uses the power from storage battery of the satellite, can realize the high voltage converter of travelling wave tube, modulate the electron beam of the travelling wave tube, amplify the wide band microwave signal and finally realize the adjustment of repetition frequency and pulse width in orbit. To achieve the long life operation and stability of the TWT amplifier, as well as the satellite, the adaptive method is adopted to modulate the voltage in the electron gun. Finally, the experimental prototype is designed to verify the performance of the proposed TWT amplifier.

articleTitle: A Dual-Beam 0.1THz Extended Interaction Klystron Amplifier
abstract: A 0.1THz pencil beam klystron amplifier with three extended interaction cavities has been presented in this manuscript. A novel dual-beam tunnel (DBT) cavity is adopted to replace the single-beam tunnel (SBT) cavity benefiting the improvement of the driven beam current. The electromagnetic features of both cavities have been analyzed and compared. Then, the output power and electronic efficiency of both the high-frequency circuits employing the single-beam tunnel and novel dual-beam tunnel cavities are verified by PIC simulation. Driven by 5 mW RF signal, the output power of the single-beam tunnel circuit reaches 144W at 100GHz, and the dual-beam tunnel mode enhances to 450W when the electron beam is 17.3kV and 0.28A per tunnel. The simulation results prove that the novel dual-beam tunnel design, compatible with a higher driven current, can help to increase the electronic efficiency to 4.64% from the 2.97% of the single-beam tunnel.

articleTitle: Eigen analysis and optimization of rising sun anode of magnetron using Backtracking search algorithm
abstract: Magnetron device designers are facing the challenge of finding the exact design parameters of the resonating structure with empirical equations alone. In the present study, an optimization MATLAB code of the Backtracking search algorithm (BSA) is used to find the exact design parameters of the rising sun bare anode block of a magnetron operating at a frequency of 2.998 GHz. Eigen-mode simulation of CST Studio Suite is used to find the suitable type of strapping case to solve the mode competition issue. BSA is validated with a Particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The obtained design parameters with BSA are slot width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(W_{rs})$</tex>, longer slot length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r_{1})$</tex>, and shorter slot length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r_{2})$</tex> which are 2 mm, 37.4 mm, and 34.4 mm.

articleTitle: A 0.65-THz Traveling Wave Tube Based on Staggered Double L-shaped Vane SWS
abstract: A staggered double L-shaped vane slow-wave-structure (SDLV-SWS), which is suitable for the sheet electron beam with small aspect ratio and is beneficial to improve the interaction of electron in the edge region of the beam, is proposed for 0.65-THz traveling wave tubes (TWTs). By using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, the SDLV-SWS shows the output power of 1.8 W with the operating voltage of 21.9 kV, current of 10.6 mA, and the corresponding gain is 35.2 dB. Besides, the output power is over than 1 W in the frequency range of 646–650 GHz, and the 3dB-bandwidth is more than 5 GHz.

articleTitle: Dielectric loss analysis of anisotropically conducting tape helix slow wave Structure in travelling wave tube
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of dielectric losses obtained through the coldwave field analysis of anisotropically conducting tape helix supported by lossy dielectric rods in travelling wave tubes (TWT). The electromagnetic field expressions are derived through field approach using Maxwell's equations and vector Helmholtz's equations by solving the complex constants through boundary conditions. Through the application of lossy dielectric permittivity in the resultant axial electric field, the shunt capacitance and the shunt conductance per unit length are obtained. The presence of lossy dielectric support rods in the slow wave structure (SWS) results in attenuation of the propagating electromagnetic wave. The attenuation constant obtained through the present analysis has been compared with the published models and experimental results. The effect of the frequency and temperature is also studied for X-Ku band and Q- band travelling wave tube amplifiers.

articleTitle: Design of Two-stage Flat-roofed Sine Waveguide SWS for a 6kW Level Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: A flat-roofed sine waveguide for Ka-band traveling wave tube is designed in this paper, in order to analyze its beam wave interaction in such frequency band. For increasing the output power and suppressing oscillatory signal, this structure adopts the two-stage structure and the phase velocity jump technology. PIC method is used to analyze the beam wave interaction and the simulation results show that the model has the advantages of wide bandwidth and high output power. In the bandwidth of 32-36GHz, the output power of the structure is greater than 6000W, the gain is above 33.01dB, and the minimum electronic efficiency is 13%.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of 1.2 MW Long Pulse Klystron for CSNS-II*
abstract: A 1.2 MW long pulse klystron operating at 648 MHz has been designed and simulated for CSNS-II at Institute of High Energy Physics. In this paper, a triode thermionic electron gun with modulating anode has been designed. A beam current of 19.5 A is obtained at operating voltage of 97 kV with cathode current density of 0.5 A/cm<sup>2</sup>. Then, the beam-wave interaction region that determines klystron characteristics has been designed and optimized. The full 3-dimensional particle-in-cell simulation of the whole klystron in CST indicates that the klystron efficiency is up to 67% using a second harmonic cavity. Finally, the microwave design of cavities for interaction section is described in detail. So far, the manufacturing of the klystron has been completed. The high-power test will be carried out in the first half of 2023.

articleTitle: Improved Synthesis of Quasi-Optical Launchers Used in Injection Locked Gyrotrons
abstract: The paper reports the improvement of the methods for the synthesis of launchers for high power gyrotrons at KIT in the period from 2018 to the present. The spectrum reconstruction method has been developed to greatly increase the curvature radii of numerically optimized launcher wall perturbations in order to reduce stray radiation. The method for the design of Denisov-type launchers has been developed for the conversion of co- and counter rotating modes in the same launcher. The design method for hybrid-type launchers has also been improved for the conversion of co- and counter-rotating modes.

articleTitle: Study of a cold cathode electron gun for THz traveling wave tube
abstract: Based on the field emission test results of the single wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) cold cathode, a cold cathode electron gun for terahertz (THz) traveling wave tube (TWT) was studied. The simulation results showed that the radius of the electron beam could be well confined within 0.05 mm when the peak value of the axial magnetic field (Br) of the periodic permanent magnet (PPM) focusing system was set as 0.8 Tesla (T). The beam waist radius was about 0.014mm, and the area compression ratio was 13. The designed cold cathode electron gun could be used in some miniaturized THz TWTs.

articleTitle: Smith-Purcell Radiation by a Two Layer Grating Structure
abstract: Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR) is generated when an electron passes near a periodic structure. Two-layer gratings are proposed to enhance SPR by improving electromagnetic coupling. Injection of an electron beam could induce more dipole oscillations in the two-layer grating structure compared to one-layer grating, leading to an increase of radiation intensity and a decrease on the starting current. Using particle-in-cell simulations, two-layer gratings have been shown to enhance SPR growth rates and reduce Smith-Purcell backward wave oscillators' start currents.

articleTitle: Research on Variable Temperature Reflectivity Measurement System of Stealth Coating
abstract: In this paper, a measurement system for reflectivity of stealth coating in variable temperature environment is proposed to study the microwave absorbing properties of stealth coating at different temperatures. The system can heat the lower surface of the stealth coating from room temperature to 500 °C, and the system is equipped with two ultra-wideband double ridged horn antennas, which can be used to test the microwave reflectivity of the stealth coating in the 2–18 GHz frequency band. The system measured the reflectivity of the stealth coating at 50 °C, 100 °C, 300 °C and 500 °C respectively. The results show that the reflectivity will gradually decrease when the temperature of the stealth coating increases, and its wave absorption performance will deteriorate.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Megawatt-Class Gyro-TWT Based on Rectangular Dielectric-Loaded Circuit
abstract: In this paper, a gyrotron traveling wave tube (gyro-Twt) based on a rectangular dielectric-loaded circuit (RDLC) is investigated and analyzed to generate the megawatt-class output power. The novel RDLC with a large aspect ratio can effectively decrease the current density of electrons due to the operating frequency of TE<inf>01</inf> mode is only determined by the narrow side. A Ka-band RDLC with an aspect ratio of 6.95 is designed, and the pulsed operation results indicate that the device driven by a 60 kV, 50 A electron beam can produce a maximum pulsed peak power of 1.13 MW, corresponding to an efficiency of <tex>$\sim \mathbf{37}.\mathbf{7}\%$</tex>, a saturated gain of 51.5 dB at 34 GHz. The 3 dB bandwidth is 4.5 GHz, and more than 1 MW output power is achieved in 33.5-36 GHz. The design provides a possible approach for developing gyro-TWTs with megawatt-class output power.

articleTitle: Investigation of Overmoded Brewster Window for Terahertz Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, the overmoded Brewster window for terahertz traveling wave tube is investigated, and good transmission characteristics are achieved in the frequency range of 0.9-1.1 THz. In order to analyze the influence of fabrication and assembly errors on the transmission, the model is simulated with different conditions of the thickness and the tilted angle of the window slice. The simulation results show that it is able to achieve good transmission characteristics with tilted angle error within <tex>$\pm 2^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> and thickness error within <tex>$\boldsymbol{\pm 0.01}$</tex> mm. Thus, the overmoded Brewster window has some tolerance for dimensional errors and is suitable for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Study on 0.65THz EIKs operating at π- and 2π- modes
abstract: The beam-wave interaction length is one of the key issues in designing THz extended interaction klystrons (EIKs). Four types of 0.65 THz EIKs with input and output cavities operating in <tex>$2 \pi$</tex> -mode are analyzed. The first type with three <tex>$2\pi$</tex> -mode idler cavities; the second type with three <tex>$\pi$</tex> - mode idler cavities; the third type with two <tex>$2\pi$</tex> -mode idler cavities and a feedback; the last type with two <tex>$\pi$</tex> -mode idler cavities and a feedback. The particle-in-cell (PIC) results show that the output power is 1.125 W, 1.116W, 0.845 W and 0.813 W under input power of 1 mW and an ideal beam of 25.3 kV and 20 mA. The interaction lengths of four type EIKs are 25.61 mm, 21.11 mm, 16.65mm and 13.87 mm, respectively.

articleTitle: Study on high-gain reflectarray antenna for X-band based on phase gradient ultra-thin surface structure
abstract: In this paper, a 19*19 dual-loop microstrip reflectarray antenna with high gain is obtained by designing dual-loop microstrip metasurface structure units with phase gradient variation and arranging these units according to the phase compensation formula. The reflector array antenna works in X band with a center frequency of 10 GHz, and its gain can reach 19.8 dBi, which is much larger than that of the feed source. Considering the focusing effect of double-loop microstrip metasurface, the sidelobe level of the reflector array antenna can be as low as -1.6 dB, which plays a good role of high orientation. It provides an effective method to realize the antenna with high gain and high orientation, and has a wide application prospect in the field of long distance wireless communication.

articleTitle: A K/Ka band Planar Dual-polarization Waveguide Diplexer
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band planar diplexer is proposed for K/Ka band satellite communications. A rotational planar topology structure is designed to minimize the system profile to only one layer. An externally convex quad-ridged waveguide is applied to the classic orthomode junction (OMJ) to improve its broadband performance. The results show that the -20 dB bandwidth(17.1GHz - 21.2GHz/27.3GHz - 31.3GHz) of the proposed OMJ covers the whole satellite communications bandwidth in K/Ka band. Its broadband performance and simpler manufacturing process indicates great potential in the application of millimeter wave and satellite communications.

articleTitle: A Passive Microwave Pulse Compressor Using Dual Spherical Cavities
abstract: A method for improving peak power gain and pulse compression efficiency of the passive microwave pulse compressor is proposed. The proposed passive microwave pulse compressor consists of a dual-mode polarizer and two parallel spherical resonant cavities. This method can effectively depress the mode contention, but also, increase the Q factor of resonant cavities. By contrast, the peak power gain and pulse compression efficiency of the pulse compressor with a single cavity are 6.52 and 22.6%, respectively, while they are increased to 7.4 and 52.43 % respectively using two parallel cavities. The latter offers a 13% improvement in peak power gain and a 30% improvement in compression efficiency over the former.

articleTitle: A Broadband Sapphire Disc Pillbox Window for Terahertz Traveling-Wave Tubes
abstract: In this paper, to develop a terahertz traveling-wave tube (TWT), a broadband sapphire disc pillbox window is investigated. The transmission line theory is used to analyze its transmission characteristics. To avoid a lot of simulation calculations and improve the design efficiency, the simulated annealing algorithm is employed to provide a rapid design scheme of the pillbox window. On the basis of the initial design scheme, the CST software is used for further optimization and the final design scheme is determined quickly. The simulated results show that the sapphire disc pillbox window has good transmission and low reflection in a broad terahertz band. The pillbox window is fabricated and tested. The preliminary experiment results show that the amplitude of <tex>$\mathbf{S}_{21}$</tex> is better than −4.5 dB from 200–240 GHz, and the amplitude of <tex>$\mathbf{S_{11}}$</tex> is less than −10 dB. This broadband pillbox window studied here will be applied to the terahertz TWTs.

articleTitle: A Novel Domian Decomposition Simulator for the Transmission Analysis of Travelling-wave Tube
abstract: The input/output system is one of the key component of travelling-wave tubes and affects the bandwidth and power capacity of the whole tube significantly. The widely used windows simulator component of MTSS for TWT's input/output system is based on finite element method. It might be inefficient when the multiscale feature of a complex input/output system leads to large numbers of mesh for accuracy. So that the matrix equation need to be solved become millions of order, which results in lots of computation resources consuming. In this work, a novel domian decomposition simulator for the transmission analysis of the TWT's input/output system is proposed. By transfer a large matrix equation solution problem into a series of smaller problems, the new simulator needs far less memory and CPU time than the one based finite element method during the simulation process. The results shows that the new simulator is more efficient than the old one under a comparable computational accuracy.

articleTitle: A Second-Harmonic Extended Interaction Klystron Multiplier-Amplifier
abstract: A Second-Harmonic Extended Interaction Klystron ( SHEIK ) is investigated at the THz band. The operating voltage and current are set to 18.2 kV and 30 mA, and the analytic magnetic source field of 0.7 T. PIC results show that the output power reaches 1.125 W at 650 GHz when the input power of 10 mW at 325 GHz. The simulation validates that the second-harmonic radiation can be generated and amplified in the EIK.

articleTitle: Research on Sheet Beam Folded arc-Shaped Ridge-loaded Groove Waveguide for terahertz TWT
abstract: In this paper, a novel slow-wave structure (SWS) called folded arc-shaped ridge-loaded groove waveguide is proposed. Based on this kind of SWS, a terahertz sheet beam traveling-wave tube (TWT) is studied, and its beam-wave interaction was simulated by CST PIC code. The transmission loss was considered by using an equivalent conductivity of <tex>$2.0^{\ast}10^{\wedge}7\ S/m$</tex> in the simulation. The beam voltage was found to be 26 kV for the novel structure and the sheet beam current was set to be 0. 15 A. The simulated results show that the saturation output power could reach 103 W at 240 GHz with a 3-dB bandwidth from 230.5 to 243.5 GHz, the gain could reach <tex>$\sim 26\ dB$</tex> at 237 GHz.

articleTitle: An electric field compression technique based on the $TM_{020}$ mode cylindrical resonant cavity
abstract: In this paper, an electric field compression technique based on <tex>$\text{TM}_{020}$</tex> mode cylindrical resonator is proposed. A magnetic medium is filled in the <tex>$\text{TM}_{020}$</tex> mode cylindrical cavity to realize the compression of the electric field inside the cavity. Through the compressed electric field, the dielectric properties of low sensitivity dielectric materials can be tested. In this study, the cavity was modeled and simulated by three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation software HFSS, and the electric field amplitude ratio before and after compression was obtained by simulation design. The results show that the high compression efficiency of electric field can be achieved in the cylindrical resonant cavity of <tex>$\text{TM}_{020}$</tex> mode.

articleTitle: Multi-mode Simulation for An Output Window of Gyrotron Based on Transfinite Element Method
abstract: In this paper, a fast algorithm to obtain S parameters and mode field using the transfinite element element(TFE) method for a multi-mode output window is presented. In the proposed method, the eigenmodes of uniform electromagnetic waveguides have been regarded as a basis function. The coefficients for incident and reflected waves can be obtained quickly by solving finite element matrix equation. As an example of the analysis, the double disks output window for a gyrotron traveling-wave tube is analyzed. The reflection coefficients of <tex>$\mathbf{TE}_{\mathbf{11}}$</tex> mode and <tex>$\mathbf{TE}_{\mathbf{01}}$</tex> mode calculated by the TFE method agree well with the results simulated by HFSS.

articleTitle: Effect of Nonuniform Electron Beam Generated by Electron Gun on Output Performance of Helix TWT
abstract: The distribution parameters of electron beam have an important influence on the TWT interaction. To be more in line with the actual situation, the distribution of the electron beam generated by the electron gun is analyzed. According to the distribution of the energy and density of electron beam, the concentric rings of electron beams model is built, which simplifies calculation and contains information on electron beam. Based on the model, a nonuniform electron beam is obtained. The output power, gain and SNR are calculated. Through simulation analysis, the results show that nonuniformity leads to a decrease in the maximum output power, as well as a decrease in the gain and SNR.

articleTitle: The Analysis of THz Electromagnetic Waves Effect on Acetylcholine Synthesis based on MD Simulation
abstract: Experiments show that terahertz (THz) electromagnetic waves can have a potential impact on a variety of physical and chemical properties of proteins and the synthesis of some substances in vivo. Many experiments use vacuum electronic devices to research THz biological effects. Based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, this paper analyzes the effect of specific frequency of THz electromagnetic wave on the binding of choline and acetyl coenzyme-A (acetyl-CoA) and then analyzes the effect of THz electromagnetic waves on the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine (Ach). This research has guiding significance for the influence of THz electromagnetic waves on Ach synthesis and the selection of THz electromagnetic wave frequency in future experiments.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Simulation of Terahertz Pulse Induced Photoacoustic Wave
abstract: Terahertz optical imaging has been studied for many medical applications. However, due to the strong water absorption of terahertz waves, in order to obtain high-contrast imaging, it is necessary to consider reducing the water content of the sample, which is difficult in many cases. The terahertz wave is completely absorbed on the water surface, and this strong absorption can effectively generate terahertz photoacoustic waves. In this paper, we constructed the terahertz photoacoustic model in water at room temperature, observed the propagation of photoacoustic signal in water, and analyzed the results. The results show that the propagation depth of photoacoustic wave is much larger than the penetration depth of terahertz wave.

articleTitle: Design of Wide Stopband and High Suppression Cavity Filter
abstract: Radio frequency filter is the core device to improve the signal to noise ratio of radar. A cavity filter for suppressing high harmonics in Ka band millimeter wave (MMW) radar is presented. The structural parameters of the filter are obtained by theoretical calculation. A cavity filter with the center frequency of 8.1 GHz and the relative bandwidth of 9.80% is designed by using HFSS electromagnetic simulation software. The spurious passband is above twice the frequency of the center frequency. The attenuation of the stopband is greater than 78 dB in 9.2 ~16 GHz, which can well meet the demand of the need of Ka band MMW radar to suppress high harmonics.

articleTitle: The Development of a 1.5kW Terahertz Gyro-TWA with 20GHz Instantaneous Bandwidth
abstract: The development of a gyrotron traveling amplifier (Gyro-TWA) with an output power of 1.5 kW and an instantaneous frequency bandwidth of 20 GHz which could be used for 263 GHz high-field electron paramagnetic resonance is presented. The gyro-TWA was designed to operate on the third harmonic of the electron cyclotron mode of an axis-encircling electron beam generated by a triode cusp electron gun. To achieve such a broadband frequency bandwidth a 5-fold helically corrugated interaction region, which has a TE31-like eigenwave with ideal dispersion properties, was designed to resonantly interact with the electron beam of energy 60 keV and current 0.75 A.

articleTitle: Development of Metrological-grade Spinning Rotor Gauge
abstract: The spinning rotor gauge is an internationally recognized high vacuum transfer standard. It is widely used in aerospace, nuclear industry, semiconductor and other fields because of its excellent metrological characteristics and chemical inertness. In order to realize the international equivalence of vacuum quantity in China's science and technology industry. Through the continuous research of key technologies, such as high-quality suspension based on permanent magnet, accurate measurement of axial displacement, residual drag suppression, construction of kinetic model of rotational speed decay rate and high precision detection, the metrological-grade spinning rotor vacuum gauge has been developed. The change of residual drag is less than 0.49 % after 50 minutes of start-up. There is good consistency and linearity in the range of 9 × 10<sup>-5</sup> Pa to 1 Pa.

articleTitle: Measurements of a G-band Broadband TWT with Driving Voltage over Designed Operating Voltage
abstract: The measurements of a G band broadband traveling wave tube with driving voltage over designed operating voltage are presented. The stable range of driving voltage was determined according to the oscillation measurements. The measurements show that the output power and bandwidth of the TWT can be effectively improved by over operating operation. When the driving voltage is 200 V higher than the operating voltage, the maximum in-band output power is increased from 16 W to 21.3 W and the bandwidth is expanded from 23 GHz to 31 GHz. The gain fluctuation is 18.4dB, which is 10 dB higher than that with the designed operating voltage.

articleTitle: A New Concept of an Electron-optical System with Two Counter-propagating Electron Beams for Advanced Gyrotron Designs
abstract: This paper presents a new concept of a complex electron-optical system for advanced gyrodevices. The system forms two helical electron beams moving towards each other in the interaction space and makes it possible to independently control the parameters of each beam.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Electron Optics System for 1.0 THz Backward-wave Oscillator
abstract: In this paper, the electron optics system of 1.0 THz backward-wave oscillator is designed, and the design process of electron gun and permanent magnetic focusing system are described. Firstly, the design and debugging of the electron gun is carried out according to the initial design value, and the electron gun with the beam range and beam radius meets the requirements. Secondly, through theoretical calculation, it is known that the uniform region magnetic field is 12000 Gauss, and the uniform magnetic field that meets the focus is designed. The simulation results show that the EOS has good laminarity, the passing rate of electron beam is 100<sup>%</sup>, and the filling ratio is about 70% under the voltage of 25kV and the beam current of 20mA.

articleTitle: Design of an Electron Optical System for a 263 GHz Sheet Beam TWT
abstract: A novel approach toward a new high compression sheet beam electron gun and an advanced hybrid periodic permanent magnet-periodic quadrupolar magnet (PPM-PQM) for the development of a 263 GHz sheet beam Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) is reported herein. The electron gun is designed to operate at 19 kV and to produce a sheet electron beam with an elliptical cross section of 0.6 mm (width) x 0.08 mm (height) compressed from a flat 0.8 mm diameter round cathode, providing a beam current density of 300 A/cm<sup>2</sup>, The modified PPM-PQM focusing system is specifically designed to transport the sheet electron beam in a 0.7 mm width and 0.12 mm height beam tunnel. The designed beam transport system achieves ~100% transmission throughout the entire 4S-mm long beam tunnel with CST Particle Tracking simulation.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Measurement of Millimeter Wave Co-planar Slow Wave Structure
abstract: In this paper, a V band coplanar slow-wave structure (SWS) for application of backward wave oscillator is designed, fabricated and measured. The dispersion characteristics and coupling impedance of the SWS are simulated using CST Microwave studio. The measurement of cold-test parameters is carried out for structures with and without the metal shield. The results show that the S parameters of the SWS with the metal shield is in good agreement with the simulation results. The SWS without metal shield has some radiation loss compared with the one with a metal shield.

articleTitle: A Bitter-Type Magnet for a Low-Voltage Compact Gyrotron
abstract: Compact gyrotron was supposed to be a promising continuous radiation source for industrial applications. Magnetic field system is one of the most crucial components for gyrotron operation. A compact gyrotron with a custom-designed magnet would be a promising continuous radiation source for millimeter-wave power applications. Gyrotron operated with room-temperature magnet and extreme low-voltage has been hugely significant in the industrial field. In this talk, the design and preliminary experiment of this compact gyrotron are presented. Both in simulation and experimental measurement, the length of the homogeneity region is 120 mm, and homogeneity <tex>$\Delta \mathrm{B}/\mathrm{B}$</tex> is <tex>$\pm 0.9\%$</tex> is obtained. Continuous emission test of oxide cathode is also presented for a low-voltage operation.

articleTitle: A Method for Detecting High Energy Density Electron Beams in Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: As the most widely used microwave vacuum electronic devices, the high performance of traveling wave tube is not only needed to be improved in design, but also important in detection and measurement technique. The state of electron beam is one of the key factors in the operation of traveling wave tube, but the detection method of electron beam is still relatively backward. In this paper, the high energy density electron beam is treated with energy reduction, which can be detected by conventional detection means under the condition that the electron energy distribution curve is guaranteed, so as to analyze the state of the electron beam.

Author Keywords: the detection method of electron beam

articleTitle: Recent Development to High-Frequency Circuit Simulator
abstract: Modeling and simulation techniques have been playing a more and more important role in designing and developing high-performance traveling-wave tubes (TWT). Recent developments to the high-frequency circuit simulator (HFCS), a 3-D advanced finite-element electromagnetic-simulation tool for TWT, are presented in this paper, using new preprocessing and postprocessing architecture. And a high performance parallel preconditioner is developed. The numerical example shows that the efficiency of matrix solution is improved.

articleTitle: 3-D-FDTD-PIC Simulation of Magnetic-Field Tuning in a THz Gyrotron
abstract: Gyrotron output under time-variant magnetic field tuning is studied by using a self-developed 3-D-FDTD-PIC simulation software. Our work demonstrated that, only one single-run simulation under time-variant magnetic field is enough to grasp the influence of different strength of magnetic field on the output, and each stage has carried enough frequency-domain and power information, whose error is no more than 1.43 dB. It can help greatly enhance the analysis efficiency and provide valuable guidance for parameter optimization during gyrotron experiment.

articleTitle: Experiment and Optimization on 0.34 THz Sheet Electron Beam TWT
abstract: A 0.34THz sheet electron beam travelling wave tube is being tested at Nanjing Sanle Group Co. LTD. The traveling wave tube is based on a Laser-fabricated staggered double vane slow wave structure, together with a tunable sheet beam electron gun, a periodic permanent magnet focusing system, and diamond windows. The simulation shows that the output power is over 50mW with 3dB bandwidth of 30GHz. This paper reports the manufacture, assembling, welding and measurement on the sheet beam TWT. In view of the existing deficiencies, the article briefly analyzes the reasons for the design and assembly of TWT. The solution for the next step is present in the last.

articleTitle: Research on S-band 3.3MW pulsed magnetron
abstract: In this paper, a method is presented to suppress the abnormal current envelope of a S-band 3.3 MW pulsed magnetron. In the test processing, an abnormal current envelope of the magnetron caused by axial electrons was found. By designing a special structure, the axial electrons are effectively suppressed, which cause the pulse current envelope improved greatly. Under the conditions of anode pulse voltage of 47.5kV, anode pulse current of 120A, and pulse width of <tex>$4.2\mu{s},$</tex>, the output pulse power of this improved magnetron can reach to 3.3MW with stable pulse current envelope, which show this method can improve the performance of high power pulsed magnetron.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of Traveling-Wave Tubes Considering Thermal Contact Resistance
abstract: Thermal contact resistance is a non-negligible problem in the thermal analysis of traveling wave tubes. If the influence of thermal contact resistance(TCR) is ignored in the thermal analysis of traveling wave tube, there will be some difference between the simulated temperature and the actual value, or even completely wrong results. In this paper, a general finite element numerical solution technique for the TCR is proposed, which treats the TCR as the boundary condition of heat conduction problem. This technique does not need to modify the geometric model or introduce the contact element, which greatly improves the efficiency of solving the TCR problems. The numerical results show that the proposed method has the same calculation accuracy as CST MPS, but has better calculation performance, which would be very useful for the design of traveling wave tubes.

articleTitle: Investigation of novel compact and lightweight C-band transit-time oscillator with low magnetic field
abstract: A novel compact and lightweight C-band transit-time oscillator with low magnetic field is proposed in this paper. Besides, a novel cathode with soft magnetic material and focusing electrode and opening foils are loaded to improve the conversion efficiency of this device. Simulation and experimental research is carried out to prove that the device can operate with a low magnetic field of 0.3 T while keeping the advantage of miniaturization. Finally, experimental research shows that when loading the novel cathode and the opening foils, the device can work with a low magnetic field and generate a GW -level microwave output with a conversion efficiency of about 28%.

articleTitle: Confocal-Cavity Terahertz Gyrotron based on Sheet e-beam
abstract: Serving as one of important sources of terahertz, the output and efficiency is limited by the size of devices and ‘unemployed’ electrons of the beam. To achieve higher electron efficiency and output power, the sheet electron beam is introduced in gyrotrons. We here present a design of a gyrotron with a quasi-optical confocal cavity which proves to possess good mode selectivity with the sheet electron beam. Besides, 3-D particle simulation is also carried out. The modified gyrotron is working at 220GHz, reaching 15kW output and 15% efficiency with lower current. In the future, the improved structure may be applied in frequency-tunable gyrotrons with high power.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of 220 GHz TWT Folded Waveguide Slow Wave Structure
abstract: In this paper, a folded waveguide slow wave structure (FW-SWS) of 220 GHz traveling wave tube (TWT) with high electron beam transmission ratio is designed and fabricated, and its transmission characteristics are tested. The output performance of the FW-SWS is simulated by CST. The simulation results show that when the electron beam voltage and current are 17 kV and 70 mA respectively, the output power is 58 W, the gain is 31 dB, and the transmission ratio is 100%. The cold test results show that the transmission characteristics of the fabricated FW-SWS are in good agreement with the simulation results to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Cross-polarization Amplitude Modulator Based on THz Dynamic Metasurface
abstract: We propose a dynamic metasurface based on a HEMT that achieves efficient linear polarization conversion in the terahertz band through a metal-media-metal three-layer design, and changes its mode of operation by integrating a HEMT into a frontal metal microstructure to produce a dynamic modulation effect. In the simulation, the modulation depth of the generated cross-polarized wave is up to 90.7%.

articleTitle: Effect of Surface Features on Emission Properties of Impregnated Scandate Dispenser Cathode
abstract: The scandate dispenser cathode has a clear advantage in current emission density but lacks emission uniformity. In this work, volt-ampere characteristics of impregnated scandate cathodes are examined at 1000, 1050, and 1100 <tex>${}^{\circ} \mathbf{C}$</tex>, respectively, in order to study the changes in the emission characteristics of the cathode after surface ion bombardment. After surface treatment, the Richardson work function decreased from 1.33 to 1.19 <tex>$e$</tex> V, and its Richardson constant dropped from 0.024 to 0.017 <tex>$\mathrm{A}/(\text{cm}^{2}*\deg^{2})$</tex>. The surface of the cathode is less rough than before ion treatment, as evidenced by the atomic force microscope image. More importantly, the cathode does not exhibit an abnormal Schottky effect after ion bombardment on the surface, which indicates that surface treatment can improve the emission uniformity of scandate cathodes.

articleTitle: The study of dielectric constant of sapphire based on terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
abstract: In this paper, two transmission terahertz time-domain spectral systems (THz-TDS) are developed, their difference is the off-axis parabolic mirror. Based on the transmission THz- TDS, the influence of sample fixture, sapphire thickness and off-axis parabolic mirror on the dielectric constant of sapphire window is studied, and the transmittance of 0.5 mm sapphire window is 66.0%.

articleTitle: Transient Thermal Analysis of Microwave Tube Based on Finite Element Method
abstract: Among the many numerical calculation methods for thermal analysis, the finite element method has become the most versatile numerical calculation tool due to its good simulation capability for complex geometric boundaries and inhomogeneous material properties. In this paper, we propose a fast finite element solution method for transient thermal analysis of microwave tubes, which adopts a post-Eulerian time iteration format for finite element time discretization to ensure the stability of the time iteration algorithm. Based on the theory of fast finite element for thermal analysis of microwave tubes, the transient thermal analysis module in TS[1], a thermal analysis simulation design software with full intellectual property rights is developed. By modelling the transient thermal analysis of microwave tubes and comparing with the commercial software ANSYS, the computational accuracy and computational performance of TS are verified.

articleTitle: 3-D PIC Simulation of A 0.14 THz Traveling Wave Tube with Varying Emission Angles
abstract: Folded-Waveguide (FWG) is an important type of slow wave structure applied in terahertz band. As a planar structure, FWG is easy to process, robust and has high thermal capacity. This kind of structure combines the advantages of helix and those of coupled cavity. But its coupling impedance is relatively low. To improve the efficiency of beam-wave interaction of FWG TWT, a simple beam-wave interaction model is simulated, where an electron beam emitted with initial angular speed is adopted. With periodical permanent magnetic field, the output power increases along with the increment of the angular speed of electrons. However, simulated with uniform magnetic field, the output power decreases at first, then returns to normal level.

articleTitle: Investigation on Thermal Efficiency Enhancement and Trapped Electron Suppression
abstract: A novel Ka band cathode with higher thermal efficiency was designed. The novel cathode makes that there is greater thermal resistance between the front and rear electrodes and the emitter. In the experiment, when the emitter is working at 1050°C, the thermal power is reduced from 85W to 42W, and the temperature difference between the front and rear electrodes and the emitter becomes larger. This shows that the front and rear electrodes will produce less trapped electrons. The absorbed power of the capture structure is greatly reduced. The novel cathode makes the magnetron injection electron gun (MIG) have better performance.

articleTitle: Compact Rat-race Ring Couplers with T type Capacitor Loading and T Type Stepped Impedance Loading
abstract: Compact rat-race ring couplers with T type capacitor loading and T type stepped impedance loading are presented in this paper. The occupied area of the coupler with T type capacitor loading is a little larger than that of the coupler with T type stepped impedance loading. The bandwidth of the coupler with T type capacitor loading is better than that of the coupler with T type stepped impedance loading. The conclusions are supported both by simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: Development and Modeling of W-band Sheet-Beam Tubes with Grating Slow-Wave Structures
abstract: The results of design, simulation and development of W-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) and backward-wave oscillator (BWO) with sheet electron beam and grating slow-wave structure (SWS) are presented. Design of the SWS was optimized to obtain synchronism voltage of 10–12 kV. The results of 3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation of beam-wave interaction are presented. The TWT with staggered double-grating SWS provides nearly 30 dB small-signal gain, 15-GHz bandwidth, and up to 50 W power at saturation. The BWO with single grating SWS provides up to 20 W output power. Electron gun providing 0.1-A sheet electron beam is designed and fabricated. Grating SWS is fabricated by a novel technology based on diffusion bonding of alternating copper and molybdenum plates and subsequent chemical etching of copper. Other key components of the device, such as depressed collector, permanent-magnet magnetic focusing system, and vacuum window are designed and currently are under fabrication.

articleTitle: A low reflection folded waveguide slow wave structure for millimeter wave traveling wave tube
abstract: A modified folded waveguide (FWG) with low reflection is proposed as the slow wave structure (SWS) to design the high power millimeter wave travelling wave tube (TWT). This low reflection folded waveguide (LRFWG) SWS possesses larger interaction impedance and lower reflection parameter than the normal FWG SWS over the whole frequency band. The beam-wave interaction simulation results indicate that the TWT based on LRFWG SWS can generate the maximum output power of 278.5W at 94GHz, corresponding to a gain of 37.45dB and an interaction efficiency of 7.67%.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experiment of G-band Folded Waveguide Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, a folded waveguide traveling-wave tube (FWG-TWT) working in the G-band is designed. The simulation result shows that the folded waveguide high-frequency system working voltage 19.54kV and current 40mA; in the frequency range of 214-226GHz, the maximum output power is 16W, and the gain is greater than 26dB. The components of the traveling-wave tube (TWT) are assembled and tested. The test results show that the FWG- TWT reaches a maximum output power of 11 W, and the corresponding gain is 37.36dB at 223GHz when the electron beam flow rate is 49.39%, and the 3dB bandwidth is about 3.6GHz. The hot test results are analyzed.

articleTitle: Circular Waveguide Polarizer for Gyrotron Traveling wave tube
abstract: A circular waveguide polarizer for high power millimeter wave is proposed in this paper. The elliptical-shaped structure converts the linearly polarized TE<inf>11</inf> mode to a circularly polarized TE<inf>11</inf> mode. This circular polarizer can be well connected to the helical corrugated waveguide in the Gyro-TWT. By optimizing the polarizer length and radius, a good simulation result is obtained with an axis ratio less than 1.2 in the frequency range of 27.4-31.5 GHz. In the operating band, the reflection coefficient is less than −40 dB and the phase difference is approximately 88–90 degrees. It has good transmission performance in the operating band.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Simulation and Experimental Demonstration of Low-Pressure Microwave Breakdown in Parallel Plates
