abstract: In this paper, a Monte Carlo simulation method was proposed to study the initial phase of low-pressure microwave breakdown in parallel plates. Calculations were performed by tracing electrons only and the 3D trajectories of the electron are only governed by the electric field. The threshold breakdown electric field can be obtained by the fluctuation characteristics of electron number. We carried out the low-pressure discharge experiment based on a coaxial resonator to verify this method and the comparison results between simulation and experiment show that it has high accuracy and the error with the Monte Carlo method prediction results is less than 5.5%.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic study of ballast resistance on the Supersonically Expanding Argon using a Micrometer Hollow Cathode Discharge
abstract: Pulsed planar discharge nozzle (PPDN), which generates supersonic plasma expansion, has been used to study spectral transient species of interest in astrophysics for nearly 30 years. Although PPDN has proved to be very useful for recording the completely resolved spectra of rotating cold <tex>$(\mathrm{T}_{\text{rot}}\sim 20\mathrm{K})$</tex> radicals and ions, attempts to optimize the product yield are still limited. The influence of ballast resistance on argon plasma are studied experimentally by spectroscopy in this study. A qualitatively comparison of emission line intensity is shown in this work. The results show that the PPDN-MHCD mode is not change by change the current-limiting ballast resistance. The Argon ions and excited stages are enhanced in the observation area. The findings show a strong potential to increase the plasma yield of astrophysics interests in PPDN with supersonic expansion.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Study on the Electron Emission Properties of the Thermionic Cathode Impregnants
abstract: The emission current density of thermionic cathode materials is predicted using machine learning methods. Firstly, four classical regression algorithms of linear regression (LR), random forest regression (RFR), XGBoost, and gradient boosting regression tree (GBRT) are used. The relation coefficient <tex>$\boldsymbol{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> is chosen for the model evaluation metrics, and the prediction results are 0.174, 0.677, 0.812, and 0.915, respectively. Secondly, to solve the problems of small training data and unstable prediction results, the small sample TrAdaboost regression algorithm is introduced to predict and adjust the parameters for each system with different percentages of each chemical component (612, 512, 411, and others), and the final prediction results <tex>$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> are obtained as 0.954, 0.95, 0.5 and 0.939. The prediction accuracy is significantly improved.

articleTitle: Cold-Test of The W-Band Nonperiodic Concentric Arc FW-SWS Based on The Beam-Wave Resynchronization Method
abstract: Cold-test of the W-band nonperiodic concentric arc folded-waveguide slow-wave structure (FW-SWS) based on the beam-wave resynchronization method is presented in this paper. The scanning electron microscope result shows that the edge of the concentric arc FW-SWS is clear, where almost no cutting burr can be observed. Moreover, the measured |S<inf>11</inf>| is below −19.5 dB from 90 GHz to 104 GHz, and |S<inf>21</inf>| is in the range of −9.2 dB to −5.3 dB. Furthermore, the cold-test result demonstrates that when the bulk conductivity of copper is set as 4.2×10<sup>7</sup> S/m higher than the common value (2.25×10<sup>7</sup> S/m) in W-band, the simulated result can be the most consistent with the measured one, which indicates that surface roughness and finish of the fabricated FW-SWS is better than expectation.

articleTitle: Design of Coaxial Input Cavity with Coupler for Inductive Output Tube
abstract: Inductive output tubes (IOTs) are widely used as microwave power amplifiers for broadcast, accelerator and scientific applications. In this presented work, simulation of coaxial type input structure at 500 MHz high power IOTs is carried out. The generalized model has been designed in CST tool. Mathematical approach has been adopted for calculation of resonant frequency and quality factor of re-entrant coaxial input cavity. The simulation results are presented in this article. Radio frequency (RF) coaxial loop coupler for input cavity has been designed and simulation results are obtained. S-parameters for the re-entrant coaxial input cavity with loop coupler have been examined.

articleTitle: Diamond Substrate Planar Slow-Wave Structures for Millimeter Wave Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: Traveling wave tubes (TWTs) are commonly used to amplify radio frequency signals in a variety of applications, including radar systems, satellite communication. In this paper, we investigate the use of diamond substrate planar slow-wave structures (D-PSWS) in TWTs operating at 210 GHz. We describe the design and a possible fabrication process of D-PSWS. The simulations show the possibility of achieving a gain higher than 30 dB at a frequency of 210 GHz with a bandwidth of 1 GHz, and a maximum output power of 4.5 W.

articleTitle: Design of 140 GHz Broadband Subharmonic Mixer Based on Schottky Diode
abstract: Terahertz wave has attracted the attention of many scholars because of its high penetration and wide available bandwidth and other excellent characteristics. As an indispensable part of communication system, mixer has an important impact on its performance. In this paper, the structure of sector probe and reverse parallel diode is adopted, combined with HFSS and ADS software, and the simulation of 140 GHz broadband sub harmonic mixer based on Schottky diode is completed through snp file. Its bandwidth can basically cover the D-band. In the working frequency band of 110–170 GHz, the frequency conversion loss is better than 8.83 dB, and reaches 7.3 dB at the best point.

articleTitle: Rising-Sun Magnetron with Axial Extraction of Radiation TE01-mode
abstract: A preliminary investigation on magnetron with diffraction output (MDO) is carried out, aiming at the application of high-power microwave (HPM) phased array system. For such system, the direction of output port should orthogonal to the radial direction of the magnetron. Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulation is applied to study the characteristics of the 10-cavity rising-sun magnetron with diffraction output whose radiation pattern is TE<inf>0l</inf> mode. The configuration of the MDO is optimized to improving the beam-to-microwave conversion efficiency. Consequently, when a voltage of 46 <tex>$\mathbf{kV}$</tex> and magnetic field of 0.204 <tex>$\mathbf{T}$</tex> are applied on the optimized magnetron, the average output power can be as high as 2.71 MW at 2. <tex>$4\text{GHz}$</tex>, corresponding to a high-power conversion efficiency of 76%.

articleTitle: High frequency field enhanced structure based on photonic crystal
abstract: A high frequency field strength enhancement structure based on photonic crystal has been proposed. The band gap and the transmission characteristics of two-dimensional photonic crystal composed of periodic dielectric cylinder square lattice of alumina dielectric column in vacuum background are simulated by using COMSOL. The waveguide transmission and field strength enhancement are realized by designing line defect structure and resonant cavity structure. It is found that the electric field of the resonator structure can be enhanced by 10<sup>4</sup>, when the input frequency is 6.48 THz. For the resonant cavity structure of photonic crystal based on dielectric cylinder, when the resonant frequency is 6.41 THz, <tex>$\mathrm{S}11=_{-}22.09\text{dB}$</tex>, and the quality factor is 687. The feasibility of input signal transmission of high frequency vacuum nano channel devices and resonant amplification of cold cathode surface excitation field has been verified. It provides a new way to improve the emission performance of vacuum field emission devices in the future.

articleTitle: A measurement apparatus for outgassing rate of pakaging materials and its background compensation method
abstract: The outgassing of packaging materials is one of the direct threats to the vacuum acquisition and maintenance of vacuum electronic devices, so its accurate measurement is of great significance to improve the quality and life of devices. However, the background leakage and outgassing of the sample chamber have a non-negligible impact on the measurement results. The outgassing rate that can be measured by traditional testing devices is generally high, and it is difficult to accurately measure the vacuum outgassing rate of packaging materials with low outgassing rates. In order to solve this problem, we develop an apparatus for measuring the vacuum outgassing rate of materials based on constant conductance method and symmetrical measurement structure, and propose a background outgassing compensation method to extend the lower limit of the outgassing rate that can be measured.

articleTitle: Preliminary Experimental Verification of High Efficiency Q-Band Helix Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, a helix slow-wave structure (SWS) with variable pitch and inner diameter is designed for higher power, higher efficiency, and gain flatness in Q-band traveling-wave tube (TWT), and its device performance is studied by simulation and experiment. Here the helix of TWT is designed with a taper scheme. Under the conditions of beam voltage and beam current of 8.8 kV and 70 mA respectively, the preliminary experimental results show that the saturated output power of the TWT is about 80 W at 37 GHz and the saturated efficiency is about 44%. The output power of the TWT is about 20 W and the efficiency is about 17% when it is backed off 6 dB from the saturation. This research has laid the foundation for the next-generation wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Study of an Axis-Encircling Large-Orbit Cusp Electron-gun for Ka-band Gyrotron Traveling Wave Amplifiers
abstract: An axis-encircling large-orbit cusp electron beam can keep stable work in high power and high frequency gyrotrons traveling wave amplifiers (gyro-TWAs) at high efficiency. However, the CUSP magnetic field is difficult to obtain in engineering realization. A gradually-varying magnetic field produced by a solenoid magnet is obtained for the axis-encircling large-orbit cusp electron beam, which is designed for a Ka-band gyro-TWAs. And a magnetic cusp gun (MCG) is designed, which can work with low parameters spread at the beam voltage of 65kV and beam current of 5A. The calculated results show that the beam can be generated with average radius 1.1 mm, average beam pitch ratio <tex>$\alpha=\mathbf{1.0}$</tex>, and the axial magnetic field <tex>$\mathbf{B}_{\mathbf{z}\mathbf{0}}=\mathbf{0.641}\mathbf{T}$</tex> is designed as the magnetic field in the interaction region. At the same time the spread of the transverse velocity and the longitudinal velocity are 2.3% and 4.3% respectively. The designed can be used for Ka-band gyro-TWAs.

articleTitle: A Chamfered-shaped Microstrip Meander Line Slow-wave Structure for D-band Traveling-wave Tube
abstract: A novel chamfered-shaped microstrip meander-line slow-wave structure is proposed for D-band traveling-wave tube to decrease the reflection and improve the transmission. The slow-wave electromagnetic characteristics and the beam-wave interaction of this structure are carried out. The high-frequency characteristics show that the interaction impedance of chamfered-shaped MML is larger than that of N-shaped MML and U-shaped MML near the center frequency of 140GHz. The transmission characteristics show that the transmission loss of chamfered-shaped microstrip meander line slow-wave structure is reduced by 0.5dB for 20 periods compared with the N-shaped microstrip meander line slow-wave structure. The simulation results show that TWT with the novel SWS can generate hundreds of watts in the frequency range of 130-150GHz, and the average output power is 578 watts with the corresponding gain of 27.62dB.

articleTitle: A 600 GHz Quasi TM51 mode Extended Interaction Oscillator with Low Injection
abstract: To meet the communication requirements at 600 GHz, a 600 GHz quasi TM<inf>51</inf> (QTM<inf>51</inf>) mode extended interaction oscillator (EIO) with low injection is proposed. Due to the higher characteristic impedance of QTM<inf>51</inf> mode and its specific field distribution, the proposed device can work stably and generate higher output power with low injection (low current density and low voltage). The particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results show that, under the condition of beam voltage of 13.7 kV, beam current of 25 mA, working in QTM<inf>51</inf><tex>$1\pi/54$</tex> mode with a single electron beam, the output power reaches 1905 mW at 604.11 GHz, and a bandwidth of 1.02 GHz over 1377 mW can be obtained.

articleTitle: A X-Band Tunable Diplexer based on Talbot Effect
abstract: Based on the principle of talbot effect, a X-band tunable high power diplexer is studied, which adopts bridge and phase shifting. The good isolation ability between such bridge ports is used to achieve dual frequency power synthesis, which can replace the filter structure in the traditional diplexer. The simulation results with Ansoft HFSS shows that the transmission efficiency of the tunable interferometer are more than 97% in the frequency band from 9.2GHz to 10GHz, and the power capacity can reach GW level. Which would be applied in the high power microwave system, through the seveal ways power synthesis, and the system whole power capacity can reach tens of GW.

articleTitle: Demonstration of High Reliability RF Chain Based on High Power Gridded Tubes For Scientific Applications
abstract: In view of future scientific applications such as thermonuclear fusion, the status of tetrode TH 781 and diacrode TH 628L for two particular applications is given. First, THALES qualification test setup and Continuous Wave (CW) measurements procedure is described. Specific pulse mode tests for Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) linac, as well as operating lifetime of qualified high-power gridded tubes are given. Outstanding performance of more than 50 khours of operation is demonstrated, highlighting the strong reliability of this technology. Finally, measurements of R&D phase of ITER ICRF are given. The results comply with the requested specifications, including the most stringent ones, such as maintaining the 1.5 MW output power under constant mis-match VSWR 2:1.

articleTitle: Inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging based on a multiple norm constrained GOMP algorithm
abstract: In this paper, an inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging method based on multiple norm constrained generalized orthogonal matching pursuit (MNGOMP) algorithm is proposed to improve the imaging process of inverse synthetic aperture radar is prone to noise interference in compressed sensing environment. Orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) and generalized orthogonal matching pursuit (GOMP) converge slowly in radar imaging and are susceptible to noise interference. Therefore, multiple norm constraints were introduced into the iteration update to improve convergence speed and accuracy and enhance noise resistance. The results show that this method is effective in suppressing unnecessary clutter and enhancing desired target.

articleTitle: Improved Laser Microprocessing of 2D Planar Microstrip Slow-Wave Structures for Millimeter-Band Vacuum Microelectronic Devices
abstract: For vacuum microelectronic devices operating at sub- THz frequencies, tiny slow-wave structures must be produced using high-precision microfabrication technologies. Nowadays, a variety of high-tech technologies, including UV-LIGA, deep reactive ion etching, 3D printing, nano-CNC milling, and laser micromachining, are used to fabricate microsized electromagnetic structures with micron and sub-micron accuracy. In this paper, we present an enhancement of our previously developed method for microfabrication of the designed 2D planar microstrip slow-wave structures for V-band operation using magnetron sputtering and nanosecond laser micromachining. A detailed illustration of the improved laser-based micromachining approach is presented. We'll go into great depth about the outcomes of the morphological analyses of the microfabricated samples slow-wave structures.

articleTitle: Simulation study of a double states input coupler for K/Ka dual-band Gyro-TWT
abstract: In this paper, the simulation results of a four slots coaxial cavity input coupler applied to a novel K/Ka band dual mode <tex>$(\text{TE}_{01}/\text{TE}_{02}$</tex> mode) Gyro- TWT are introduced. In two working states and both inputs are introduced through the standard rectangular waveguide. In order to prevent the occurrence of backward wave at the Ku band input port, Bragg reflector is added to the rectangular waveguide in this input section to cut off the backward wave. At the same time, the input TE<inf>10</inf> mode is coupled into the interaction waveguide through the coupling slot of the coaxial cavity, and the circular TE<inf>01</inf> and TE<inf>02</inf> modes are successfully excited. The simulation results show that the effective bandwidth is 18.5GHz to 20.5GHz in the K band and 33.5GHz to 35.5GHz in the Ka band. Compared with the analysis results of nonlinear theory, it can basically meet the requirements of Gyro TWT.

articleTitle: A Multi-Stage Depressed Collector for 0.22 THz Sheet Beam Traveling-Wave Tubes
abstract: In this paper, in order to improve the device efficiency of 0.22 THz traveling-wave tubes (TWTs), a multi-stage depressed collector (MDC) is investigated. For the purpose of designing a suitable collector structure and reasonable collector voltages, the energy distributions of the spent sheet beam is analyzed, and then the information of the energy distribution of the sheet beam is obtained. Through the theoretical calculations, the design scheme of a four-stage depressed collector is determined, and the maximum collector efficiency (98.11%) and the corresponding collector voltages (21.70 kV, 22.25 kV, 23.35 kV, and 24.40 kV) under ideal conditions are obtained. An elliptical four-stage depressed collector is accordingly designed by CST. After simulation optimization, it is finally determined that the collector voltages of each stage are 21.3 kV, 22.3 kV, 23.3 kV, and 24.4 kV, respectively. The collector efficiencies without and with considering the secondary electrons are 95.19% and 91.74%, respectively. These results are important for the design of the MDC for the 0.22 THz sheet beam TWTs.

articleTitle: Tunability Enhancement of Ku-Band Oscillator using Distributed Bragg Reflectors
abstract: It is possible to improve the tunability range of slow-wave structure oscillators with the use of distributed Bragg reflectors (DBRs). In this paper, an aperiodic DBR made of rectangular surface gratings is applied to a 16GHz (Ku-Band) sheet beam oscillator which previously did not exhibit good tunability when coupled with a single grating reflector. The device operates at the central frequency given an input current of 2.195kA and 178keV beam energy with an axial magnetic field of 1.02T. The designed peak power output is 145MW. The DBR geometry is optimized using CST Studio to achieve the desired reflectivity range. It is observed that the DBR improves the tunable frequency range by 2.85 times, i.e. increase from 350MHz to 1GHz while maintaining an output power of at least 40MW.

articleTitle: Quasi-Analytical Spatio-Temporal Theory of the Gyro-BWO with Zigzag Electrodynamic System
abstract: We describe a quasi-analytical theory of a new type of backward-wave gyro-oscillator (BWO) generator with a quasi-optical electrodynamic system with the operating wave beam propagating along a zigzag trajectory. The theory is based on the multi-frequency spatio-temporal approach describing the evolution of the wave in the periodic quasi-optical microwave system. Simulations provided on the basis of this approach predict stationary single-mode operation with a piecewise character of changing the output power and operating frequency in the process of changing the operating magnetic field. In addition, at relatively high operating currents the transition to regimes with auto-modulations of the output power is described.

articleTitle: Interaction of Terahertz Waves with the RNA Hairpin
abstract: The vibrations of low frequencies and the functional groups of nucleic acid molecules, hydrogen bonds, van der Waals, and other weak intermolecular interactions are in the THz band. Theoretically, nucleic acid molecules are capable of interacting with THz waves. The vacuum electron THz source can be used to study the interaction of THz waves with nucleic acids. This paper simulates the effect of the THz waves on the binding energy of the folded WT-30nt. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations show that the THz waves at 4 THz, 23.8 THz, and 37.4 THz can weakly affect the stability of WT-30nt, while the others cannot. This suggests that even THz waves with stronger amplitudes can rarely affect the binding ability of double-stranded RNAs by affecting hydrogen bonds, and it is estimated that THz waves would have difficulty affecting the stability of RNAs with more complex structures and more nucleotides.

articleTitle: Development of A 3-D Multistage Depressed Collector Simulation Program
abstract: In this paper, a 3-D multistage depressed collector simulation program is studied and developed, which consists of electrostatic potential calculation, electron trajectory tracking, space charge density calculation, secondary electron emission model, etc. To benchmark this multistage depressed collector simulation program, an identical model created by CST was used for comparison. Several different sets of voltage settings were used to compare with and without secondary electrons emission, and then electron trajectories are plotted. The comparison includes collector simulation efficiency and back-streaming rate. This program uses interface design and easy to use, which is a good method to assist the design of multistage depressed collector.

articleTitle: Final version - Improvements on Distortion of Frequency Spectrum for a Type of X Band Magnetron via PIC Simulation
abstract: Basing onthe curve of anode voltage via anode currents, cold and hot test data, structure parameters of the resonance system, 3D-models of a particular type of X-band magnetron were established for studying distortion of frequency spectrum in the tube. The amplitudes and frequencies of all modes were acquired via PIC simulation in CST Microwave Studio while altering the cathode's height and diameter, emission current from the cathode, static magnetic field, and anode voltage. When comparing these simulations with experiment results, it was determined that the main cause of spectrum distortion was the splitting of the operating mode and the disturbance of competitive modes, which was brought on by an imbalance between the structure of the interaction gap, the size of the cathode, the electric current from the cathode emitter, and operating magnetic strength. By adjusting the operating and other structure settings, properly increasing the cathode axial height and diameter, reducing the axial magnetic field on the cathode surface, selecting appropriate electric currents from the cathode emitter, this problem has finally been resolved.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter-free Weighted Median Operator for Robust Spectral Analysis in Heavy-Tailed Noise Environment
abstract: The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression has been widely used for high-resolution spectral line estimation. Since the derivation of the LASSO is based on <tex>$l$</tex>-2 norm, it loses robustness in environments with heavy-tailed noise. combining the LAD and LASSO criteria, the least absolution deviation (LAD)-LASSO can effectively resist outliers and heavy-tailed errors. However, this method encounters the problem of optimal artificial parameter selection. In this paper, a robust Semi-Parametric/SParse Iterative Covariance-based Estimator (SPICE) is first introduced, which significantly eases parameter selection. Secondly, a weighted median algorithm is uesd to robustly estimate each frequency coefficient in a coordinate descent framework. The proposed method can effectively resist outliers and heavy-tailed errors without tuning user parameter, and greatly improve the computational efficiency compared with traditional SPICE. Simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)

articleTitle: Novel Semi-Ellipse Bending Waveguide Slow Wave Structure for Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: A novel semi-ellipse bending waveguide (SEBWG) slow wave structure (SWS), which evolves from the folded-waveguide slow wave structure (FWG-SWS), is proposed to develop the wide-bandwidth, high power and high efficiency traveling-wave tube (TWT). The major advantages of this novel SWS are flatter dispersion, larger coupling impedance and better transmission characteristics in comparison with the conventional FWG-SWS. With a pencil electron beam of 20.8 kV and 50 mA, the particle-in-cell simulation results show that, the proposed SEBWG-TWT, within the operating frequency band from 150 GHz to 165 GHz, is capable of producing saturated output power greater than 35.5 W. Simultaneously, the maximum power of 51 W, corresponding to the gain of 53.1 dB and the beam-wave interaction efficiency of 4.9%, could be obtained at the frequency point of 159 GHz. Compared with those of FWG-TWT, the output power and beam-wave interaction efficiency of the SEBWG-TWT are considerably improved. At the same time, the SEBWG-TWT achieves length reduction and bandwidth expansion.

articleTitle: G-band Traveling Wave Tube Based on the Elliptical Pillar Defect Photonic Crystal
abstract: To further reduce the loss of the slow wave structure (SWS), an elliptical cylindrical defect photonic crystal waveguide (EPDPCCW) is proposed as a slow-wave structure of traveling wave tube (TWT). EPDPCW is a variation based on rectangular defect column photonic crystal waveguides (RPDPCW). Excellent dispersion and normalized impedance are displayed by the EPDPCW between 200 GHz and 240 GHz in simulations of the high frequency characteristics. According to transmission simulations for EPDPCW and RPDPCW, the former has smaller ohmic losses than the latter. In addition, particle in cell (PIC) simulations show that the saturation output power of the EPDPCW-TWT is increased compared to the RPDPCW-TWT.

articleTitle: Design of a Sheet Beam Electron Gun for a 220 GHz Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: The sheet beam electron gun is one of the most important parts of a sheet beam traveling wave tube (SB-TWT). In this paper, a 220 GHz sheet beam electron gun is designed and optimized by using CST. Simulation results show that the beam current of the designed sheet beam electron gun is 0.1 A with a beam voltage of 30 kV, and the sheet beam size at the beam waist is about 0.6 mm * 0.12 mm. The sheet beam electron gun can be used to construct 220 GHz sheet beam traveling wave tubes.

articleTitle: Electrothermal coupling analysis of microwave windows using finite element method
abstract: With the continuous improvement of the performance of microwave electro-vacuum devices, high-power microwave windows are the key component of high-power microwave electro-vacuum devices, which have important influence on the frequency band, power capacity, reliability and service life of the devices. In this paper, a software package called electrothermal coupling simulator (ETCS) is developed for electrothermal coupling analysis of microwave windows by using the finite element method. The influence of temperature-dependent permittivity of ceramics, high-frequency dielectric loss and ambient temperature of heat dissipation on the transmission characteristics is analyzed. Compared with the commercial software ANSYS, the numerical results demonstrate the correctness of ETCS.

articleTitle: Study of the Influence of Synchronization on the Mode Competition in a Gyrotron
abstract: The mutual synchronization of two delay-coupled gyrotrons has attracted a considerable interest in recent years. In this paper, we study the effect of synchronization on the mode competition scenario in a multimode gyrotron. The possibility of controlling the processes of mode competition by increasing the power of the synchronizing signal is discussed. Synchronization of gyrotrons can contribute to the suppression of parasitic modes.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of water load on waveguide structure
abstract: With more attention and development of high-power microwave in the world, water load high-power meter is widely used. Generally, the water load power meter is not only placed in the terminal of the radar transmitter, but also used as the system matching load, which is the key device in the microwave system. In this paper, a waveguide structure water load is optimally designed. In the frequency range of 34GHz to 36GHz, its VSWR (voltage standing wave coefficient) is less than 1.1. The water load adopts high density alumina ceramic as the microwave window, which has the advantages of large power capacity, low voltage standing wave coefficient, wide frequency band, small size, convenient loading and unloading.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Segmented Staggered Double Grating Slow Wave Structure for 340 GHz TWT
abstract: In order to improve the performance of the sub millimeter wave Traveling Wave Tube (TWT), a novel slow wave structure (SWS) operating at 340 GHz, named segmented staggered double grating (SSDG), is proposed in this article, which is based on the sine waveguide (SW). SSDG-SWS not only has a higher interactive impedance than SW-SWS under the same dispersion, but it is also easier to manufacture than SW-SWS. In addition, PIC simulation results show that SSDG-TWT has an output power of more than 17 W in the ultra-wide frequency range of 316–405 GHz at an operating voltage of 19.2 kV and an operating current of 60 mA, reaching the maximum output power of 32.8 W at 340 GHz with the corresponding maximum electronic efficiency of 2.84 %.

articleTitle: High-Dimensional Uncertainty Quantification in Multi-Physics Simulation for 3D Large-Scale High-Power Microwave System
abstract: We propose an uncertainty quantification method in multi-physics simulation for 3D large-scale high-power microwave systems, such as vortex electromagnetic wave radar transmitter, which is competent to handle high-dimensional uncertainty. Due to the coupling of the concentration field, electric field, and temperature field, traditional intrusive uncertainty quantification methods, requiring the modification of the original solver, are infeasible for the high-power microwave system simulation. To address this challenge, we maintain the original backend code of the solver and construct a surrogate model based on data-driven ideology. With a sparse strategy, the method can be implemented with a limited data set, reducing the computational cost of sample acquisition. The numerical results showcase the effectiveness and efficiency of the method in statistical feature extraction.

articleTitle: Preparation of ZnO Nanowire Cold Cathode on Hemisphere Brass Substrate for Radiotherapy X-ray Source Application
abstract: In this study, ZnO nanowires were grown directly from brass substrate by using thermal oxidation. The results show that ZnO nanowires grown on brass substrate have good field emission properties. A hemispherical cold cathode X-ray source device for intraoperative radiotherapy application is designed and fabricated. The results verified the feasibility of cold cathode hemispherical X-ray source device.

articleTitle: A Three-stage Depressed Collector For a V-band TWT
abstract: A three-stage depressed collector was designed for a V-band traveling wave tube based on sheet electron beam and staggered vane to recover the energy of electrons. Kinetical and positional information of the beam electrons after beam-wave interaction were extracted and sampled as input for the simulation and optimization of the collector. The voltages and the geometrical parameters of the collectors were optimized from the sampled distribution of the spent electron beam. A collection efficiency of 94.5% was achieved, and only 0.5% of the electron was back streamed to the interaction region. The maximum power dissipation density on the collector was about 50 <tex>$\mathbf{W}/\mathbf{cm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of Improvement of Output Power and Bandwidth for Terahertz EIK
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary study and numerical calculations for a high-power, high-efficiency, wide-bandwidth extended interaction klystron (EIK) based on mode overlap and multiple resonant cavities in the terahertz frequency band. The 11-gap intracavity mode with a center frequency of 0.22 THz is analyzed for its high frequency characteristics and electric field distribution. The adjacent operating modes of the <tex>$\pi$</tex> -mode, <tex>$\pi+1$</tex> -mode, and <tex>$\pi+2$</tex> -mode of the TM11 mode are selected to achieve mode overlap and expand the bandwidth. The number of cavity gaps and the length ratios of long and short slots are optimized to achieve proper frequency spacing between modes. The S-parameter analysis of the extracted structure input window cold measurement results obtained a −5 dB bandwidth greater than 2.5 GHz.
